News.title: Urgent emissions cuts needed to ‘minimise’ peak global warming, UN warns
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Deep and rapid reductions in greenhouse gas emissions are vital if peak global warming is to be kept to 1.7C-1.8C above pre-industrial levels by mid-century, according to UN scientists.

The world is set to pass the key threshold of 1.5C warming above pre-industrial levels, worsening the risks of climate change.

However, UN secretary-general Antonio Guterres insisted that "overshoot is not surrender", as the UN Environment Programme (UNEP) detailed how nations might limit the scale and duration of the breach, seeking to bring warming back under 1.5C as rapidly as possible.

The benchmark formed a core element of the landmark 2015 UN Paris Agreement, which committed nations to capping temperature rises well below 2C while striving for 1.5C.

Scientists warn that failing to contain warming will drive more frequent and severe extreme weather, from heatwaves and droughts to wildfires and flooding, with grave consequences for humanity, nature and global economies.

It could also trigger severe climate tipping points, causing lasting destruction through permafrost thaw, coral reef collapses and ocean circulation failures.

open image in gallery The world is set to pass the key threshold of 1.5C warming above pre-industrial levels, worsening the risks of climate change ( Getty/iStock )

The warnings came in the UNEP's latest "Emissions Gap" report, released on Wednesday.

It found the “lowest possible” scenario would now see an overshoot of 1.7C to 1.8C by the middle of the century, and global temperature rise returning to or below 1.5C by 2100, with about a 50% chance.

To get on to this pathway, global emissions would have to be reduced by 18% by 2030, 45% by 2035 and 69% by 2040, all relative to 2025 levels, it said.

However, the UNEP experts found countries’ current climate plans – known as nationally determined contributions (NDCs) which they must publish as part of the Paris Agreement – would only reduce emissions by 5-8% by 2030 and 11-15% by 2035, relative to 2025 levels.

Mr Guterres said: “Overshoot is not surrender.

“We can still keep it as small and as short as possible – and bring temperatures back below 1.5C by the end of the century.”

Under the current policies in place across the world, the UNEP projects warming could reach 2.8C within this century and continue to increase thereafter.

open image in gallery The warnings came in the UNEP's latest "Emissions Gap" report, released on Wednesday ( Getty/iStock )

If all NDCs are delivered and similar efforts continue, the agency found warming will be limited to 2.6C.

These projections are higher than the UNEP report’s projections last year, with the experts attributing this to the United States’ withdrawal from the Paris Agreement as well as revised estimates of historical emissions.

New NDCs submitted by countries since last year’s report have made a negligible difference for these projections, it added.

Even in the most optimistic scenario, where all NDCs plus additional net-zero targets are achieved, global warming would only be limited to 2.1C in this century.

The UNEP report said advances in renewable energy and climate policies have delivered real emission reductions across countries and sectors since the adoption of the Paris Agreement, with total energy supply from coal and oil growing slower than projected.

However, it also warned of the massive global scale-up required to get on track to achieve the goals of the Paris Agreement and that there are more opportunities than ever to accelerate action.

Inger Andersen, executive director of UNEP, said: “Every additional fraction of a degree and additional year of warming above 1.5C increases climate impacts and risks, such as the deadly floods, heatwaves and wildfires that have plagued many nations this year.

“We must pull out all the stops to minimise peak warming and return to 1.5C by the end of the century. This is possible.

“We have a wealth of success stories showing that emissions can be cut quickly.

“It is now up to nations to urgently put in place policies that spark fast, deep and sustained emissions reductions, and put the world on track for a more stable climate and more stable economies and societies.”

News.title: Why single women in their thirties think Noah in Nobody Wants This is the perfect man
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Create a machine that makes the perfect man for single straight women in their thirties, and I’ll bet the only thing that pops out is Noah Roklov. Or variations of Noah Roklov – maybe in some versions he’s taller, younger, or has blonde hair. But the fundamentals will stay the same.

At his core, this is the person we’re all yearning for: a man whose personality, attachment style, and communication habits defy every stereotype and expectation. The reason? He was created by a woman. I’m talking about Nobody Wants This, the hit Netflix series whose third season lands on the streaming platform on Thursday.

In case you need reminding, the romcom series revolves around a relationship between two people in their mid-30s: agnostic podcaster Joanne (played by Kristen Bell) and bohemian rabbi Noah (Adam Brody). In the previous two seasons, we’ve seen the breakup and makeup several times, often over the same issue: Joanne isn’t Jewish and is reluctant to convert.

open image in gallery Everybody wants this: Noah is the ideal man – is it because he was created by a woman? ( KATRINA MARCINOWSKI/NETFLIX )

Well, this season, that’s no longer an issue. And all seems well in the land of Joanne and Noah, mostly because he is, quite simply, the perfect man. Beyond that, though, he seems to represent everything that single straight women are looking for, and largely failing to find, on the dating scene today.

The fervour around this character was there from the outset. Kind, understanding, patient, and charmed rather than repelled by Joanne’s neuroses, Noah represented everything anxiously attached women like me dreamed about. Someone who embraced the chaos and found it endearing. And wanted to support her in her vulnerable moments rather than run a mile from her. A person secure enough in themselves to find humour in occasional bouts of hysteria. And hold her hand when that was all she needed.

One moment from season one stands out. After Noah clearly expresses his romantic interest in her, Joanne turns around to look the other way, explaining that her biggest fear is becoming emotionally dependent on a man who will one day realise she’s too much for him and break her heart. Again, this is a song all of us have sung at one point or another. I certainly have, anyway. Particularly in today’s dating scene, which feels so loaded with emotional grenades, it’s practically a war zone.

Joanne freaks out about having her morning routine disrupted by Noah’s presence. He laughs it off and gently asks her what she needs from him to feel more comfortable

So many of us are jaded, unavailable, and unsure of what we want, spending too long trying to figure it out with someone while sending so many mixed messages they might as well be in different languages. It’s hard to be vulnerable, to ask someone straight up: are you going to break my heart? Well, in this scene, Joanne does. And Noah’s reply is pitch-perfect (remember, he’s the invention of a woman; the series was created by Erin Foster): he listens, gently holds her shoulders, and tells Joanne that he wants to be with her. That he wants to be with all of her. She finally feels accepted for who she is! Hooray!

It’s scenes like this that make Nobody Wants This so popular. It’s also the fact that these characters are at an age when dating can start to feel characterised by feelings of fear and desperation. What if he isn’t out there? What if I’m too broken from previous partners to fall in love again? What if I don’t find someone in time to have children? And so on. Put simply: single women have more emotional baggage in their mid-thirties than we might’ve had in our mid-twenties. Our desire to feel safe, seen, and understood is more potent than ever.

Nobody Wants This does a very good job of reminding us that Noah serves that exact purpose for Joanne throughout its latest season, too, regardless of how increasingly neurotic she seems. After moving in together, Joanne freaks out about having her morning routine disrupted by Noah’s presence. He laughs it off and gently asks her what she needs from him to feel more comfortable. Again, this is exactly what we’d all hope for.

Another moment crops up later on when a f*** boy from Joanne’s past shows up and badmouths her to Noah, who instantly shuts him down. Later, when Joanne says she noticed Noah speaking to her ex, he decides to spare her the humiliation and tells her the ex is still obsessed with her, knowing that’s just what she wants to hear. See? He’s a superhero.

open image in gallery Superhero: the character seems intent on fulfilling everything a woman in her thirties needs ( KATRINA MARCINOWSKI/NETFLIX )

He’s also a mirage, a character so rooted in fiction and mythology that meeting a man like this in real life would be akin to seeing a unicorn on London Fields with a top knot. It’s important to remember that, particularly in a dating landscape that often sees us making sweeping judgements about a prospective partner based on nothing but six photos and a few pithy, and potentially AI-generated, prompts. Our imaginations can run wild, and we fill in the gaps with whatever we want to see, often missing red flags in the process.

Noah is perfect because he’s not real. Just like other pop culture heroes before him.

So, without further ado, please enjoy our list of the good and bad boyfriends of modern telly who millennial women like me have likely been fixated on at one point or another.

The good:

open image in gallery Seth Cohen walked so Noah Roklov could run ( Warner Bros )

Seth Cohen: There’s a reason they cast Adam Brody as Noah. He’s a grown-up variant of another beloved TV boyfriend: The OC’s infamously awkward, bumbling, and charming Seth Cohen. He made some mistakes, don’t get me wrong, but for the most part, Seth was the kind and considerate partner to Summer (Rachel Bilson) we all pined after.

open image in gallery Paul Mescal and Daisy Edgar Jones in Normal People ( BBC/Element Pictures/Hulu )

Connell Waldron in Normal People: Technically this is a character from a book, but given that Normal People was such a successful TV adaptation, one that shot Paul Mescal into stratospheric fame, it would be remiss not to include the brooding, sensitive but deeply caring, chain-wearing Connell Waldron.

open image in gallery Jonathan Bailey as Anthony in Bridgerton ( Liam Daniel / Netflix )

Anthony Bridgerton: Oh, how we swooned for Jonathan Bailey when he depicted the male lead in Bridgerton opposite a love interest played by Simone Ashley. The lovers-to-enemies trajectory has us caught in a chokehold, as did Anthony’s transformation from lascivious Lothario to committed lover boy.

The bad:

Mr Big: He’s probably the worst of them all. The indisputable bad boyfriend in all TV history: Carrie Bradshaw’s on-off situationship who cheats on his wife, spends years manipulating Carrie, and ultimately leaves her at the altar. Oh, and he also has the emotional capabilities of a teaspoon.

open image in gallery Big and bad: Carrie Bradshaw’s recurring love interest might be the worst of them all ( HBO )

Joe Goldberg: A serial killer does seem like a fairly obvious bad boyfriend, but You’s Joe Goldberg was a character cloaked in charisma that made him all the more complex – and pernicious. Responsible for giving millennials everywhere anxiety about being cyber-stalked, Joe is certainly up there with one of the worst TV boyfriends we’ve ever seen.

open image in gallery You’s creepy Joe Goldberg ( Netflix )

Damon Salvatore: The ultimate bad boy, Damon was the sexy anti-hero we all loved to hate. But in spite of all the murders, the rage issues, and the manipulation of Elena, we still tried to believe he was one of the good ones. He was not.

News.title: I fell in love with the food scene in this Asian city – these are the places you should eat at
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

With over 450 distinct neighbourhoods, separated north to south by the Han River, Seoul is a city of contrasts, where centuries-old hanoks (traditional houses) sit side-by-side with glistening high-rise buildings. And perhaps the best way to get a taste of this unique mix of heritage and innovation is by eating your way around the city’s best foodie venues – which is convenient as you’ll need plenty of fuel for your inevitably high step count.

There are bustling neon-lit alleys, filled with street food joints emitting the fragrant smoke of decades-honed snack recipes – from nogari (fried pollack) to mung bean pancakes. A sensory overload, in the best way. And the perfect way to bring your cortisol levels back down? The near-meditative experience of a steamy serving at one of the city’s hanok tea houses.

The South Korean capital city’s food landscape changes rapidly, with a constant stream of new openings. As Sooji Im, a Korean native and founder of London’s first Korean matcha cafe group, Tokkia, explains: “Seoul’s culinary scene is arguably the most fast-paced and trend-sensitive in the world. Food crazes move rapidly, so restaurants and cafes are constantly reinventing themselves, experimenting with new concepts, and evolving to stay relevant.”

I thought London took coffee seriously until visiting Seoul this spring. It has one of the highest densities of cafes in the world, with reportedly more than London and New York combined. Many of the coffee shops are concept spaces that double as art galleries, gardens, and listening bars.

open image in gallery Travel writer Hayley Spencer at Sansuhwa Teahouse and Shop ( Hayley Spencer )



During my trip, I ate more than my fair share of buttery, flake-topped salt bread (Korea’s answer to Japanese shio-pan), dabbled in its niche wine and cocktail scene, and ate at speciality restaurants only serving one signature dish, such as rotisserie chicken or mandu (dumplings). Look out for where the elderly locals are gathering and you’ll know you’re onto a winner, as they’re the city’s most discerning diners.

If you’re unsure where to start, I’d advise exploring a neighbourhood at a time, so that you can immerse yourself in the sights, sounds and smells at your own pace. These were three of my favourites. And remember – Seoul is a proudly 24-hour city, so bars stay open late. Consider your culinary adventure a marathon, not a sprint.

Hannam-dong

Known for its fashion boutiques and galleries, Hannam-dong in the Yongsan District is popular with the style set in Seoul, and also has more than its fair share of design-led cafes, impressive restaurants and hidden wine bars. You could easily spend a whole day soaking in the creative atmosphere and cafe-hopping.

I recommend lingering over speciality coffee at GML, a third-floor multi-roaster with a sleek minimalist aesthetic, where burled wood counters are bathed in light from picture windows. It also has a sun-trap terrace away from the hubbub of the shopping streets below.

open image in gallery In Seoul they take coffee brewing seriously ( Hayley Spencer )

Later, grab lunch at Muwol, a modern Korean restaurant serving classics such as bulgogi (marinated beef), mouthwatering hoe (Korean sashimi), and creative specials.

Stop by Sansuhwa Teahouse and Shop, where mountain-sourced teas are served on beautiful vintage crockery and tableware, accompanied by delicate biscuits and cakes. It also has a basement gallery space, Night & Day, that hosts rotating exhibitions.

One of the best spots to try a speciality dish in the area is Hannam Hanbang Tongdak. This local favourite serves sizzling, oakwood-baked rotisserie chicken stuffed with herbs on a bed of sticky rice. “It pairs best with a cold draft beer (chimaek style),” says Im.

Seongsu

One of the city’s trending neighbourhoods, Seongsu in the east of the city, has garnered comparisons to Brooklyn thanks to its industrial feel and young, fashionable crowd. The former factory district is known for conceptual pop-up stores, art installations and niche beauty stores, plus excellent coffee shops and cocktail bars that buzz with creative energy.

This is the area to sample salt bread. The jury is still out on whether Beton or Etre Bake House serves the best – so why not try both? At Beton, you can sample truffle or cream cheese-and-chive stuffed versions, while Etre does a chocolate bread that has gone viral. This area rewards wandering, so grab a Korean matcha to go.

Daelim Changgo is a buzzy warehouse building and former rice mill that’s now a cafe and gallery space. You can sample a plethora of Instagrammable pastries, like a strawberry-and-cream croissant, plus seasonal drinks and snacks ranging from pizza to pasta.

If you're in the area at night, Break Silence, a hi-fi bar, clothing boutique and loft space, is a vibey spot for a cocktail. Try a hibiscus highball, or its take on the Amaretto sour.

open image in gallery Muwol is a modern Korean restaurant serving classics such as bulgogi (marinated beef), mouthwatering hoe (Korean sashimi), and creative specials ( Hayley Spencer )



Euljiro

Nicknamed “Hipjiro”, this central neighbourhood is steeped in history, but is having a major creative resurgence. Decades-old workshops sit alongside modern galleries, while blink-and-you’ll-miss-them side streets are packed with natural wine bars and cafes.

A must-visit is Coffee Hanyakbang (named for its historical use as a medicine room), where a scruffy exterior opens onto a three-floor treasure trove of vintage artefacts, nodding to the Japanese colonial period. In the service area, stunning reclaimed mother-of-pearl cabinets house vintage coffee paraphernalia and records, and medicine bags hang from the ceiling. It’s known for its hand-drip filter coffee and serves elegant domed cakes from a patisserie across the road. Order the Mousse Omija, made with the uniquely flavoured Korean five-flavour red berry.

Euljiro Nogari Alley is where young locals gather after work for cheap beers and snacks, including its namesake nogari (dried pollack), while Manseon Hof is renowned for its garlicky fried chicken. The street is perfect for a taste of local late-night culture under the neon glow of packed restaurant signage.

Hayley travelled as a guest of Virgin Atlantic

How to get there

Virgin Atlantic operates direct daily flights from London Heathrow to Incheon International Airport in Seoul, starting at £889 economy. Flight time is around 15 hours.

Where to stay

The Mondrian Seoul Itaewon is a colourful, design-led stay within easy reach of central neighbourhoods. B&B rates, which include an extensive continental breakfast spread, start at £200 for a Signature King Room.

News.title: Pakistan arrests man accused of costing US Postal Service $126m through online fraud scheme
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A man accused of operating an online counterfeit postage scheme that cost the US Postal Service more than $126m has been arrested in Pakistan, the country’s cybercrime agency said on Tuesday.

Faheem Akram, 33, was detained after a search spanning several weeks that involved raids across multiple regions, Atif Ameer, senior official at the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency, told reporters.

Mr Akram, a resident of Khanewal in eastern Punjab province, was indicted by a federal grand jury in the Southern District of Florida, according to a statement from the US Attorney’s Office on 28 September.

Prosecutors alleged that he operated Labels Bank, an unauthorised online platform that sold over 5.1 million fake postage labels to more than 5,200 customers. The labels were typically priced at $2 each, regardless of a parcel's weight, size, or destination.

The counterfeit labels permitted customers to dispatch parcels at rates drastically below official postage costs, resulting in lost revenue and shipping expenses for the Postal Service.

US prosecutors noted that the estimated loss of over $126m reflected the damage to the service rather than direct sales generated by the website.

Ameer said Pakistani investigators discovered Mr Akram ran the operation from August 2023 through September 2026, using 16 bank accounts registered to himself, his wife, brother, sister, and aunt.

It remains unclear whether Mr Akram will face trial in Pakistan or be extradited to the US.

News.title: Rio Ngumoha dazzles with coming-of-age night in Europe
News.content:
Iraola noted later that Ngumoha had taken care of the defensive work too against Sergi Cardona, an attacking left-back who scored his team’s second goal. From an attacking point of view, Iraola agreed, Ngumoha had periods of the game when he looked unstoppable. “If we can put Rio in situations one-v-one, he makes plays, [and] he produces things,” Iraola said. “The assist for Alexis is a lovely play. He could go down for a penalty but he decides to continue which is a great decision. Also endurance-wise he is able to play more minutes.”

He becomes the youngest Liverpool player in Champions League history to register an assist in the competition. For Iraola it will be hard to leave Ngumoha out of the game against in-form Brighton and Hove Albion on Sunday. “I believe in myself to do it,” Ngumoha said to Amazon Prime TV. “The more chances we get, the more it makes the opposition worry. I just keep going and be ruthless.”

Iraola would later bring on the three £100m attackers whom he had left on the bench, with Sunday’s game in mind. Florian Wirtz, a half-time arrival, scored the fourth and Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak would later come on. Hard to call how it might go at home to Brighton. Liverpool’s defending was erratic at times, but their comeback was impressive.

Iraola made major changes at half-time, substituting Araújo and playing without a conventional right-back for the second half. It was brave and changed the momentum of the game, pushing his team higher up the pitch in what looked like a man-to-man marking arrangement. It enabled Iraola’s players to deny Villarreal the space and possession they had enjoyed in the first half when they had taken a two-goal lead – chiefly because of the mistakes of the home team. However much that was destabilising for Liverpool, by half-time they were level.

“They are so good on the ball,” Iraola said of Villarreal afterwards. Indeed, Villarreal’s manager Iñigo Pérez, a former Athletic team-mate of the Liverpool manager, was a coach whom Iraola sought to appoint at Bournemouth. “People probably don’t rate them [Villarreal],” Iraola said, “but after Barça they are probably the best in La Liga. They have 61 per cent of possession. Probably they have not had the results they deserve. If you are not really aggressive, you are not going to get the ball.

“We didn’t take as much risk. We were struggling because it is not a team that you can just press a bit. Either you go all the way [against Villarreal] or you will struggle without the ball.” Once Liverpool had done so, he said, his team had “won a lot of duels”. He was right in that respect. With the space squeezed, it was the power of Liverpool’s midfield that was telling.

Virgil van Dijk gave the first goal to Villarreal’s small No 9 Georges Mikautadze who had looked up to that point like he was hopelessly mismatched against the Liverpool captain and Jérémy Jacquet. Van Dijk’s misjudged header back to Alisson let in the striker who did well to gather the ball and then hit it early. The second Villarreal goal at the midpoint of the first half was a mistake from Kostas Tsimikas who failed to step up and played both Mikautadze and Cardona onside from Nathan Saliba’s ball. Either might have tucked it in but it was the left-back Cardona who took it on.

News.title: England dealt harsh lesson in Pakistan collapse
News.content:
Brendon McCullum wants his team to learn how to adapt as they prepare for the World Cup and this was a lesson in how not to master a run chase.

Failing to overhaul 302 is not an embarrassment, but the way England threw away a good start with some brittle batting gives McCullum plenty to ponder.

Spin exposed familiar failings as left-armer Arafat Minhas added six for 40 to his 59 from 58 with the bat, but it was also short balls from the seamers that hurt England. A two-paced pitch made the back-of-a-length delivery tricky, as it had in the match between Sri Lanka and Pakistan on the same ground at the weekend, but England failed to find a way to adjust their tempo.

Ben Duckett, Joe Root and Sam Curran were all dismissed by seamers hitting the pitch hard and forcing them to play square while Arafat exposed limitations against spin. He bowled Harry Brook for five with a beauty that dipped and straightened as he mixed up his arm ball with consistent accuracy to deadly effect.

News.title: Fried chicken and sugary drinks: Tanzania battles a growing obesity problem
News.content:
In early 2025, Said Shukuru, 31, was experiencing life-threatening health concerns. He weighed 150 kg (over 20 stone); his body mass index (BMI) was over 40 and he had a blood pressure of 190/100.

“It was very serious,” says Shukuru. In April last year, he underwent a successful mini gastric bypass operation at the Aga Khan Specialised Polyclinic in Masaki, Dar Es Salaam. His weight has since halved.

Shukuru’s case may be extreme, but his story serves as a warning. Overweight and obesity levels are increasing fast across East Africa, and particularly in Tanzania. Unless the government responds properly, the country faces a looming public health crisis.

Overweight and obesity in Tanzania have grown over the past 40 years because of economic development and liberalisation, urbanisation and increasingly sedentary lifestyles. Traditional diets, based on whole foods, are being replaced by refined and processed products. To make matters worse, chicken and chips, known as kuku chips, and sugary drinks are everywhere.

“When you live in an urban area like Dar (Es Salaam),” says Shukuru, “junk food is cheaper than groceries.”

The origins of these developments lie in Tanzania’s economic history. During the colonial period, fruits and legumes were exported while high-energy, starchy foods like maize were produced for domestic consumption, says Joyce Kinabo, professor of nutrition at Sokoine University.

“Food security was considered as having a lot of maize,” says Kinabo.

News.title: US warns over travel in Kenya as Ebola cases mount
News.content:
The United States has urged citizens to reconsider travel to Kenya, raising its travel alert level after the country reported an eighth case of Ebola.

The East African nation has recorded a rash of cases linked to a Kenyan businessman who died after travelling from Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).

DRC is currently enduring the second worst Ebola outbreak on record with more than 4,000 deaths since May, though the true toll is thought to be far higher.

“The level was changed from Level 2 to Level 3 due to health risks,” the US embassy in Kenya said, a day after the State Department issued renewed travel advice for its citizens.

“Reconsider travel in Kenya due to risk of health, crime, kidnapping, terrorism, unrest and traffic safety. Some areas have increased risk,” it said.

The alert came as Kenyan doctors leaders demanded better protective equipment against the highly infectious virus.

Three of the confirmed Ebola cases are reported to be health staff who cared for the businessman and the others are thought to be relatives who visited him.

News.title: US records first human case of H5N1 this year
News.content:
A man in Washington has tested positive for H5N1, marking the first human case of bird flu in the US this year.

The patient, who works on a dairy farm, was reportedly infected after being exposed to two infected cows.

H5N1 has become endemic on US dairy farms after ‘spilling over’ from birds in 2024, and has since infected more than 1,000 herds across dozens of states.

The person is not seriously ill and is isolating at home, according to the Washington State Department of Health.

Scientists have long warned that if H5N1 mutates and gains the ability to spread person-to-person, it could trigger the next global pandemic – and each new infection gives the virus more opportunities to replicate and change.

Last week, a 50-year-old man in Taiwan was infected with a different strain of bird flu, H7N7, genetic analysis of which showed the virus had undergone adaptations to spread more effectively between mammals.

Of the more than 1,000 people who have contracted H5N1 since it was first detected in the late 1990s, almost half have died.

Its “extraordinarily high” mortality rate means that, were it to gain the ability to spread between people, it would be of “enormous concern”, the World Health Organization (WHO) previously warned.

However, the strain circulating among US dairy cattle, clade 2.3.4.4b, has proven less lethal to humans.

News.title: French bond sell-off spreads across Europe
News.content:
Thanks for joining me. The cost of French government borrowing has risen at the fastest pace among G7 nations after a second night of riots.

The yield on 10-year French bonds, known as OATs, climbed from 4.80pc to 4.85pc on Monday, the steepest increase among major world economies.

Bond yields are effectively the interest rate paid by governments when they borrow money by issuing bonds to financial markets.

Emmanuel Macron is facing a crisis after shops were looted and vandalised across the country.

More than 2,300 people were arrested on Saturday after protests against the cost of living and poor school conditions.

Jim Reid, an analyst at Deutsche Bank, said: “This won’t make it easy for the international community to be totally comfortable buying OATs, so the modest recovery in French spreads over the last week or so will be tested today.

“With France already facing a difficult fiscal backdrop and the 2027 election approaching, the weekend adds another layer of political risk for markets.” Here is what you need to know.

5 things to start your day

1) Burnham seeks EU embrace over AI | UK presses for access to a scheme that will prioritise investment in sovereign technology

2) Larry Ellison’s TikTok bans ad account for Musk documentary | Social media company blocks promotion for the film because of its political content

3) Profit warnings rise ahead of Budget | Most companies blame government policy and geopolitical uncertainty for worsening outlook

4) Istanbul airport stockpiles jet fuel over shortage fears | Turkish hub can sustain flights for three weeks without topping up tanks

5) GB News to launch ‘all-British’ radio station | New broadcast venture will attempt to win market share from BBC

What happened overnight

Oil prices fell more than 1pc after Donald Trump’s decision to waive sweeping sanctions on Russia.

On Friday, the President signed an executive order that delayed a wave of fresh sanctions and tariffs as they were set to take effect.

Brent crude edged down by nearly 1pc to just under $109 a barrel, with West Texas Intermediate hovered at around $101 a barrel.

Asian shares were mixed as volatility in technology stocks persisted.

South Korea’s benchmark Kospi index was up 1.1pc to 5,729.58 on Monday, after falling sharply last week. The Kospi is down more than 18pc over the past month, and still well below the 9,000 mark it crossed in June at its peak on the global AI frenzy.

Japan’s Nikkei 225 lost 0.8pc to 64,799.03. Japanese chip equipment maker Tokyo Electron lost 2.1pc, and OpenAI investor SoftBank Group dropped 3.6pc.

Hong Kong’s stock market was closed because of a holiday. The Shanghai Composite index edged 0.2pc higher to 3,722.20, after China reported better-than-expected growth of 4.5pc for its economy in the third quarter.

CXMT, China’s leading memory chipmaker, fell more than 7pc despite the company forecasting a strong profit for the first nine months.

China’s official growth data is set to be issued on Monday, giving the markets a glimpse into how the world’s second-biggest economy is faring.

The data is expected to show that China’s economy expanded by 4.4pc in the third quarter, improving on a multi-year low in Q2 but still falling just short of its annual target.

Beijing is aiming for growth of around 4.5pc to 5pc this year, which is its lowest goal in decades.

However, experts think China is on course to miss its annual economic target, weighed down by the Iran war energy shock.

China’s economy has been under pressure from mounting energy costs and faltering domestic demand. Researchers polled by AFP suggested exports were its sole outperformer.

Taiwan’s Taiex fell 1pc. Shares of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co., or TSMC, the world’s biggest contract chipmaker, were down 0.6pc. Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 was 0.3pc higher at 8,832.20. India’s Sensex edged down 0.1pc.

Indonesia’s benchmark stock index fell another 5pc to its lowest level since 2020, after it plunged over 11pc on Friday following a warning from index provider MSCI that it would downgrade the country from its “emerging market” status.

Sports.title: ‘Not a very nice question’ – Cesc Fabregas shows his class as he’s asked about being a future Man Utd manager
Sports.content:
Next

LEGENDARY former midfielder and Como manager Cesc Fabregas angrily dismissed a question about Manchester United ahead of Wednesday’s Champions League clash.

The ex-Barcelona, Arsenal and Chelsea man was having none of it when he was asked about United’s managerial situation.



The Spaniard was asked if he would entertain the possibility of managing Man Utd, amid uncertainty surrounding current boss Michael Carrick.

Fabregas said: “I won’t answer that question because I think that’s not a very nice question.



“I don’t think that shows enough respect to a great footballer and manager like Michael Carrick at the helm of a wonderful Manchester United side.”

The Como gaffer’s class shone through as he honoured and respected a former opponent on the pitch in Carrick.

But there is real and genuine pressure on the United boss, who hasn’t won a game in six.

Everyone associated with the Red Devils will be hopeful of a result in Wednesday’s earlier kick-off, but Como are no mugs.

Fabregas’ side began Champions League life in fine fashion, thumping Leipzig 4-1 on matchday one and narrowly losing out to Feyenoord away from home last time out in the competition.

Carrick’s United smashed Azerbaijani minnows Sabah in their opener before losing 2-0 to Atletico Madrid at the Metropolitano last time in a chaotic clash which saw Leny Yoro sent off.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Following this the pressure mounted, but Carrick has come out kicking ahead of Como, insisting he retains the backing of the Manchester United board.

He also revealed earlier in the week that United will be without NINE senior players for their trip to Italy as travelling fans face a very wet time in the Lombardy region.

Sports.title: Thousands stay away leaving 20,000 Etihad seats EMPTY for Man City clash as fans joke supporters are abandoning ship
Sports.content:
Next

USUALLY when the Champions League rolls into town, fans are queueing up desperate to get tickets, unless you are Manchester City.

In fact, the Etihad outfit confirmed the attendance for their 5-1 thrashing of AEK Athens was 40,042 – over 20,000 less than the ground’s capacity.



Fans who did turn out on a cold Tuesday evening were able to see Phil Foden run riot with a hat-trick.

Meanwhile, there was also Elliot Anderson‘s first Champions League goal and a Rayan Cherki sweetener to satiate the appetite of Enzo Maresca‘s goal gluttons.



But unfortunately, that great display was only played out in front of a stadium two-thirds full.

Footage captured inside the ground laid bare the extent of the empty seats, with much of the upper stadium showing the club’s blue colours rather than a sea of fans cheering on the team.

In fairness, many may not have wanted to brave the cold and spend their hard-earned cash on a wet Tuesday night for a fixture as inconsequential as AEK Athens in the league phase of the Champions League.

There is also the fact that City don’t have the best relationship with Uefa given past sanctions, so bear a grudge against the normally illustrious tournament, usually shown in the form of boos that ring around the stadium during the anthem, though City do certainly pack it out in the knockouts.

But fans seeing the images on social media were stunned and couldn’t help but poke fun at the previous stereotype of the club being unable to fill their seats.

One said: “This is a Champions League game ladies & gents.”



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

A second said: “Crazy how empty it is…”

A third added: “Yet we’re all still meant to believe they rival Real Madrid on revenue.”

Another said: “It’s the Emptyhad.”

Despite some fans being MIA, City boss Maresca wasn’t worried.

He told reporters after the game: “I think the ones in the stadium were good. The last game against Ipswich they were top.



“And next week two games against Brighton and I’ve no doubt the environment will be good again.”

City are top of the Premier League with a 100 per cent winning record, and have only suffered defeat against the defending two-time European Champions, Paris Saint-Germain.

However, the club have the looming worry of potential punishments following the guilty verdict by an Independent Commission on the investigation into alleged Premier League financial breaches.

City were found guilty on over 100 charges, including all the financial irregularities they were accused of.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

They strongly deny any wrongdoing and have appealed the decision.



It’s been suggested the club could receive a record-breaking fine and points penalty if the appeal fails.

Sports.title: Manager who had bust-up with Mario Balotelli after calling him ‘brainless’ appointed as new Turkey boss
Sports.content:
Next

TURKEY have appointed Sergen Yalcin as their new boss following a horror start to their Nations League campaign.

Vincenzo Montella was ruthlessly sacked after suffering defeats in all four showdowns during the international break.



But the Turkish FA moved quickly to convince Yalcin, 53, to take the top job.

The former midfielder had been out of management since quitting Besiktas at the end of last season.



And, following a crucial board meeting, Yalcin was earmarked as the preferred candidate to repair the mess left by Montella.

A statement read: “The Turkish Football Federation board of directors decided today, in the meeting it held, to appoint Sergen Yalcin to the position of head coach of our national team.

“A four-year contract will be signed with the 53-year-old coach and his staff.

“Sergen Yalcin, opening a new chapter in his career, will now bring the experience he gained at the club level to our Crescent and Star-clad team and work henceforth for the success of our national football team.

“As the Turkish Football Federation, we wish Yalcin success in his new role and hope that this decision proves auspicious for our country and our national team.”

Turkey, who crashed to an early World Cup exit during the summer, are already on course to finish bottom of their Nations League group.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

They are six points adrift, with a goal difference of minus nine, and only have two clashes remaining.

Yalcin’s first encounter in charge will be against Belgium on November 12, ahead of taking on Kylian Mbappe and his French team-mates three days later.

But the controversial chief previously had a huge bust-up with former Manchester City striker Mario Balotelli.

The Italian famously attempted an audacious backheel when through on goal during a pre-season friendly with LA Galaxy.



And Yalcin, who was working as a pundit at the time, described Balotelli as “brainless”.

The Turkey squad he has inherited includes Brighton left-back Ferdi Kadioglu and Manchester United flop Altay Bayindir.

Sports.title: Man Utd ‘made shock summer transfer enquiry for “untouchable” Chelsea star’
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER UNITED reportedly made a shock enquiry for Chelsea defender Josh Acheampong in the summer.

The Red Devils rebuilt their midfield before the Premier League season kicked off, with Andrey Santos, Carlos Baleba and Youri Tielemans among the senior additions.



Head coach Michael Carrick allegedly considered adding Acheampong to his team in a bid to bolster it further – until Chelsea put a stop to any interest.

TalkSPORT claims United were among several clubs that expressed an interest in the 20-year-old.



However, the Blues rejected all approaches.

It’s now understood that Acheampong is deemed “untouchable” in the squad.



Chelsea are also set to hand him a bumper new contract in a bid to secure his future.

His current deal expires in 2029 but he could follow in the footsteps of Moises Caicedo and Cole Palmer in committing his future until the mid-2030s.

Acheampong has made eight appearances for the Blues so far this term.

Meanwhile, United face a defensive crisis going into their Champions League clash with Como on Wednesday.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Ayden Heaven, Lisandro Martinez, Luke Shaw and Patrick Dorgu are among the defenders absent ahead of the match.

Meanwhile, Leny Yoro is unable to play after being sent off last week in the 2-0 loss to Atletico Madrid.

United currently have three points in Europe following their opening two games.

Meanwhile, in the Premier League they sit 13th with seven points from their opening seven.

Sports.title: Man City 5 AEK Athens 1: Hat-trick hero Phil Foden back to his best as Rayan Cherki also turns on the style
Sports.content:
Next

AFTER ALL the anger, the accusations, the finger-pointing and Manchester City’s fans going bananas this was just a night to have a bit of fun.

Phil Foden collected a hat-trick and Elliot Anderson bagged his first-ever Champions League goal.



Rayan Cherki produced a dazzling moment of magic to claim City’s third and last night at least, all was well with the world again in the Etihad.

Here was a clash that bore no relation to City’s 4-2 defeat by Paris Saint-Germain eight days earlier that was all art and sophistication and edgy skill.



Nor was there any of the fire and fury that erupted before Saturday’s 3–2 win over Ipswich Town.

For a start the Etihad was only half-full, the banana count dramatically down following the mass protest by the Blue Moon brigade over that guilty verdict handed down over the £830M “sham contract” scandal.

But it did offer Enzo Maresca’s men the chance to just enjoy what they do best.

The Greeks champions came bearing gifts and they bit their hands off.

Thing were so much calmer on this occasion with only a few of the yellow inflatables to be seem– and some of them were held up by AEK supporters.

But City fans love to hate on Uefa too, having booed their pre-match anthem for years over their long-held views that Europe’s rulers, just like the Premier League, are out to get the club.

Their hostility towards the Champions League organisers goes back a dozen years to when City were hit with a £49M fine for breaking financial fair play rules.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

It got more intense after UEFA tried to ban the club over another FFP breach, only for the appeal by the Etihad hierarchy to the Court of Arbitration to be successfully upheld in 2020.

So the home supporters vocally let fly as is now their habit.

But on a wet Tuesday night and with masses of empty blue seats on view nobody was getting too hot under the collar in what turned out to just be an enjoyable continental interlude.

Not that boss Maresca started out taking many risks.

The Italian was without Erling Haaland, no gamble being taken with the Viking marauder who claimed a double against Ipswich but picked up a minor strain in the process.

Antoine Semenyo, who suffered a knee injury in that clash, was starting two months of rehab and so Floyd Samba, 17, was thrown in at the deep end for his Champions League debut.



He scored a brace in last month’s Carabao Cup 5-0 hammering of Norwich City last month and there are high hopes about his prospects.

Even so, Maresca took out an insurance policy worth £241M in Fernandez and Anderson, neither of whom started against the Tractor Boys.

Their job was to plough through any threats offered by Greek attackers but as it happened they contributed the 12thminute opener.

City won a free kick 20 yards, brought about by Samba’s determined dash and from it Fernandez produced a delicious delivery.

But while the £125M midfielder’s attempt hit the crossbar Anderson was the first to react, taking a whack from desperate defender Lazoras Rota as he prodded the ball over the line.



He picked himself up, rubbed his jaw…then it dawned on the £116M England man that he had just ticked another box in his upwardly mobile career.

Last season’s Greek champions had beaten LASK in their opening Champions League fixture but last week lost 3-1 to Shakhtar Donetsk at Stamford Bridge.

Even against Maresca’s side that was far from full strength, with £34M Brazilian Allan making his third appearance since his summer arrival from Palmeiras, they were on damage limitation from the moment Anderson struck.



And that attempt at keeping down the numbers didn’t work anyway for by the 34th minute City were two ahead and in cruise control.

The second deserved a much bigger audience than that which only half – filled the Etihad.

Foden flicked to Rico Lewis, another of the shadow squad given some light to shine and the right back re-delivered in style, his team mate controlling beautifully before smacking high into Alberto Brignoli’s net.

The strike had real style about it, an indication that Foden is finally rediscovering the form that made him double player of the year for season 2023-24.

Since then there were times when he became peripheral at best – losing his England spot too – and the arrival of the cheeky and inventive Ryan Cherki suggested to some that that the much – loved homegrown star might be better off out of there.



But he got a fine opener against Ipswich, added another in the grandest of style and the smile was well and truly back on his face in what was little more than a first half training exercise.

Maresca looked like he was enjoying it too – that is until AEK suddenly woke up in the 52nd minute as Stavros Pilios piled down the left flank and smashed past Gianluigi Donnarumma.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Not that he had to fret long for Cherki then brought the house down.

Foden cut the ball back to him the Frenchman who then dragged the ball back with his right foot before deftly finding the bottom corner with his left – ces’t magnifique indeed.

And the “Stockport Messi” wasn’t finished either, flashing home a high strike before tapping in to complete his treble.

Sports.title: PSG 4 Barcelona 2: Champions League holders make huge statement as they end Barca’s flawless 2026/27 record
Sports.content:
Next

ANTHONY GORDON had a nightmare visit to the French capital as Paris Saint-Germain won the battle of the European pace-setters.

Barcelona’s run of 11 straight wins was halted as the reigning continental champions maintained their position at the top of the Champions League league phase.



England winger Gordon was at fault for not defending a corner properly as Lucas Hernandez scored with a powerful header on 72 minutes at the Parc des Princes.

Hernandez, 30, got the jump on the former Newcastle star at the set-piece to score for the first time since February 2024.



And Gordon, 25, could only watch helplessly as Vitinha first scored a magnificent goal and then Fabian Ruiz added a tap-in to settle this memorable match between two super clubs.

Given all the civil unrest, protests and violence that had swept across the city in recent days, there were concerns over whether this would go ahead as planned.



But after the riots in Paris, a football match finally broke out and thank goodness it went ahead – because it was a cracker to watch for the neutral.

The first goal came on 38 minutes from the talented Desire Doue, who scored for the third successive game.

Doue, 21, benefited from Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal carelessly conceding possession and he showed fast feet and even quicker thinking before drilling a strike into the net for the opener.

Aston Villa fans will have their own nightmares over Doue, who scored the winner against them in the Uefa Super Cup in August.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Barcelona equalised on 55 minutes when right-back Xavi Espart, 19, ran on to a lovely pass by team-mate Fermin Lopez.

It was his first Champions League goal – and this was some place to announce himself to the watching world.

How different the result could have been if English referee Michael Oliver had decided to send off Lopez for kicking PSG centre-back Willian Pacho flush in the face – the incident was subject to a VAR check.

World Cup winner Ferran Torres had two decent chances in the first half and hit the post after the interval – but Hernandez did not miss with his effort with 18 minutes remaining.

Yamal, 19, equalised on 79 minutes to make it 2-2, a reminder of his class just days before he jostles with Bayern Munich and England striker Harry Kane for the Ballon d’Or award on Monday.



But then Vitinha struck with a thunderbolt and Ruiz scored from two yards out to settle it for the two-time champions of Europe.

PSG – nine points out of nine this campaign – have gone 13 games without defeat in the competition, the longest run in their history.

The only bad news for PSG was that reigning Ballon d’Or recipient Ousmane Dembele pulled up with a suspected left hamstring issue on 20 minutes.



And then Georgian playmaker Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and captain Marquinhos came off with injury concerns.

Sports.title: Liverpool 4 Villarreal 3: Reds complete incredible fightback from 2-0 down as Mac Allister inspires Champions League win
Sports.content:
Next

RIO NGUMOHA delivered a brilliant performance to save Liverpool from a Champions League humiliation.

While his senior team-mates were mostly hopeless, 18-year-old Ngumoha was unplayable as he helped his team recover from two goals down.



But here was still a reminder that Liverpool are nowhere near where they need to be under Andoni Iraola.

Iraola has still only lost once in 11 matches – and that was the 3-0 home loss to Manchester City – but he watched in disbelief as his Liverpool team delivered a shocking and embarrassing first 30 minutes when they conceded twice and it could have been worse.



Villarreal’s merry band of 680 fans could not believe what they were seeing as the team led with goals from Georges Mikautadze and left-back Sergi Cardona.

But while the rest of his team were all over the place, teenage terror Ngumoha grabbed the game by the scruff of the neck. He was absolutely outstanding.



He created the leveller for Ronald Araujo and the third for Alexis Mac Allister, who had earlier pulled the score back to 2-1.

With the Anfield crowd chanting ‘Rio, Rio’ sub Florian Wirtz made it 4-2 for his first goal since April. Yet Liverpool were still given a late warning with Tani Oluwaseyi pulling one back.

With one eye on Sunday’s difficult home game with Brighton, Iraola delivered an educated gamble by delivering some rotation. He made six changes from Saturday’s 2-1 win over Brentford and started the £364million trio of Alexander Isak, Bradley Barcola and Florian Wirtz on the bench.

So playing Ngumoha along with fellow youngsters Trey Nyoni and Lewis Kounas was a risk but it was the rest of the Liverpool team who were so bad.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Villarreal, managed by Iraola’s former No2 Inigo Perez, are 12th in LaLiga and definitely nothing special but they embarrassed Liverpool for the opening spell.

Virgil van Dijk is not having a great season and there are many Reds fans who have become increasingly concerned with the 35-year-old’s form and the basic errors he keeps making.

Van Dijk started the game badly and made a couple of silly mistakes even before his disastrous attempted header back towards Alisson after a long punt from Renato Vega.



Mikautadze, Villarreal’s record signing at £25million, took a lovely first touch and swivelled to squeeze a shot past Alisson from a tight angle.

Struggling Van Dijk was then unable to block a pass from Nathan Saliba’s pass towards Cardona who was helpfully being played onside by Kostas Tsimikas.

Left-back Cardona had never before scored a Champions league goal but you would not have known that by the way he casually side-footed a shot past a bewildered-looking Alisson.



At least Tsimikas redeemed himself by delivering the corner which led to Mac Allister’s glancing header, a rare occasion that a home player won a challenge.

That lifted the mood and in the final kick of the half, incredibly, Araujo, on loan from Barcelona, sneaked in at the far post to score with a header after Cardona made the mistake of not clearing a terrific cross by Ngumoha.

The 18-year-old continued to terrorise the Spaniards and delivered more magic when he provided the chance for Mac Allister to score with a shot via the underside of the bar. Best of all, Ngumoha could have gone down for a penalty and kept his feet.



Cody Gakpo set up Wirtz for 4-2 to fire into the corner with his left foot.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Hero of the night, Ngumoha, received a standing ovation when substituted, although Liverpool ended the game as badly as they started it.

Sub Oluwaseyi scored with a decent finish but there was no late Liverpool disaster and they still have a 100 per cent Champions League record.

Sports.title: Former Arsenal star rips into 60,000-capacity Champions League stadium and fumes ‘it’s not what you’d expect’
Sports.content:
Next

GIOVANNI VAN BRONCKHORST brutally slammed the condition of the pitch ahead of his Feyenoord side locking horns with Real Betis.

The Dutch giants have jetted in to Spain looking to notch back-to-back Champions League wins following a narrow victory over Como last week.



But Van Bronckhorst, 51, is unhappy with the playing surface at the 60,000-capacity Estadio de La Cartuja ahead of the showdown on Wednesday.

And the former Rangers chief tore into the turf during his pre-match press conference.



Van Bronckhorst, who was part of Arne Slot’s backroom staff at Liverpool, said: “The pitch is not in optimal condition. We’ve played on excellent surfaces recently, but this one is different.

“It’s not what you expect at Champions League level. We’re surprised it’s not in top condition.”

Feyenoord were on the wrong side of a battering from Barcelona when they headed to Spain last month.

The Rotterdam-based giants suffered a 5-1 mauling in their opening clash of the European campaign.

But Van Bronckhorst’s side have made the trip to Betis in higher spirits after overcoming Cesc Fabregas’ Como.

And Feyenoord are three points clear at the Eredivisie summit following a stunning run of form.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Van Bronckhorst had a two-year spell with Arsenal during his stunning playing career.

The Dutchman made 64 appearances for the Gunners – notching two goals and nine assists along the way.

Despite suffering a long-term knee injury during his time in North London, Van Bronckhorst got his hands on the Premier League and Community Shield, along with the FA Cup twice.

He also featured for Feyenoord, Rangers and Barcelona – where he was in the starting line-up for Lionel Messi’s debut – before hanging up his boots in 2010.



And Van Bronckhorst was involved as the Netherlands lost to Spain in the 2010 World Cup final.

Feyenoord are set to face Inter Milan, Porto, Viking, Galatasaray and RB Leipzig following their visit to Betis.

Paul George scored 38 points, the most by a Celtic in his debut. The nine-time All-Star, in his 17th season, showed he's still got it in his first game with Boston since it acquired him from Philadelphia in exchange for 2024 NBA Finals MVP Jaylen Brown.

Sports.title: Hat-trick hero Foden shines as Man City thrash AEK Athens
Sports.content:
Phil Foden bagged a hat-trick as dominant Manchester City cruised to a 5-1 win over AEK Athens to claim their second Champions League victory of the campaign.

Foden had waited 10 months for a goal before four arrived in back-to-back outings, adding to his strike against Ipswich at the weekend with three tidy finishes, the first two from Rico Lewis assists.

Man City had far too much quality for their Greek visitors despite leaving Erling Haaland in the stands, with Enzo Maresca allowing 17-year-old Floyd Samba to deputise in his place. Maresca proved his point in doing so: City have many other means of scoring beyond Haaland.

Elliot Anderson was also on target in a dominant first half that included 10 efforts on Alberto Brignoli's goal, with Allan striking the crossbar and Rayan Cherki going close.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Anton Toloui provides insight on three things we learnt from Manchester City's dominant Champions League performance against AEK Athens

Man City on a roll This was Man City’s 10th win in 12 matches in all competitions this season (L2) – of sides in Europe’s big-five leagues, only Barcelona have won more (11).

AEK failed to land a shot on target until Stavros Pilios pulled a goal back early in the second period. But their hope was short-lived. Cherki scored City's third five minutes later to kill any suggestion of a comeback and Foden issued another timely reminder of his class by completing a statement hat-trick.

The last time Foden scored three times in the same game was April 2024. It's felt like a lifetime since the City Academy graduate, a known favourite of Pep Guardiola, was anywhere near his dazzling best. His latest display was somewhere close to perfect.

The key moments from the Etihad

12: GOAL! Anderson steers home the rebound from Enzo Fernandez' free-kick for his first club goal.

23: CROSSBAR! Allan crashes a fierce effort off the woodwork as City threaten again.

34: GOAL! Foden combines neatly with Lewis and stabs beyond Alberto Brignoli.

52: GOAL! Pilios gives AEK a lifeline with a well-taken strike across Gianluigi Donnarumma.

57: GOAL! Cherki finds the bottom corner to kill any AEK momentum.

65: GOAL! Lewis tees up Foden and he guides the ball into the top corner with a wonderful finish.

76: GOAL! Ryan McAidoo offers Foden the chance to complete his hat-trick with an easy tap-in.

Image: Elliot Anderson scores his first goal in Man City colours

Maresca backs Foden to return to top form

Man City boss Enzo Maresca:

On Foden: "I've said since day one, I consider him one of the best English players. For different reasons, in the last two years, he was not good enough. But I know how good he is. We are trying to help him because we are sure he's going to help us."

On the performance: "It was not easy, especially after the PSG game. We had two games that we certainly needed to win, and we did our job.

"I'm also happy because some of the players have not been playing many minutes, but they were ready. This is important. It is the best feeling for any manager when you make many changes but the performance is still good."

Foden insists his best is yet to come

Man City forward Phil Foden to TNT Sports:

"I enjoyed that a lot. We showed determination again; it wasn't pretty at times, giving sloppy passes away, but I thought we stuck at the game plan, we kept going, and in the end we broke them down.

"I've still got a long way [before I'm back at my best], but I'm going in the right direction and scoring along the way. It definitely helps.

"I just want to keep working hard and trying to be the best I can for the manager and for the team."

Nikolic: We gave City too much respect

AEK Athens boss Marko Nikolic:

"We didn't want to sit back and try to survive, like I said before the game. We wanted to be dangerous with the ball.

"But of course the quality in the finishing phase from City was brutal. These guys were much better in the final third than us. They punished every mistake. A deserved victory for City.

"AEK is only playing Champions League group phase for the second time in 20 years; we're trying to compete. Maybe we showed too much respect for our opponent."

Man City's next fixtures...

Sports.title: Ngumoha stars as Liverpool come back to win thriller against Villarreal
Sports.content:
Liverpool came from two goals down to defeat Villarreal 4-3 at Anfield and make it three wins from three in this season’s Champions League.

Two goals from Alexis Mac Allister and one apiece from Ronald Araujo and Florian Wirtz completed the turnaround, with Rio Ngumoha superb. All of it came after Virgil van Dijk's poor header allowed Georges Mikautadze to score in the fourth minute.

It was the earliest that Liverpool had fallen behind at Anfield in a major European tie for a quarter of a century but worse was to come when Sergi Cardona raced through to finish off a slick move for the Spanish side's second, a deserved lead at that stage.

But Mac Allister's header from Kostas Tsimikas' corner pulled one back and the lively Ngumoha then fashioned an equaliser when Araujo ghosted in at the far post with Cardona sleeping. It was hardly deserved but Liverpool were rampant after the break.

Image: Liverpool's Ronald Araujo scored a first-half equaliser

The introduction of Wirtz undoubtedly helped but it was Ngumoha whose dancing feet opened up the Villarreal defence to set up Mac Allister for his second. Wirtz then made it four himself with a left-footed finish beyond Peter Gulacsi. His relief was palpable.

Image: Substitute Florian Wirtz put Liverpool 4-2 up

Andoni Iraola will likely feel the same after Tani Oluwaseyi set up a nervous finish. Liverpool have conceded three goals in each of their last two Champions League games but won them both. It has not been entirely convincing but it is a third victory in a row.

Analysis: Ngumoha lights up Anfield

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Vinny O'Connor provides insight on three things we learnt from Liverpool's comeback victory against Villarreal.

They played Rio by Duran Duran upon the final whistle at Anfield, so obvious was it that the winger had been the best player on the pitch. Mac Allister scored two, Wirtz had his big moment but for all the expensive signings on show, Rio Ngumoha was the standout.

Ngumoha finished with two assists and seven successful dribbles. There were times when three Villarreal players were trying to stop him but it never deterred him and you always sensed that the teenager had the trickery and the talent to find a way through.

Image: Rio Ngumoha's touch map for Liverpool in their 4-3 Champions League win over Villarreal

Iraola: Ngumoha difficult to stop

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Following his side's sensational Champions League comeback against Villarreal, Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola heaped praise on young winger Rio Ngumoha, after his dazzling display.

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola speaking in the press conference:

"I think he was coming from a very good game the other day, he had a good second half against Brentford. Today he didn't have an easy game also because they were demanding him defensively and their left-back was attacking a lot.

"There was a moment offensively where he was very difficult to stop. If we can put Rio in situations one against one, he makes plays, he produces things, today the assist for Alexis is a lovely play. He could go down for a penalty but he decides to continue which is a great decision.

"Also endurance wise he is able to play more and more minutes. We were pushing him a little bit. He was tired but I think he has done a good effort and I'm very happy for him.

"I am happy with his attitude because he is eager to improve things that we think he needs to improve. He is eager to add more things to his game.

"He has been on the right lately, he is feeling more comfortable now, shooting on his left, he can add this to his game. He is only 18, still not the full package and it is not always going to be like this, there will be ups and downs in the process."

Perez: Ngumoha had a great game

Villarreal head coach Inigo Perez speaking in the press conference:

"The key moment was when they equalised to make it 2-2 just before half-time. We had a fantastic first half. But the mentality and emotion drops, theirs grows and it affects you, particularly at Anfield. But we still managed to stay in the game until the end.

"Rio Ngumoha had a great game but many other players played well. There were emotions, there were goals. When you play at Anfield these things can happen. When a goal is scored here, you can feel the reaction.

"But I don't think we were close to being hammered. I believe if we are able to correct simple details - but elite details - we would be able to win on these big stages."

Liverpool's next fixtures...

Sports.title: 'Appalling' batting and 'wickets in clumps' leave England with ODI setback
Sports.content:
England captain Harry Brook admits his side were 'too careful' against Pakistan’s spinners after collapsing to a disappointing 87-run defeat in their ODI tri-series opener.

Arafat Minhas starred with bat and ball in Rawalpindi for the hosts, who recovered from 133-5 to post 302-9 from their 50 overs before skittling England for 215 to claim their second win of the tournament.

Pakistan's all-rounder fired 59 off 58 deliveries and was part of a strong lower middle-order fightback, with Hasan Nawaz top-scoring with a 74-ball 79 and Faheem Ashraf adding 39 off 26 deliveries in the closing overs.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Pakistan’s innings against England in the ODI tri-series, where the hosts recovered from a slow start

Tom Banton and Ben Duckett shifted the momentum in England's favour with a 91-run opening stand, only for Arafat to bamboozle the visitors with a career-best 6-40 and help Pakistan wrap up victory with more than 11 overs to spare.

"We thought they [Pakistan] were slightly under par," Brook said after their defeat. "It got dewy, as we thought it would do and we were pretty happy at halfway.

"We thought [Tom] Banton, Ducky [Ben Duckett] set the tone to nearly get a 100 partnership and then it was a case of losing too many wickets in clumps. We couldn't really string the partnerships together and we ended up on the wrong side.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ben Duckett and Tom Banton were both dismissed quickly after putting on a 91-run opening stand

"We've spoken a lot about rotation of strike through the middle but I think we were a little too careful against the spinners especially, so we can probably put them under a little bit more pressure in stages.

"We've got to tonight to talk about it and tomorrow and bounce back better on Thursday."

England were well placed at 165-3 - despite Arafat removing Banton (57) and Brook (five) - when Naseem Shah bowled Joe Root for 33, with the tourists still in a good position until losing their last five wickets for 18 runs in a chaotic five-over spell.

Jordan Cox was trapped lbw by Arafat before Pakistan's spinner removed Jamie Overton in his next over, with the manner of the dismissal criticised by former England bowler Stuart Broad on commentary.

"That's appalling batting," Broad told Sky Sports, having seen England slip to 205-7. "With Will Jacks at the other end, you're saying England have a chance, you play for your partner.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Stuart Broad called out Jamie Overton for his 'appalling batting' after his dismissal

"You say you have a weakness against spin, that's certainly not what you do - he's just chipped it down long-on's throat. A poor wicket for England to lose."

Arafat closed out victory by being involved in all three final wickets, coming in the space of four balls, dismissing Jacks and Adil Rashid in successive deliveries before running out Gus Atkinson.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gus Atkinson was run out in chaotic fashion to complete England's defeat to Pakistan

He became the third Pakistan all-rounder - after Abdul Razzaq and Shahid Afridi - to grab a five-wicket haul and score a half-century in an ODI, with the 21-year-old proud of his man-of-the-match display.

"Hasan [Nawaz] and I discussed that we need to bat deep," Arafat said. "I took charge after Hasan got out and I tried to bat until the end of the innings, which helped in taking the score beyond 300."

On his bowling, Arafat added: "I kept my plans simple. I think variations are very important for a spinner, as they help in deceiving the opposition batters."

Image: Arafat Minhas took 6-40 from his 8.4 overs

Pakistan take plaudits as England need to 'learn from mistakes'

Victory for Pakistan is their second successive win in the ODI tri-series, following their 37-run win over Sri Lanka in the tournament opener, keeping them top of the standings and leaving them well-placed to qualify for the final on October 31.

"A bit of credit to Pakistan, who in both innings fought back," former England captain Nasser Hussain told Sky Sports. "They were 81-4 and 133-5 and yet managed to get over 300.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jamie Overton's brilliant yorker cleans up Hasan Nawaz during England's tri-series games against Pakistan

"England were going well and everyone was thinking they were going to win this game, but there was a bit of fight and a bit of character from Pakistan - with bat and ball."

England - missing several key players - have won all three ODI series this year after losing six of seven bilateral series before that, with Hussain expecting them to take lessons from their convincing defeat.

"He [Sam Curran] looks a bit short of a gallop at the moment, both with the ball and with the bat," Hussain added. "He didn't have rhythm, but that will come. Adil Rashid will get better the more he bowls - he's obviously coming back from injury.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Nasser Hussain and Stuart Broad discuss England’s ODI opening options, following another half-century for Tom Banton

"They are missing Jos Butler - England's greatest ever white-ball player. They're missing Jofra Archer and they're also missing Jacob Bethell.

"They've been on a good track, so don't get too up when you win and don't get too down when you haven't chased 300 - just learn from the mistakes that you made today."

Sports.title: Barcelona handed first defeat of season by PSG in classic
Sports.content:
Barcelona were handed their first defeat of the season as they lost 4-2 to Paris Saint-Germain in a Champions League classic.

In a game that saw a total of 40 attempts on goal, it was the reigning European champions who were able to outgun the visitors in a contender for match of the season.

The pair traded goals, with Desire Doue's strike and Lucas Hernandez's header each being cancelled out courtesy of youngster Xavi Espart and the irrepressible Lamine Yamal.

Seconds after Barca's number 10 levelled things for a second time, Vitinha restored PSG's lead as Barcelona ran out of gas. Fabian Ruiz put the icing on the cake five minutes later with a tap-in as Hansi Flick side tasted defeat for the first time in 12 games this season.

There were some sour notes on an otherwise exhilarating evening. Ballon d'Or holder Ousmane Dembele came off with a suspected hamstring injury inside the opening 20 minutes. Team-mate Khvicha Kvaratskhelia was also helped off in the second half after picking up a knock.

Dani Olmo was also withdrawn in the first half for Barcelona, who are already struggling with an injury crisis. It adds another blow for the LaLiga leaders, who visit Real Madrid in the first El Clasico of the season on Sunday.

Key moments from a classic at the Parc des Princes...

2: POST! Kvaratskhelia smashes the woodwork in less than 120 seconds.

5: SAVE! Garcia denies Dembele and Doue in quick succession.

10: CHANCE FOR GORDON! Ball drops to Englishman in good position, but he fails to make the most of it.

14: JUST WIDE! Olmo misses target in Barcelona's first meaningful attempt.

19: INJURY! Ballon d'Or holder Dembele comes off with suspected hamstring issue.

Image: Ousmane Dembele came off with a suspected hamstring injury inside 20 minutes

25: HUGE MISS! Substitute Torres denied by Garcia from close range.

27: INJURY! Olmo replaced as Barca's injury list grows.

29: CHANCES GALORE! PSG squander three brilliant attempts in a matter of seconds.

38: GOAL! Doue finally puts PSG ahead after Lamine Yamal mistake.

Image: PSG's Desire Doue celebrates opening the scoring

40: SAVE! Nearly immediate response from Barca as Fermin is thwarted by Safanov.

51: SAVE! Hakimi denied as PSG miss more chances.

55: GOAL! PSG punished as Espart equalises.

Image: Barcelona youngster Xavi Espart equalised early in the second half

59: INJURY! Kvaratskhelia is helped off the pitch on the hour.

Image: PSG's Khvicha Kvaratskhelia was helped off the pitch after picking up an injury just before the hour mark

71: POST! Torres misses again as he strikes the post from close range!

72: GOAL! A set-piece does the job as Hernandez's header restores PSG's lead.

Image: Lucas Hernandez made it 2-1 with a bullet header

79: GOAL! Lamine Yamal smashes Barca level from a tight angle.

Image: Lamine Yamal squeezes in equaliser to make it 2-2

81: GOAL! Vitinha hits back immediately from edge of the box.

Image: Vitinha celebrates in front of PSG fans after restoring lead

86: GOAL! Ruiz seals the deal as Barca run out of steam.

Image: Fabian Ruiz celebrates scoring PSG's fourth goal

Gordon: We need to try and become PSG

Barcelona forward Anthony Gordon speaking with TNT Sports:

"I think it was quite predictable that it was going to be high-scoring and a good spectacle for people to watch. I was hoping we would come out on the right side of that, but unfortunately we didn't.

"They deserved it. They were the better team and had the better moments with real quality. Athletically, they were able to sustain the pressure and intensity for longer than we were. They've been the team to beat for two years and tonight they gave a great example as to why.

Image: Barcelona's Anthony Gordon said his side can take positives from the defeat

"I think we can take great positives because we played well. It was a competitive spectacle. We've still got work to do and that's a good position to be in. They've been the team to beat for two years. We need to do enough work, analyse the game and try and become that."

Football at its most entertaining

Analysis from Sky Sports' Callum Bishop:

"I covered PSG's 5-4 win over Bayern Munich last season. It was a breathless game and one of the greatest I had ever witnessed.

"While tonight might not quite have been at that level, it was in a very similar bracket. Two of the best teams in the world with full belief in themselves and only one intention: outscore the other.

"No one could've blamed Barcelona if they came to the French capital and decided they were going to shut up shop and try to stop the potent PSG attack.

"Their approach was the complete opposite. They had faith that their attack was as lethal. In the end, they fell short, but they can hold their heads high.

"As a neutral, these are the types of games you dream of watching. It makes you feel things only free-flowing football can.

"If you want a demonstration of what two heavyweight giants playing each other should look like, it is this. Blow for blow, haymaker for haymaker.

"A joy to watch."
