Sports.title: Rio Ngumoha breaks Liverpool record and is a major England threat to Bukayo Saka
Sports.content:
Rio Ngumoha dazzled for Liverpool in their 4-3 victory over Villarreal - and Bukayo Saka should be worried about his England spot.

It's a suggestion made by Jason Cundy after the teenager picked up two assists in the Champions League thriller at Anfield on Tuesday.

3 Ngumoha arguably had his best Liverpool performance to date as he assisted two goals in their comeback win over Villarreal Credit: Getty

Player-of-the-match Ngumoha provided for Ronald Araujo with a floating cross and then teed up Alexis Mac Allister as Liverpool came from behind to win their third European match of the season.

The teenager has started in all of their Champions League ties and is becoming an integral part of Andoni Iraola's squad, with a new deal also a possibility.

He featured in England's pre-World Cup training camp, and made his debut during the 1-0 friendly win over New Zealand.

Thomas Tuchel did not select him as part of his final 26-man squad but, with Euro 2028 the next major tournament, and Cundy believes the starlet is capable of battling Saka for a starting spot on the right.

Ngumoha v Saka for England starting role

When asked if Ngumoha should play right-wing for England, Cundy said on The Sports Bar: "After that performance, you have to be seriously looking at him. He was involved in the last squad.

Cundy added: "He has caught the eye. Every time he plays, he catches the eye. And there are very few players that can do that at his age. But the thing that he's got, he has the ability because he's so young.

"There's no fear of failure. You get this with young players. They don't know what it's like. Failure doesn't exist in their lives. They've always been the best.

"They just go out and just go and showcase what you've got. Go on, do a step over. Who cares if I get it? And more often than not, because he's so full of confidence…

"There will be a moment in his career where there will be a dip, he will drop in form. It inevitably happens with most young kids but wow, what a performance, what a player."

Cundy then claimed that Saka, who is the consistent starter at right-wing for England, may be wary of Ngumoha's rise as he said: "Saka's had a lot of injuries, but he's England's starter right now in England's best team.

3 With 59 caps, Saka has been the long-term go-to choice on the right for England - but Cundy thinks Ngumoha can rival him for the starting role Credit: Getty

"But, when you're watching young players come through, and even though Saka's still got to reach the peak of his powers...

"When you're looking over your shoulder, you're going, 'Wow, this kid has got something'. Liverpool fans should be very excited, England fans should be very excited."

Ngumoha with a record-breaking display

Ngumoha and Barcelona star Lamine Yamal are the only two teens in this season's Champions League to bag two assists in one match.

The cross for Araujo also made Ngumoha the youngest ever player to score or assist in the competition for Liverpool, doing so aged 18 years and 52 days.

In addition, he is the third-youngest Englishman to provide an assist after Jude Bellingham, Lewis Miley and Theo Walcott.

Ngumoha has now made seven Champions League appearances for Liverpool, although he is still waiting for his first competition goal.

3 Ngumoha broke a club record on what was a night to remember in Liverpool colours on the Champions League stage Credit: Getty

"Tonight is up there with one of the best I've played I think," he said in his post-match interview with Amazon Prime. "I enjoyed myself out there, the team helped me a lot…

"Whenever I get the ball and have the opportunity to go one v one, or sometimes two v one, I'll by all means go for it.

"I believe in myself to do that and the more chances we get the more we can worry the opposition and be ruthless."

Ngumoha added: "To hear my name being chanted by the crowd is a dream. We have the best fans in the world."

Sports.title: EFL managers separated at full time in furious touchline spat
Sports.content:
Wolves and Portsmouth managers Cesar Peixoto and John Mousinho were involved in a heated altercation at full-time of their Championship clash.

Emotions boiled over at the final whistle following the 1-1 draw at Molineux, as Terry Devlin's 86th-minute equaliser snatched a point for Pompey.

5 Cesar Peixoto angrily approached Mousinho at full-time

5 The two managers began to bicker and had to be separated as things threatened to boil over

Wolves had taken the lead through Jordan James, before being made to settle for a draw as Mousinho's side grabbed a late goal.

The result appeared to leave Peixoto frustrated, as footage shows him angrily approaching Mousinho as the full-time whistle blows.

He can be seen making a talking gesture with his hands whilst walking towards his Portsmouth counterpart, who responds by putting his hands on Peixoto and attempting to move him away.

But this only appeared to anger the Wolves boss more, as he continued to appear animated whilst gesticulating at Mousinho.

Other members of staff soon became involved in the heated altercation with players also appearing on the scene to separate the two.

With others beginning to push and shove each other, Mousinho walked away from his opposite number as things calmed down.

It isn't clear what sparked the touchline spat, with Peixoto clearly the more angry of the two managers.

The draw leaves Wolves - who were relegated last season - seventh in the table on 18 points, while Portsmouth are 13th, three points behind them with a tally of 15.

Mousinho reveals Peixoto anger

Speaking after the heated full-time scenes, Mousinho revealed that Peixoto had been angered by his vocal manner on the touchline.

He told The News: "I shook the manager’s hand and then he said I talk too much. So I very politely told him that that’s probably what I do, that’s my job as head coach.

5 Peixoto cut a frustrated figure at full time at Molineux Credit: Getty

5 Mousinho has been Portsmouth head coach since 2023 Credit: Getty

"It was just handbags, absolutely nothing, it’s just one of those, shake hands and walk off.

"I didn’t quite understand it, but it’s fine, no worries."

Stressing that the altercation was nothing serious, Mousinho explained that his questions for the fourth official during the game had annoyed Peixoto.

He continued: "During the game, I got up to talk to the fourth official, I don’t know if you aren’t allowed to any more, I was told in no uncertain terms, quite a rude way, that I needed to sit down and not talk to the fourth.

"I tried to point out that I didn’t know there had been a law change where I wasn’t allowed to speak to the fourth any more, that was it.

"You know what I’m like, just let each manager speak to the fourth, just get on with your own job.

5 Terry Devlin's second goal of the season grabbed a point for Portsmouth at Wolves Credit: Getty

"My job is quite difficult, I’m sure his job is quite difficult as well, let them get on with it. Let the staff do their own thing, stop interfering."

This wasn't Mousinho's first touchline altercation, having also been involved in a spat with Coventry boss Frank Lampard last season.

Sports.title: Como vs Man United Champions League clash could be postponed amid weather warning
Sports.content:
Torrential rain could bring disruption to the Champions League clash between Como and Manchester United.

The misfiring United have arrived in Italy for the matchday three tie on Wednesday evening, live on talkSPORT 2 at 5:45pm UK time.



2 Como host United on one of the biggest nights in their history, but severe weather has been forecast Credit: Getty

Como are playing in the Champions League for the first time in their history and set for their first match against an English opponent.

However, there is concern over the weather forecast just a day before the match.

Champions League weather warning

Lombardy, the region in which Como is located, has been issued with an orange warning for rain.



This is described as a severe warning of dangerous weather and there is a call for vigilance.

Rain has fallen throughout Tuesday afternoon and into the evening in northern Italy, and is set to continue until the end of the match on Wednesday.



Simon Peach of the Press Association has also reported that 64mm worth of rain is forecast before kick-off at Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia.

Only one of the four stands at the stadium are covered, which means some fans are set for very wet conditions.



Lightning could also appear around kick-off, though Como are said to be confident of the pitch holding up and avoiding postponement.

Despite the looming weather, United head coach Michael Carrick isn't too worried about the rain.

"No, nothing immediate from me, we're used to the rain," he said on his potential concerns. "We'll make the most of it!"

2 Heavy rain is expected to continue overnight and into the evening, with the match set for wet conditions Credit: Getty



Six players were missing from United training on Tuesday morning in what is a big blow to their match preparation.

They were said to be Ayden Heaven, Kobbie Mainoo, Marcus Rashford, Lisandro Martinez, Luke Shaw and Patrick Dorgu.

United are looking to end their run of six matches without a win in all competitions when they face Como.

Their last European fixture ended in a 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid, after which Martinez called out the club board in a scathing rant.



He publicly apologised for his comments and played in the 1-1 draw at Leeds United on Sunday, although went off at half-time due to injury.

United have already picked up a Champions League win as they beat debutantes Sabah FK 4-0.

Sports.title: Arsenal could make January move for star smashing this season’s Champions League
Sports.content:
Arsenal are reportedly considering a January move for Club Brugge striker Nicolo Tresoldi as they look to strengthen in attack.

Mikel Arteta has relied heavily on Kai Havertz this season - starting the German in all seven of his side's Premier League games despite also having £63.7million Viktor Gyokeres at his disposal.



4 Tresoldi has caught the eye with his goalscoring exploits in the Champions League this term Credit: Getty

Having failed to convince as first-choice last season, Gyokeres has lost his place in the Gunners' starting XI this term and is yet to score at all.

The Sweden star has started twice in the Champions League and once in the Carabao Cup, as well as featuring four times off the bench.

His struggles for game time have led to suggestions that Gyokeres could look to leave the club in January, while Arsenal now appear to be considering alternatives too.



According to the Sun, Arsenal are interested in bringing in-form Club Brugge star Tresoldi to the Emirates Stadium in January.

The Germany Under-21 international has already registered nine goals in 12 appearances across all competitions this season.



That includes four goals in two Champions League games, with Tresoldi scoring in Brugge's’s 3-2 loss to Aston Villa.

He then took centre stage against Inter Milan, as he fired in a stunning hat-trick in his side's thrilling 4-3 victory at the San Siro.



Arsenal identify January target

Tresoldi's goalscoring exploits have now led to Arsenal considering a January swoop for him.

He wouldn't be the first player to go from Brugge to Arsenal in recent months, with his former teammate Christos Tzolis making the same move in the summer.

The Greece star joined the Premier League champions in a bargain £34m deal, and made a strong start to life at the club.

4 Tresoldi has fired in 32 goals in 69 games since joining Club Brugge from Hannover 96 in 2025 Credit: Getty



4 Gyokeres could be the man to make way if Arsenal make a move for Tresoldi

Following his arrival, the 24-year-old has provided four assists in eight appearances for Arsenal across all competitions.

However, his progress has been halted more recently after picking up a thigh injury whilst on international duty with Greece, which has caused him to miss his team's last three games.

It's fair to say a reuniting Tzolis and Tresoldi would give the Gunners a boost up top, as the pair previously proved a deadly duo.



The two players were the Belgian Pro League’s top scorers last season - with Tresoldi topping the charts with 19 goals in 40 games.

Tzolis wasn't far behind, finding the net on 17 occasions to earn him a Premier League switch.

Arsenal wouldn't be the first club to go after Tresoldi, with Brugge rejecting a £30m bid from Italian giants Roma for him in August.

4 Christos Tzolis has quickly established himself at Arsenal after his summer arrival from Club Brugge Credit: Getty



The Italy-born Germany youth star has reportedly risen in value since then, with the Sun's report adding he is now worth around £42m.

Meanwhile, the Gunners could face a battle from AC Milan in January to sign Tresoldi, with the Serie A outfit said to be very interested, while the player is a boyhood supporter of the club.

Sports.title: Barcelona forced to wear old kit in bizarre change for Champions League showdown
Sports.content:
Barcelona forced to wear old kit in bizarre change for Champions League showdown

Barcelona will wear their 2025/26 season third kit against Paris Saint-Germain due to a colour clash.

The European heavyweights meet in the French capital on Tuesday night for a huge Champions League tie, live on talkSPORT 2.



2 Barcelona will reuse their third kit from last season against PSG tonight in a late change of attire Credit: Getty

Barca famously wear a blue and dark red colour combination on their home strip.

This season's away shirt is purple and black, whilst the third kit mixes two shades of blue.

However, Barcelona will recall their orange third kit from last season when they take on PSG at the Parc des Princes.



Why are Barcelona wearing an old kit?

The decision was confirmed by Barca under two hours before kick off.

It's thought that none of their 2026/27 kits have been deemed to be wearable for the match by UEFA.

They teased the kit they will wear via social media earlier on Tuesday as Lamine Yamal, Anthony Gordon and Pedri posed in the attire.



The changed has been made due to the television broadcasting criteria, with both clubs' kits needing to be distinguishable.

Barca's latest kits are adjudged to be too similar to PSG's home shirt, and so they have made a last-minute change.



However, they trained in blue during the lead-up to the Champions League blockbuster.

Kick-off is still going ahead despite the recent riots in Paris and other areas in France.

2 None of Barcelona's current kits are allowed to be worn in the match due to broadcasting rules Credit: Getty

Over 2,400 arrests have been made as protesters clashed with police.

The cost of living, rising oil prices and declining public services are the cause of the protests.



Some cities across France were issued curfews on Monday night, but the PSG v Barca match is unlikely to be affected.

The two teams sit top of the Champions League league phase on six points, with the French side top via goals scored.

PSG were 6-1 winners over Slovan Bratislava on matchday one, before beating Manchester City 4-2 last week.

Barca thrashed Feyenoord 5-1 in their opener and then won 4-1 away to Galatasaray.

Sports.title: Dele Alli offered shock return at EFL club as star goes a year out of football
Sports.content:
Dele Alli offered shock return at EFL club as star goes a year out of football

Dele Alli's former boss Karl Robinson has revealed he offered the midfielder a route back into football at Salford City this summer.

Ex-Tottenham star Alli has now been without a club since September 2025 after having his contract terminated at Como.

5 Alli was last on the books at Como - featuring just once for the Italian outfit Credit: Getty

Once regarded among the best young midfielders in the world, the 30-year-old has been targeting a return to the game this summer.

He was first linked with a move to Barnet after using the League Two side's training facilities, but a deal never materialised, and was later pictured training with semi-professional side Windsor & Eton.

However, Alli currently remains without a club, having last played a competitive game in March 2025 - when he was sent off just nine minutes into his Como debut.

It's a far cry from the ex-England star's glory days at Tottenham, where he won PFA Young Player of the Year award twice.

Alli turned down football return

While finding a club has proved challenging for Alli, his first ever manager has revealed he previously offered him a chance at Salford.

Ex-MK Dons boss Robinson gave Alli his senior debut as a 16-year-old at Stadium MK, before overseeing his development that eventually earned him a move to Tottenham in 2015.

Until earlier this summer, Robinson was in charge of League Two outfit Salford, where he looked to reunite with his former protégé.

Speaking to Boyle Sports and Footy Accumulators’ podcast No Tippy Tappy Football, he shared: “If a job comes up, Dele Alli is always more than welcome to come anywhere I go, if he wants to.

“All I can say is that I hope he’s well, I hope he’s healthy, and I hope he’s in a good place.

“If he ticks all those boxes, I don’t care about whether he’s a footballer. I worry about Dele as a young man – he is someone that I will always be there to pick up the phone to.

5 Alli scored 24 goals in 88 games for MK Dons - all of them coming under Robinson Credit: Getty

5 Robinson was sacked by Salford in June after two seasons in charge Credit: Getty

“I would 100 per cent give him a chance.

"I saw him in the gym in June, and I told him to come to Salford. But he probably looked at me and went, ‘gaffer, come on, I’m not doing that.”

While Robinson's sacking by Salford this summer now rules out a straightforward move for Alli, he will surely be keeping an eye out on wherever his old boss goes next.

But the 46-year-old coach also claimed that the midfielder will still have the self belief that he can play at the highest level.

Naming Manchester United as an example - who are currently struggling under Michael Carrick - Robinson insisted Alli would back himself to transform the club's fortunes.

He continued: “The reason these players are these players is because they have a self-belief and a poorly-developed sense of fear.

5 Alli was one of the Premier League's star players during his time at Tottenham Credit: Getty

“I guarantee if you sit down now, he would probably say he could turn around the fortunes of Man United.

“Because that’s how those real top players who produce their moments of magic think.”

Given Alli's rapid rise in his early career, it isn't hard to see why he would still believe in his ability to make an impact at the highest level.

He previously starred in a Spurs side that reached the 2019 Champions League final and recorded a second place Premier League finish in 2017, scoring 67 goals in 269 games for the club.

The two-time PFA Young Player of the Year was also part of England's run to the 2018 World Cup semi-finals, but things later started to unravel.

After leaving Spurs in 2022, a rapid decline followed with Alli enduring failed stints at Everton, Besiktas and Como.

5 Alli has not played in the Premier League since 2023 - during his spell at Everton when he played just 13 times Credit: Getty

In 2023, Alli opened up on the mental health struggles and childhood trauma which halted his progress, while injuries have also played a part.

Robinson discussed his recent struggles, admitting that despite this, Alli's undeniable talent should have seem him find a club by now,

He said: “When this boy left MK Dons at 18 to go to Spurs, he was getting compared to Lionel Messi, David Beckham, Zinedine Zidane, James Rodriguez.

"To see his rise with the national team and with Spurs, and looking to where he is now – and I hope he listens to this – I don’t know why he’s not playing football.

"He is a tremendous young man who has come through a lot of situations that he’s struggled through, but he’s risen above it to become the person he is.”

Sports.title: Former Man United star released on free transfer would be their best defender right now – ‘A revelation’
Sports.content:
Former Man United star released on free transfer would be their best defender right now – ‘A revelation’

Gabby Agbonlahor believes that Victor Lindelof would be Manchester United's best defender if he was still at the club.

The Sweden international is into his second season at Aston Villa after joining the club for free in the summer of 2025 and has gone on to become a key player for Unai Emery.



4 Man United have problems in various areas of the pitch, while Lindelof is a key player these days Credit: Getty

He started the Europa League final in midfield as Villa beat Freiburg 3-0 to secure a place in the Champions League and claim a trophy.

Lindelof has played every minute of every match this season, bar Villa's victory over Coventry in the Carabao Cup, where he was left on the bench.

And with his contract set to expire next summer, reports suggest he will be offered a new deal after impressing so much.



And Agbonlahor was full of praise for Lindelof, telling Jeff Stelling on talkSPORT Breakfast: "There is one defender who Aston Villa have got who would be Manchester United's best defender right now, and that is Victor Lindelof. He has been a revelation.

"He's been a great pro as well, last season, he wasn't getting as many starts because Ezri Konsa was there.



"But he was fantastic, and I think Taylor Harwood-Bellis has got a long way to get Lindelof out of the side.

"He would be Manchester United's best defender now."

Lindelof's resurgence

Speaking about Lindelof last season, Emery praised his leadership and experience.



He said: “He has experience and he is a very good professional. He has qualities too. He is still being young to play football.

“We signed him in the last moments of the transfer window, because when we identified that possibility, I wanted in that moment everything that he did last week [vs West Ham].

4 Lindelof spent eight years at Man United Credit: Getty

4 Man United are shot of defensive options at the moment with injuries and suspensions causing all sorts of problems Credit: Getty



“In 90 minutes he did everything I expected from him. He was really fantastic.

“Every day it is easy how we are working because his adaptation is so quick, and everything we need, through his experiences, he can give us.

“He gave us experience before, but maybe the best moment he had until now with us was the match at West Ham. He played a fantastic match.

“Now, he has shown us his level. He can’t stop now, and he must keep it! He is very mature, of course. This is very important.



“He is responsible too, and he has experiences, and hopefully he can help us a lot for the rest of the season.”

From that moment on, he hasn't looked back, and he looks to be thriving away from the pressure cooker that is Man United.

4 Lindelof always put everything he had on the line for Man United Credit: Getty

Lindelof's Man United departure

The centre-back joined Man United in the summer of 2017 from Benfica.

At the time, he was considered one of the best young defenders around, and he joined while Jose Mourinho was manager.



However, he never quite lived up to the expectations, but he still managed 284 appearances and penned a heartfelt goodbye when he departed.

He said: "It's been a lot of ups and downs.

"But I mean, for me to be able to represent this club for eight years, it's been an honour and a privilege, and a dream come true.

"I've had so many good memories here. Just looking at the Stretford End here, I mean, I'm going to miss it a lot.

"They're [the fans] with us through absolutely everything, and it doesn't matter the result, every single week, they come here and they support us and they sing their souls out.



"I just want to say thank you so much for taking me in."

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel’s long-time assistant Anthony Barry could land Premier League job
Sports.content:
Anthony Barry could become a managerial target for Premier League clubs in a potential blow to the England national team.

Barry has worked as assistant to the Three Lions head coach Thomas Tuchel since January 2021 when the latter joined Chelsea.



2 Barry is a key member of the England coaching team, but could soon become a candidate for a Premier League job Credit: Getty

He followed the German to Bayern Munich in April 2023 and was then announced as part of the England coaching staff 18 months later.

The 40-year-old former midfielder has also worked in the Republic of Ireland and Belgium coaching teams.

Barry extended his England deal through to Euro 2028 with Tuchel in February after a successful 2026 World Cup qualification run.



However, as reported by The Sun, Tuchel's right-hand man is keen on managing in the Premier League.

He is also likely to be in contention for a top flight job as a number of clubs already face questions over their incumbents.



Which Premier League managers face the sack?

As talkSPORT reported on Sunday, Pierre Sage is fighting to save his job at Crystal Palace just four months after moving to Selhurst Park.

Palace were thumped 5-0 by rivals Brighton on Sunday and sit above the Premier League relegation zone by just one point.



Alvaro Arbeloa has been under intense pressure at Fulham as they went winless in their opening six matches of the season.

They beat Hull City 1-0 at the weekend, but still find themselves in the bottom three.

Nottingham Forest boss Oliver Glasner has had his future questioned, whilst Matthias Jaissle is struggling at Newcastle.

2 Barry is a trusted aide for Tuchel and has plenty of experience in coaching at international and club level Credit: Getty



Meanwhile, Michael Carrick remains under the microscope at Manchester United having gone winless in their past six matches.

However, if a managerial change was to be made at Old Trafford, the club would likely go for an experienced replacement.

Antonio Conte is understood to be interested in succeeding Carrick if need be, having left Napoli in the summer.

The Italian won the 2016/17 Premier League title at Chelsea but may be an option for his former club Juventus in Turin, where he lives.



Brighton head coach Fabian Hurzeler is admired by the United board, and former Germany boss Julian Nagelsmann is also an option.

Sports.title: NFL ramps up security operation for Paris game... as Steelers star TJ Watt's wife calls out league for not moving game after violent protests
Sports.content:
The NFL has promised 'heightened' security for this weekend's clash between the Steelers and the Saints in Paris.

The league's first ever game in France is taking place against a backdrop of violence and anarchy after protests turned ugly in cities across the country.

In France's worst civil unrest in years, rioters clashed with police, set cars on fire, stormed public buildings and engulfed a historic city hall in flames. In Paris alone, more than 100,000 people hit the streets.

The chaos plunged this weekend's clash between Pittsburgh and New Orleans at the Stade de France into doubt, with the wife of Steelers star TJ Watt, Dani, among those to express their shock that the game would go ahead.

'Tell me how this makes sense???' the former soccer player said.

But the NFL has ignored calls to move the game and on Tuesday, an official said the league will step up its security operation.

The NFL's first ever game in France is taking place against a backdrop of violence and anarchy

In France's worst civil unrest in years, rioters clashed with police and set cars on fire

The wife of Steelers star TJ Watt, Dani, expressed her shock that the game would go ahead

Executive VP of club business, international and league events Peter O'Reilly said the NFL is working with Parisian and national authorities overseas, along with the U.S. State Department.

He added that league officials, including senior VP of security Cathy Lanier, have been on the ground in France.

'There's nothing more important from our standpoint than the teams' security, the fans' security - everybody involved with this game,' O'Reilly said at the league's annual fall owners meeting.

'Obviously being very vigilant in everything we do, in all of our planning on an hour-by-hour basis, working closely with the two teams.'

O'Reilly insisted the game was never in danger of being moved. He cited other sporting events ongoing in the city, including a Champions League soccer match between Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona on Tuesday night.

The NFL has in the past moved games to avoid getting in the way of local response to an unforeseen event, and officials believe that is not an issue for the league's debut in France.

'We feel confident that we would not have any impact on the broader resources needed,' O'Reilly said.

Around 2,400 people were arrested, with thousands of businesses damaged or looted

The New Orleans Saints traveled directly to Paris after playing at the New York Giants

'That's always top of mind for us, and we feel confident that we wouldn't be depleting resources in a negative way around this game.'

Around 2,400 people were arrested over the weekend, with French authorities claiming thousands of businesses were damaged or looted.

The rioting overshadowed demonstrations against rising living costs and poor conditions in schools in which hundreds of thousands of people marched peacefully.

The Saints traveled directly to Paris after playing at the New York Giants and are practicing in the area this week. The Steelers are set to travel closer to kickoff.

Sports.title: How Ezri Konsa became Arsenal's 'blessing' in defence: The challenge Mikel Arteta set him to keep William Saliba out of the team, dressing-room impact and his excellent record against the world's best strikers as he faces off with Harry Kane again
Sports.content:
For Ezri Konsa, putting in a last-ditch, match-saving tackle to deny Nottingham Forest’s Liam Delap in the final minutes on Sunday was just part of his job. Nothing more, nothing less.

Mikel Arteta later paused and grinned while describing the crucial sliding challenge on 93 minutes as ‘unbelievable’, after the defender raced back to reach Delap in the nick of time and preserve a hard-fought, attritional 1-0 win – and Konsa's fifth clean sheet in nine Arsenal appearances.

A more fitting word to label the £55million summer buy from Aston Villa rests tattooed on 28-year-old Konsa’s left hand: ‘Blessed.'

For the Gunners could not have wished for more when looking for a player capable of filling the William Saliba-shaped hole in their backline.

When it emerged Saliba would be sidelined for a prolonged period because of a back injury sustained with France at the World Cup, Arsenal fretted and a like-for-like replacement became a summer priority for the team with the best defensive record in each of the last three Premier League seasons.

An Arteta team starts from a rock-solid base with multiple versatile defenders, often at the expense of frontline options.

Ezri Konsa has seamlessly filled the William Saliba void at Arsenal since joining for £55m from Aston Villa this summer

Konsa's last-ditch tackle on Liam Delap, racing back to slide in at the perfect time, preserved Arsenal's 1-0 win over Nottingham Forest on Sunday

Various right-sided centre backs who also cover right back were looked at including Jarell Quansah and even former Tottenham captain Cristian Romero, before Konsa became the one they set their sights on.

A number of factors influenced Arteta’s decision. His background checks were glowing, helped by the defender’s pre-existing ties to the England contingent at Arsenal of Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Eberechi Eze, Myles Lewis-Skelly and Noni Madueke.

Another was his availability at Villa, making 96 per cent of the Midlands club’s matchday squads last season. For a team like Arsenal hunting down four trophies, availability is paramount. So, too, is versatility – which Konsa demonstrated by playing right back for England at the World Cup.

He has slotted in seamlessly thus far, starting six of Arsenal’s seven league matches and the two Champions League fixtures against Napoli and Lille. The statistics reflect a centre back who is Saliba-esque in his comfort with the ball at his feet – and capable of making crucial tackles in crunch moments.

Across the league’s defenders, he ranks fourth and sixth respectively for passing accuracy (96.13 per cent) and average carry distance with the ball (14.8 metres). Konsa’s ability to drive the ball high up the pitch has allowed Arteta's full backs to push on and invert effectively, meaning Ben White and Riccardo Calafiori can be extra men in the attacking line.

Konsa ranks first for interceptions (eight) and second for recoveries (20, behind Gabriel's 21) among Arsenal's defenders. Against Leeds he made three tackles and five clearances in shutting down Dominic Calvert-Lewin, and at Sunderland he was responsible for fending off the extremely physical Brian Brobbey.

On that cold night at the Stadium of Light, he stepped up on a mixed evening for his centre-back partner Gabriel, recovering from a penalty given against him for a tussle with Dan Ballard that was later deemed erroneous, and led the backline with his aerial duels and important challenges to claim another clean sheet.

And then there was the thundering tackle on former Villa team-mate Morgan Rogers to help Arsenal beat Chelsea in his first match at the Emirates Stadium and immediately endear himself to the home faithful.

Konsa's thundering tackle on a counter-attacking Morgan Rogers helped seal victory on his home debut for Arsenal

And Konsa also shut down Dominic Calvert-Lewin against Leeds in another 2-1 win

He recovered from a penalty being erroneously awarded against him at Sunderland to claim another clean sheet in what is proving to be a fantastic partnership with Gabriel

He has settled in well behind the scenes, too. Konsa is said to be very confident around the training ground with a good sense of humour, and is a proud father of young twins with his girlfriend Ronni.

His ease in adjusting to life at London Colney has been noticed by staff, and helped by those existing relationships, with Konsa especially close to Eze. There’s also a maturity he and fellow summer signing Bruno Guimaraes have brought to the squad, having operated at an elite level for a number of years. This was key in the absence of Saliba, who returned to individual training last week.

Arteta has a headache on his hands when the Frenchman is back fit, and isn’t set on a straight swap out. He’s challenged the England man privately to fight for his place.

For now, Konsa’s next task is to shackle his England skipper and Bayern Munich goal machine Harry Kane at the Allianz Arena in the Champions League on Wednesday.

Konsa boasts an impressive record against Kane, having faced him seven times. The defender has four wins against Kane’s teams and three losses, while Kane has only scored twice against him, both from penalties.

The seventh and most recent meeting came in October 2024, Konsa’s Villa beating Kane’s Bayern 1-0 at Villa Park.

‘The Villa-Bayern game… to beat them at home and keep a clean sheet… it was very special for the players and the fans,’ said Konsa. ‘I don’t really look much at those kind of stats (against individual players) but I am relishing the challenge.’

The talent has always been there. Konsa's formative years were spent at Senrab FC, in Forest Gate, London, with alumni including former Arsenal Invincible Sol Campbell and John Terry. Konsa was labelled the next Rio Ferdinand in his youth.

Konsa boasts an impressive record against Harry Kane in seven meetings, winning four of them. Kane has only scored twice against him, both from penalties

Delap was the latest to run into Konsa on Sunday and come up empty-handed

Konsa has stepped up to meet the moment throughout his career as he's risen from Brentford to Aston Villa, become an England regular and now taken to life at Arsenal with ease.

For all the attention on Kane’s extraordinary scoring record of 155 goals in 157 appearances at Bayern, Konsa has built his career on making life uncomfortable for the finest forwards in the game.

Erling Haaland, for example, has just one goal in six games against Konsa for club and country, and Delap was the latest to run into the England man's defensive wall.

On Wednesday in Munich, he has another chance to prove that his calmness and knack for a decisive intervention can carry Arsenal through their toughest test so far this season.

Sports.title: As Harry Kane aims to haunt Arsenal again, and with the Ballon d'Or on the horizon, this is the story of his remarkable rise - and what English football must do to unearth its next superstar
Sports.content:
As Harry Kane closes in on some of football’s most prestigious accolades, the man who gave him his big Premier League break fears Tottenham have failed their next generation. Kane’s success, competing for the Ballon d’Or and becoming England’s most-capped player, reflects well upon Spurs, the club where he came through the youth ranks and scored a club-record 280 goals before leaving for Bayern Munich three years ago. At least, it does to a point. For Tim Sherwood, the brilliant rise of Kane serves to highlight how English clubs can produce more world-class talent if they are prepared to show more faith. ‘The academy side of that club is unrecognisable now,’ Sherwood, 57, tells Daily Mail Sport. ‘They might as well close it up and batten down the doors. ‘You can’t tell me there’s not been one player through that academy who has not been good enough to play for Tottenham on a regular basis since Harry Kane. ‘Either they have let whoever has been the manager close them off or they have not been banging down the door like we used to do. They have failed them.’ Harry Kane will look to take down Arsenal with Bayern Munich and could be crowned as the Ballon d’Or winner next week Kane scored his first Premier League start for Tottenham in 2014 against Sunderland Tim Sherwood, who gave Kane his break, fears Tottenham are failing to give chances to the next generation Kane’s career might have taken a very different route without Sherwood’s 148 days in charge of Spurs after Andre Villas-Boas was sacked in December 2013. It was Sherwood who thrust him into the team for his first Premier League start against Sunderland aged 20, the first of six successive starts at the end of the season. Having spent four seasons there as a player, Sherwood joined Harry Redknapp’s Spurs coaching staff in 2008 and later become technical director, working with Les Ferdinand and Chris Ramsey to oversee the academy. When he took over from Villas-Boas, his instinct was to trust his young players. ‘I didn’t do it because I was on an ego trip trying to put in as many academy boys as possible,’ says Sherwood. ‘I judged everyone on a level playing field. I was qualified to make that judgment because I knew those boys and I’d walked that path as a kid who was awful when he first went into the team and was kept in for long enough to become average and then very good. I know how vital it is for someone to trust you and give you an opportunity.’ When Mauricio Pochettino replaced Sherwood, Kane knew what was required to score in the Premier League. But amid seven different managers in seven years since Pochettino, such opportunities have vanished. The only academy graduate to play in the Premier League for Spurs this season is Mikey Moore, now on loan at Cologne in Germany. ‘I know how important it is for the Tottenham manager to get results,’ says Sherwood. ‘They tend not to look at the academy. Or they’re waiting for a Lionel Messi to fall from the tree, but it doesn’t happen like that. ‘They tend to look at the transfer market or try to get a tune from experienced players. They would argue they haven’t got time to wait and I’d argue back because those players who cost £50million, £75m or £100m, they will let you down as well.’ Sherwood cites Florian Wirtz, who cost Liverpool £116million from Bayer Leverkusen in 2025 and is yet to make an impact. Sherwood and others on Tottenham's coaching staff worked closely with Kane as he developed during loan spells at Leyton Orient, Millwall, Norwich and Leicester When Pochettino replaced Sherwood, Kane knew what was required to score goals in the Premier League and thrive ‘We all know Wirtz has ability,’ he says. ‘He is a wonderful talent. But he has played more than 50 games now for Liverpool. Are you telling me an academy kid would have had 50 games if he was playing as bad as Wirtz? Never.’ Sherwood’s passion is clear. ‘Recruitment has not been good enough,’ he says. ‘Kids have found the pathway blocked by bang-average players who get more opportunity because of their reputation and their prices tags. It’s just not on.’ When Kane’s chance came, he seized it and did not look back. ‘Harry’s mentality was special,’ says Sherwood. ‘I can see his mentality is the same now as when he was 16-18. He doesn’t think he has reached his ceiling. He is still looking to improve. He was never afraid to ask questions if he didn’t understand something and once he understood, he did whatever he could to improve. ‘We had individual programmes to make him better — as we did with all those boys. Now we have too many coaches interested in enhancing their own careers rather than the boys’ careers. ‘It’s geared towards winning. They are applauded by the hierarchy for winning Under 21 leagues. Who cares? No one cares who wins those leagues. ‘I’m a firm believer that if they are not in the first team at 18, you need to find them a pathway. They need to go and play games, but if no one is fighting for those kids they will never make it. ‘All that stuff you hear about, “If they’re good enough they’ll make it in the end”, is the biggest load of b*****ks I’ve heard. There are sliding-doors moments and it’s about getting the opportunity and grasping it.’ Ramsey, Ferdinand and others on the Spurs coaching staff shared this belief and they worked closely with Kane as he developed, supporting him through loans at Leyton Orient, Millwall, Norwich and Leicester. Kane scored a club-record 280 goals for Tottenham before leaving for Bayern Munich three years ago Sherwood questioned Tottenham's sales of Troy Parrott and Will Lankshear, who he believes should have been given the same opportunity as Kane to establish themselves at Tottenham ‘People would say to me, “I know you like Harry but he’s at Orient and it’s not exactly the Premier League”,’ Sherwood recalls. ‘I’d say, “Well, send Luka Modric there and let’s see how he gets on”. It’s f***ing hard at that level. It’s almost a different sport. ‘Just because he didn’t score bundles of goals everywhere he went doesn’t mean he failed. It was just about progression, and it was far better for his development than Mickey Mouse U21s football where no one cares who wins or loses. ‘We weren’t normal in the way we fought for those kids. I have enormous pride in the work put in by me, Chris and Les and everyone else who helped develop Harry Kane.’ Spurs have struggled for goals since Kane and in the summer they sold 21-year-old Will Lankshear to Middlesbrough, where he has scored 11 in 14 games. ‘There are clear parallels,’ says Sherwood. ‘I knew Harry and the other boys like they were my own. I knew how their hearts would beat and how to work them. I don’t know Will Lankshear but if I’d worked with him, I would know him and know if I felt he had the drive and determination and ability to play for Tottenham. I would not have let them sell him for £10m. ‘Put an arm around him and give him a chance. Tell him, “Don’t worry what the crowd are thinking, you’ve got the opportunity and if you do well they’re going to love you”. ‘Big him up. Tell him he can be the next Harry Kane. There’s no reason he can’t be. What are you selling Will Lankshear for when you’ve got strikers who can’t score a goal? Troy Parrott is another I would not have let go.’ Sherwood hailed Kane's mentality and believes the forward would genuinely rather win the Champions League with Bayern Munich than win the Ballon d’Or for himself Parrott made two brief Premier League appearances for Spurs before he was sold aged 22 to AZ Alkmaar, where 51 goals in 97 games earned him a £17million move this year to Real Betis. Kane, meanwhile, forges on towards his dreams. ‘If he can win the Champions League or the Ballon d’Or I know what he will say,’ says Sherwood. ‘And it won’t be a stock answer, it will be a genuine answer. The genuine answer is he would rather win the Champions League with Bayern Munich than win the Ballon d’Or for himself. ‘That’s the mentality we’re talking about. That’s why he’s the best. That’s why I’ll have a lot of respect for the Ballon d’Or if he wins and I won’t if he doesn’t. ‘Kane is a total team man. That’s why he’s a great example to any kid coming through but those kids will not get the same opportunities unless there are people inside these academies fighting for them.’

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo's night to forget: Star, 41, misses huge chance AND a penalty in Al-Nassr win, hours after being attacked by Erik ten Hag for 'letting down' Man United
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo endured a nightmare evening as he missed a penalty and squandered another huge chance for Al-Nassr. Ronaldo's misery started in first-half stoppage time when he failed to hit the target with a spot kick after Joao Felix was brought down inside the box, much to the shock of those in the stadium. Ronaldo, 41, went even closer in the second half when he was teed up for an open goal by Sadio Mane just yards out, but he inexplicably volleyed the ball over the bar. The 41-year-old cut a frustrated figure after that as he threw his hands up in the air and looked to the sky in exasperation, before he bowed his head to the ground. Thankfully for the global superstar, his side still won the match, beating Neom 1-0 after Felix's second-half strike. The victory left Al-Nassr in third place in the Saudi Pro League, three points behind table-toppers Al-Qadsiah having played a game fewer. Ronaldo It’s time to say goodbye to football 🙄 pic.twitter.com/hPCR3Nugdq https://t.co/B6obI4G0d7 — The Final Whistle (@Rufus_45) October 20, 2026 Cristiano Ronaldo endured a night to forget as Al-Nassr held on for a 1-0 victory over Neom Ronaldo's difficult evening capped a tricky day for the Portuguese forward after former Man United boss Erik ten Hag hit out at his attitude in a wide-ranging interview with The Athletic. Reflecting on his time at Old Trafford, the Dutchman accused Ronaldo of letting United down by failing to prepare himself for matches, with the former Red Devils boss claiming the forward pulled out of training sessions and encouraged team-mates to 'save their legs'. Ronaldo left Man United by mutual consent in November 2022 after a bombshell interview with Piers Morgan, in which he claimed he had been 'betrayed' by Ten Hag. Ten Hag claimed Ronaldo did not get himself to the 'right fitness levels' after withdrawing from training sessions and failed to get his heart rate raised to the required level when he did train. 'He let the team down, and he let me down, because we planned with him,' Ten Hag said. 'Obviously, he's one of the best in football history. I respected him a lot. But at that time, as a manager, I had to make a rational decision and keep the players I admire in. 'Many times I say, "Ronnie, everyone wants to work for you to bring you in the right position, but if you can't bring yourself in the box, you can't score". 'He was not capable to do this. It's the wrong idea to put this to me that I expected him to do the pressing, that he's exhausted. But he couldn't. He ran neither in possession nor out of possession. The reason was because he didn't prepare himself.' Ten Hag continued: 'Every top team has to embrace the top player, but the top player has to work for the team. 'He was telling the players, "Save your legs at the training". I understand it when you are top fit; you have sessions, you can save the legs. But first you have to train yourself to get into the right fitness levels.' Ronaldo missed a first-half penalty and also squandered an open goal from a few yards out Meanwhile, on Monday, Ronaldo received a strangely light punishment by Portugal despite walking out on their camp during the recent international break. The forward was provisionally suspended by the country's FA after leaving the squad following a dispute with head coach Jorge Jesus. Ronaldo had claimed Jesus broke promises when he was kept on the bench for their game against Norway. Despite his misdemeanour, the Portuguese FA announced that he has been fined just £215 and is free to play again in next month's international break. The superstar, 41, has technically been banned for a month by Portuguese football chiefs - but that punishment is backdated to his strop on September 30, reports in his homeland claim. That means his ban will be served by the time Portugal's next fixture against Denmark rolls around on November 14. Meanwhile, his piddling fine of £215 will take the billionaire approximately 38 seconds to recoup on his £488,000-per-day salary at Al-Nassr.

Sports.title: The night Rio Ngumoha cemented his status as a future world-beater: Liverpool had a £400m attack at their disposal but it was the 18-year-old who shone brightest in chaotic comeback win, writes LEWIS STEELE
Sports.content:
They used to call it 'Pep roulette' at Manchester City. A phrase coined by fantasy football nerds about Pep Guardiola's tendency to chop and change his front line every week to devastating effect. We haven't refined our snazzy phrase for Andoni Iraola yet – the working drafts are 'AI Bingo' or 'Iraola tombola' – but the Liverpool boss has a devastating depth of attacking talent that, if they all fulfil their potential, can lead this team to dizzying heights. That is caveated with a reminder that Iraola's Reds are simultaneously plagued by many teething problems in other areas and are far from complete. We will discuss that in due course but first, a word on Iraola's deck of cards that contains multiple aces and jokers. With the best part of half a billion pounds worth of attackers not starting this comeback victory against VIllarreal, it was left to others to step up and no one caught the eye more than the potential world-beater but lesser-heralded Rio Ngumoha. At just 18, Ngumoha already has three England caps and is well on the radar of Thomas Tuchel, but he is not yet guaranteed a starting berth at Liverpool and has had to bide his time due to competition and having been asked to swap wings by Iraola after the arrival of left-winger Bradley Barcola. The teenager, who was poached from Chelsea in 2024 to much fury at Stamford Bridge, will cost a maximum of £6.8million but his ceiling is just as high as £125m Alexander Isak, £123m Barcola or £116m Florian Wirtz. Liverpool beat Villarreal 4-3 in a chaotic Champions League encounter at Anfield on Tuesday Alexis Mac Allister was Liverpool's hero, scoring twice as the Reds came from behind to win But it was Rio Ngumoha's display that was most impressive as he showed all of his quality Ngumoha is yet to score this season but was the shining light here with two assists in a spell-binding performance that helped tilt the game in Liverpool's favour. That was far from guaranteed after a shoddy, uncharacteristic and worrying first half an hour. Liverpool 4-3 Villarreal: MATCH FACTS LIVERPOOL (4-2-3-1): Alisson 6; Araujo 7 (Wirtz 46, 7), Jacquet 6 (Gomez 74, 6), Van Dijk 5, Tsimikas 6; Nyoni 7 (McConnell 81), Mac Allister 8; Ngumoha 8 (Barcola 74, 6), Gravenberch 6; Gakpo 6; Koumas 6. Subs not used: Mamardashvili, Woodman, Kerkez, Isak, Chambers, Danns, Laffey. Booked: None. Scorers: Mac Allister 36, 65, Araujo 45+2, Wirtz 68. Manager: Andoni Iraola 7. VILLARREAL (4-2-3-1): Gulacsi 5; Mourino 5, Navarro 5, Veiga 6, Cardona 6; Saliba 7 (Oluwaseyi 46, 7), Gueye 6; Buchanan 5 (Freeman 60, 6), Comesana 6 (Moreno 78), Moleiro 6 (Foyth 54, 6); Mikautadze 7 (Perez 60, 6). Subs not used: Luiz Junior, Akhomach, Costa, Diatta, El Jmili, Gaitan, Macia. Booked: Moleiro, Mourino. Scorers: Mikautadze 4, Cardona 29, Oluwaseyi 87. Manager: Inigo Perez 7. Referee: Szymon Marciniak (Pol) 7. Attendance: not provided. Alexis Mac Allister is also worthy of vast praise as the Argentine struck a brace to continue his resurgence and stellar season after a year-long dip, while Ronald Araujo and substitute Wirtz also scored. As the scoreline suggests, Liverpool's defence was all at sea and that will provide a headache for Iraola in the coming days, especially given they have conceded 10 in their last four games, also shipping three to Manchester City and Austrian side LASK. But while the boss agonises over fixing the defence, he knows he has cracked it at the other end. Ngumoha can trouble any defence, Isak can win any game with his instinctive poacher-like finishing, Wirtz and Barcola are starting to show signs they can unlock stubborn sides. Then there is Cody Gakpo, who returned from injury and showed signs he is picking up where he left off, and the energetic Victor Munoz, who missed this game but was described as a 'Formula One car' in these pages yesterday. And don't forget £79m injured striker Hugo Ekitike. Liverpool's array of weapons in attack were needed to help them get over the mess of the first half an hour, as Iraola was being taught a lesson by his former right-hand man, Inigo Perez, who was the No 2 during the Basque's formative years at Rayo Vallecano. Perez could not move to England when Iraola did because some wise cracks at the Home Office said he was not skilled enough for a work permit. The 38-year-old has made a mockery of that since, leading Rayo to the Conference League final after taking over from Iraola as head coach and now managing in the Champions League, where, for 35 minutes at least, his team played six-time European kings Liverpool off the park. Liverpool fought back after a dreadful first 30 minutes that saw Villarreal go 2-0 ahead Ronald Araujo scored his second goal in a week and celebrated by jumping into the stands Florian Wirtz (right) was also on the scoresheet to cap off a good few days for the German RIO: ONE OF THE BEST I'VE PLAYED Rio Ngumoha said his virtuoso performance against Villarreal was up there with the best in his budding career. The 18-year-old registered two assists and was the star man as Liverpool put a worrying start behind them to come from 2-0 down to beat their Spanish opposition. And the three-time England cap said: 'It's up there with one of the best I've played, I think. I enjoyed myself out there. The team helped me as well a lot. I enjoyed today. 'Like I always say, we have the best fans in the world. To hear my name being chanted is a dream.' Boss Andoni Iraola added: 'The good thing with Rio is he is still 18, he is not the full package, he can add things fortunately for us. 'Hopefully he can continue in the same way. He's not always going to be like this, he will have ups and downs in the process. 'But I'm happy because attitude-wise I think he's in a great place.' Alexis Mac Allister was also a shining light and scored twice. The Argentine said: 'Look at Rio, he was amazing tonight. He made the difference. He was really important and I'm glad for him. 'It's clear the quality Rio has. Everyone knows. It's easy to say he's a really good player but he needs to focus on other things. He worked really hard off the ball.' On his fine headed goal, Mac Allister added: 'It's not something I really practice. My dad is a bit smaller than me but he was quite good in the air so maybe it's something I got from him. 'Last year was a really difficult year for all of us. It was clear I was not at the level and I am the first one to say. Something wasn't right in the group and this manager changed it. The way we play is different, I don't like to compare. I'm feeling good.' By Lewis Steele Villarreal were magic, Liverpool tragic. This was by far the worst half hour of the Iraola era, more worrying than the capitulation against Manchester City. At least that time they had the defence of going down to 10 men. No excuse on this occasion, apprentice Perez was simply schooling master Iraola. Villarreal, nicknamed El Submarino Amarillo or The Yellow Submarine, were enjoying themselves in the land of the Beatles – whose song inspired that tag and is played before games at Estadio de la Ceramica. They were ahead after just four minutes. Virgil van Dijk made a honking error to head a long ball straight to the path of Georges Mikautadze, who could not believe his luck and scored. Van Dijk barely makes one wrong step, never mind a catastrophic mistake like this, and everyone at Anfield looked shellshocked. The 1,500 or so away fans and sea of vibrant yellow shirts were soon jumping for joy again on 29 minutes when Sergi Cardona sprung through a shoddy offside trap and waltzed through on goal to slot past a helpless Alisson for 2-0. Iraola was left scratching his head and probably regretting the six changes he made from the team that fought from behind to beat Brentford on Saturday. But out of nowhere, his team found something and started the comeback, through a Mac Allister header on 36 minutes. The Argentine may be small but is as good as most in the air and connected well with Kostas Tsimikas's corner to score. Anfield found its voice and the Reds responded. Ngumoha made the equaliser with a fine ball that was headed home by Ronald Araujo for his second goal in a week after scoring at LASK. The Uruguayan loanee, here for the season from Barcelona, is quickly becoming a cult hero and is being affectionately referred to as 'Big Ron'. He jumped into the Anfield Road End and made the night of one lucky lady, who received a bear hug. There was never any looking back from there, and Mac Allister put Liverpool ahead on 65 minutes after a dancing run from Ngumoha, before Wirtz came on and put gloss on the victory with a fine finish to continue an eye-catching week for the much-criticised German. Tani Oluwaseyi made it a nervy finish with an 87th-minute goal which highlighted Liverpool's defensive issues once more, but at least they can follow the old mantra of 'you can score, we will just score more'. How long that will last, who knows, but it is certainly not going to be boring this year.

Sports.title: Why defiant Man City fans are going bananas: former forward Imre Varadi on his trademarked giant inflatable fruit based on his famous terrace nickname... with club set to order another 30,000!
Sports.content:
Why defiant Man City fans are going bananas: former forward Imre Varadi on his trademarked giant inflatable fruit based on his famous terrace nickname... with club set to order another 30,000!

Bananas are back in fashion, and Imre Varadi is a man in demand. 'The phone is ringing off the hook,' he explains and right on cue his device pings and lights up with another message.

This time it is a request for him to appear on a radio show coming his way via former team-mate Lee Chapman.

They, like the rest of us, want to know how at the age of 67, and 40 years after he first played up front for Manchester City, his cult status has been revitalised by giant inflatable bananas.

It is a twist of fate not only good for Varadi’s ego but good for his business as two years ago he acted upon the random fact that City supporters came to affectionately refer to him as Imre Banana back in the day by trademarking the name.

Call it a striker’s instinct. Or business acumen after 25 years working as an agent. He saw the opening and made his move.

Now he produces branded inflatable bananas, T-shirts and pin badges.

He sells them around the world and has a partnership with Manchester City, who are understood to be planning to order another 30,000 bananas.

City fans are embracing bananas all over again as a symbol of solidarity in the wake of criticism after the club was found guilty of breaking the Premier League’s financial rules.

Imre Varadi produces inflatable bananas with his nickname as well as T-shirts and pin badges

The bananas have become a symbol of City fans' defiance after the guilty verdict handed down by the independent commission

'I think it’s their way of saying that whatever happens we’ll be behind the team and the club, and we’ll still be having fun,' says Varadi. 'We’ve had bad times. We’ve been in the second and third divisions and never forget the history, but we love the club and we’ll always stick with them and support them.

'It is great fun and it has helped to galvanise everybody. The sea of bananas in the away end at Anfield was great to see and to be at the Etihad on Saturday [against Ipswich] and see all the Mums and Dads and kids carrying them to the game was incredible.

'I’m so honoured and proud to be such a part of it. I don’t think many of them know I was ever a footballer.'

Varadi was born in London with an Italian mother and a Hungarian father and came through the youth ranks at Luton Town.

'They released me and Kerry Dixon, and we both cried our eyes out,' he says. 'But you dust yourself down and get on with it. Kerry ended up playing at Dunstable and I went to Letchworth.

'After a year, Harry Haslam rang me and told me to come to Sheffield United, so I went up there played in a reserve game and scored a hat trick, played in another reserve game and scored again.

'He gave me a two-and-a-half-year professional contract and I never looked back. Kerry as we all know went to Reading, Chelsea and played for England and had a fantastic career.'

Imre Varadi scores City's second in a 3-1 win over Aston Villa in 1986

Varadi in action during a 1-1 draw against Manchester United at Maine Road in 1986

From left to right; Martin Hodge, Varadi, Mick Lyons, Gary Megson and Pat Heard at Sheffield Wednesday in 1984

Varadi did not stay anywhere for too long. He left Bramall Lane for Everton and scoring the winner in an FA Cup tie against Liverpool at Goodison Park remains one of his fondest memories.

'Everton hadn’t beaten Liverpool in years, and I lost it when I scored, running round the back of the goal to celebrate with the supporters. Within three or four seconds I realised these were the wrong supporters.

'It was the Liverpool supporters, and someone threw a meat and potato pie and hit me right in the middle of my face. I can still taste it today. I’ll never forget it.'

At Newcastle he wore the famous No9 shirt, scored goals at a rate close to one-in-two and spent a season playing alongside Kevin Keegan.

In the first of his two spells at Sheffield Wednesday, he won promotion to the top-flight before a season at West Bromwich Albion and the move to City in 1986.

He finished the season as City’s top scorer but could not do enough to stop them sliding back into the second tier. As the next season got under way at home against Plymouth Argyle, there was a supporter called Frank Newton who took an inflatable banana with him to Maine Road, basically for a laugh.

'I remember jogging out on the game and seeing a banana,' says Varadi. 'That was strange enough and then one banana became two or three and then eight or nine and then it went whoosh.' Fans started singing Imre Banana instead of Imre Varadi and the craze spread across the country.

Varadi with Kevin Keegan during his time at Newcastle between 1981 and 1983

'West Ham had inflatable hammers, Norwich had canaries, Grimsby had the fish, but we started it,' says Varadi. 'People have called me Imre Banana from there.'

He scored 31 in 81 games for City before returning to Wednesday in September 1988. There were then three years at Leeds, again with Chapman, but mainly as back up. He did not make enough appearances for a title winners’ medal in 1992.

There was a brief return to Luton, six games on loan, and two successful years at Rotherham among other ports of call before ending his career in non-league, coaching at Matlock Town and Stalybridge Celtic before taking his qualifications to become an agent.

'I just sort of fell into it,' he says. 'I always thought I’d go into coaching but because I had a lot of clubs, I had a lot of contacts and knew a hell of a lot of people. The opportunity came to go into an agency, so I took my exam and I’ve been a FIFA licensed agent ever since.'

For 16 years he worked at the Stellar Group agency, then struck out alone with a small group of clients. 'I’ll always do that,' he says. 'I love working, I work every day. I love interacting with players, speaking to clubs and watching games.'

Varadi was at home on his sofa recovering from a toe operation when he finally did something about an idea about the inflatable bananas.

'I’d thought about doing it years ago but never got round to it,' he says. 'And there I was, watching City winning the fourth title in a row and the bananas were coming out again to celebrate.

'I decided I’d take a closer look into the business and found inflatables were a multimillion-pound industry. I was sure there was a gap I could slide into. Some people think I’m jumping on the bandwagon but I’m the original story. I’m the original Imre Banana. That’s me.'

Sports.title: The Phil Foden show in front of 20,000 empty seats at the Etihad: Man City's hat-trick hero has found the fizz and purpose that deserted him last season as he stakes his claim in style, writes JACK GAUGHAN
Sports.content:
More competitive adverts for the Champions League’s group phase are available – a night when thousands of blue seats remained strikingly vacant - but Phil Foden won’t mind that.

While all eyes are on how Manchester City replace Erling Haaland in the eventuality of a more pressing injury than the knock from the weekend, Foden made his point around who fills in for Antoine Semenyo.

Semenyo will miss the next two months with a knee problem and it will be a fight between Foden and Iliman Ndiaye as to who makes that spot their own. Foden’s hat-trick with AEK Athens in town after notching against Ipswich Town four days earlier do his chances no harm. His first two goals were products of super link up with Rico Lewis, the pair in sync in one-touch blurs of movement, and Foden slamming high into the net with a purpose not always seen recently.

And after appearing generally more buoyant at the weekend, Foden is playing with a little more fizz – the sort he found early on last season before his form nosedived – and just looks more confident.

It is only a start at the moment and Semenyo’s absence should provide a greater chance to build upon that.

‘I consider Phil one of the best English players,’ Enzo Maresca said. ‘For different reasons in the last two or three years, he was not good enough. But I know how good he is. So we are just trying to help him; we are sure that he's going to help us this season.’

Phil Foden sparkled like the player of old as he snagged a hat-trick against AEK Athens at home

With the absence of Erling Haaland in the starting XI, it was up to the Striking Viking's team-mates to seize the spotlight in Europe

City were already leading once Foden first found the net, Elliot Anderson mopping up the rebound once Enzo Fernandez’s free kick had kissed the bar and bounced back.

The free kick had been won by European debutant Floyd Samba, a 17-year-old who became their second-youngest Champions League starter in the Champions League. Son of former Blackburn Rovers defender Chris, the academy graduate scored twice in the Carabao Cup against Norwich City last month in an unfamiliar centre forward role and was called to perform similar on Tuesday.

Samba’s tenacity in tracking back saw him barge Kervin Arriaga out of possession and off he charged towards goal, bouncing off challenges until finally felled 20 yards out. Seconds later, Anderson had his first goal since a £116million summer move.

Rayan Cherki’s sumptuous drag back produced the third, the Frenchman placing into the far corner, after AEK briefly threatened to make a fist of the evening when Stavros Pilios drove across Gianluigi Donnarumma.

Some of the City movement showcased further signs of their improvement under Maresca, and the Cherki clipped pass for Lewis to lay-off for Foden’s to finish first time in netting City’s fourth provided the best example of that. Yet eyes continued to cast up towards the stands. Whatever the reason, it almost felt as if there were more inflatable bananas inside this stadium on Saturday than there were supporters for this continental tie.

The Etihad Stadium and City fans are often dealt a bad rap for attendances but the sparsity was certainly stark. Unusually stark, the new Pep Guardiola Stand yawning three weeks since the guilty verdicts dropped and the appeal lodged.

Rayan Cherki produced a sumptuous third goal but there were fewer than normal in the Etihad to watch the show

The stands were unusually bare - but the rafters will be packed for the return of Premier League action

This will be back to being a full house for their next Premier League assignment, against Brighton a week on Saturday, although it will be intriguing to see how many show up when Napoli arrive at the end of November. The potential to watch Kevin De Bruyne again might skew that somewhat.

The Etihad was only really half-full, a similar crowd to that Norwich game in fact, and those absent missed the Foden show.

That was complete 14 minutes from time when he raced away into the corner having secured a hat-trick, his fourth for the club. A gaping net, timing a run to meet the cross of another European debutant, Ryan McAidoo. Maybe that month off following the red card at Old Trafford did him good.

Sports.title: Revealed: How Lord's is taking drastic action to sort pitch problems for 2027 Ashes Test after 'unsatisfactory' surface against New Zealand
Sports.content:
Lord’s will not host any cricket for 18 days during the build-up to the 2027 Ashes Test in a bid to avoid a repeat of the pitch problems that made headlines over the summer.

The groundstaff had only a clear 10 days before the first Test against New Zealand in June, when a surface of variable bounce was rated ‘unsatisfactory’ by the ICC, prompting a public apology from MCC and earning the venue an unprecedented demerit point.

There were also 10 days between finals day of the Hundred and the second Test against Pakistan in August, when the surface was rated ‘satisfactory’ – the second-highest of the four ratings.

The ECB want to ensure venues have between seven and nine clear days before hosting a Test next summer.

But Lord’s officials are taking no chances when it comes to next summer’s high-profile second Test against Australia starting on June 30, and have given head groundsman Karl McDermott and his team what Rob Lynch, MCC’s director of cricket and operations, called ‘the best chance of producing the best pitch’.

MCC’s determination to deal with the slowness and inconsistency of their surfaces has produced a raft of bold measures, including the recent decision to dig up Pitch 9 – which hosted the New Zealand Test.

Lord’s will not host any cricket for 18 days during the build-up to the 2027 Ashes Test in a bid to avoid a repeat of the pitch problems that made headlines over the summer

The pitch for June's Test against New Zealand was rated 'unsatisfactory' amid variable bounce

It is the first time in over 25 years that the home of cricket has taken such drastic action, taking the pitch out of action until 2029. The process involved digging down 12 inches, and replacing it with four inches of stabilising crushed granite, 20mm of porous matter and nearly eight inches of Ongar loam.

As Daily Mail Sport revealed earlier this year, MCC are also moving ahead with plans to instal three permanent drop-in pitches over the next few years, with a view to staging a domestic match on one of them in 2029, and international cricket the following summer. Each pitch should have a lifespan of 10-15 years.

With the Wormsley ground, an hour’s drive away up the M40, now bearing some of the Lord’s load, MCC plan to reduce the number of days’ cricket they host in 2027 from this year’s 63 to 55 or 56.

Sports.title: Cesc Fabregas' apology to Man Utd boss after coming clean on Arsenal incident
Sports.content:
Cesc Fabregas' apology to Man Utd boss after coming clean on Arsenal incident

Former Arsenal star Cesc Fabregas is set for a reunion with Manchester United after at least one heated moment in the past

View 2 Images Cesc Fabregas will face old rivals Manchester United as a manager this week (Image: Yannick Verhoeven/Newhouse Media/MB Media/Getty Images)

When Manchester United take on Como in the Champions League on Wednesday night, they will find themselves up against a familiar foe. Cesc Fabregas is now in charge of the Italian side but there was a time when he was regularly lining up against the Red Devils as an Arsenal player.

‌



‌



The Spain international was involved in plenty of heated encounters when Arsene Wenger was Arsenal boss and Sir Alex Ferguson was in the United dugout. Few were more heated than the so-called 'Pizzagate' clash, so much so that it took Fabregas more than a decade to share the story of one of the Premier League's greatest mysteries.

‌



The event in question took place in October 2004, in the aftermath of United's victory over Arsenal at Old Trafford. The hosts had denied their opponents a chance to go 50 league games unbeaten after a contentious penalty call left tempers high and Ferguson was hit by pizza as things boiled over post-match.

‌



For more than 10 years, debate raged over who was responsible for throwing the food which hit Ferguson. Finally, in 2018, Fabregas admitted he was the one responsible.

Man Utd players claim they have been banned from interviews by club after Martinez outburst READ MORE :

Rio Ferdinand tells Man Utd they made transfer mistake over 'incredible' Man City star READ MORE :

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

There had been plenty of speculation, with Fabregas named as a potential culprit by Ferguson himself. Former Arsenal centre-back Martin Keown fanned the flames, suggesting "A Spanish fella with great technique" was responsible but not naming any names.

‌



Fabregas was still a teenager at the time of the incident and perhaps didn't feel comfortable putting his head above the parapet. However, during a 2018 appearance on Sky show A League of Their Own, he finally fessed up.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"Martin Keown is a liar because I saw him in front of me just, like, punching people so he didn't see anything," the World Cup winner said. "All of a sudden, I heard noises, and I thought, 'What's happening?' So I go out with my slice of pizza and I saw Sol Campbell, Rio Ferdinand, Martin Keown... everyone pushing each other.

"I was like, 'I want to get in, but I don't know how to', and I threw, just threw it. Once I saw it was hitting, like, who it was hitting, which I didn't mean…"

‌



Later, when speaking to beIN Sports, he confirmed he had already apologised to Ferguson in person before indicating he wouldn't behave in the same way now he is older. "I was young, I definitely wouldn’t use a pizza now, I would get straight in there now!" he said.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



View 2 Images Cesc Fabregas played against Manchester United in the 2004 Community Shield but was an unused substitute in the league two months later (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

In 2022, Fabregas shed a little more light on Pizzagate in an interview with ITV. At the time, he was winding down his own playing career with Monaco and would embark on one final season with Como in 2022/23 before moving into coaching.

‌



"We were 49 games unbeaten. They were so competitive but they were very smart people. I was getting a lot of stick as well," he said when reflecting on the Old Trafford defeat.

"I was very frustrated. You’re warming up and didn’t play. You’re annoyed you lost. I just went in quickly to the dressing room and there was some food there, I was starving.

Article continues below

"I took a slice of pizza and we started hearing noises. The first thing that occurred to me was to throw the pizza because I didn’t have the power or the courage maybe to go into that fight."
