Sports.title: Formula 1’s move to shorter grands prix in 2027 will not be permanent | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Formula 1 will reinstate full grand prix distances in 2028 after shortening the races this year, the FIA has confirmed.

The championship announced last month it will cut 15 kilometres from the standard grand prix distance next year as a result of the new fuel flow limits which will come into force. Shortening the grand prix distances will reduce the number of components teams need to redesign next year.

The shortened distance of 290 kilometres will apply for all grands prix except Monaco, which has run to a shorter distance of 260km for many years and will continue to.

However the first edition of the 2027 Formula 1 Sporting Regulations published by the FIA notes the previous distance will apply again from 2028. “The distance of the race [i.e. grand prix], from the start signal referred to in Article B5.7.2 to the end-of-session signal referred to in Article B5.16.1, shall be equal to the least number of complete laps which exceed a distance of 305km,” it states.

Formula 1

Sports.title: Featured Comment: Budget cap not to blame for lack of winning teams in F1 | Brief
Sports.content:
This week’s poll asks whether Formula 1 needs to rethink its budget cap as the series’ top four team have pulled further away from their rivals this year.

But reader @Skydiverian suggests it might not be realistic to expect F1 to regularly have more than four race-winning teams:

Four competitive teams has happened before but it’s still not great and the problem is as it always is, money. And I’d like to see more teams in a season have a realistic shot of winning races. It’s unfortunate that the stats are not on my side.

Pretty much since the late 80s the problem has been that the best teams could throw more money at the problem to fix it. Now, teams that are significantly behind can’t throw more money at the problem to catch-up due to the cost cap, rather than simply not having the money in the first place as was common in the 80s. (This season is interesting. It seems that Mercedes blew most of it’s cap early to get and maintain their advantage, whereas Red Bull didn’t and that’s in part why Max has had a better car the last two races. But it’s not like Williams or Aston Martin can fix their problems by spending more money to fix the deficit).

The problem is that ultimately there’s no easy fix, but spending millions to be the so-called best of the rest basically seems pointless if there is a very unlikely chance of a team outside of the top four having a realistic shot at the podium or even a win. And that’s always been a problem going back decades.

Some number crunching by looking at the history books: the 500th race was 1990 Australia, 1,100th being Vegas 2023. In those 600 races I’ve found six that were won by drivers driving for teams who finished outside the top four in the constructors championship.

That’s six of 600 races over 33 years where we had a winner driving for a team who finished outside the top 4 in that years constructors championship, 1% of all races. Seven if you count Johnny Herbert’s win at the Nurburgring which to me was a genuine surprise at the time. To me those stats aren’t good enough.

Whether that’s the fault of teams with no money, teams with too much money or teams with a cash limit so they can’t design their way out is up for debate. But my point is that I’d like to see more teams have a reasonable chance of winning. F1 has never really had that and will continue not to unless something changes (maybe by letting teams further down have a bigger budget the following season rather than just more CFD time).

I’d rather that at least 70% of drivers have a realistic chance of winning, ideally 100% of teams. It’s the reason I preferred IndyCar before Alex Palou showed up, results were unpredictable and smaller teams have a chance of getting a win or two. That’s just so rare in F1 and the current cost cap rules will continue to make unlikely.

@Skydiverian

Sports.title: Early coronation for Antonelli? Five talking points for the United States Grand Prix | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli could win the world championship this weekend in only his second year as a Formula 1 driver. Here are the talking points for the United States Grand Prix.

Will Antonelli clinch the title?

The odds are stacked heavily in favour of Mercedes’ new star clinching the title at some point, but most likely not this weekend. That said it is not beyond the realm of possibility team mate George Russell could have another poor weekend and come away point-less while Antonelli takes his ninth victory of the season, putting him over the line.

The title has been won at this track twice before, and both times it was by a Mercedes druver: Lewis Hamilton won the championship there in 2015 and 2019. But regardless of whether Antonelli does clinch the title this weekend it is clearly a matter of ‘when’ not ‘if’.

Verstappen dominating again?

The driver most likely to delay Antonelli’s championship celebrations is not his team mate but Max Verstappen. Red Bull have made a breakthrough with their RB22 and as well as winning the last two grands prix plus a sprint race, Verstappen could have taken victory in Baku as well with better luck.

He arrives at this weekend’s race looking like the driver to beat, with every indication he could dominate the final rounds of the season, setting himself up for a shot at the title next year.

McLaren’s driver headache

McLaren arrive in Austin in a curiously similar situation to last year: a clash between their drivers at the previous race in Singapore has created an obvious tension. What’s more, Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri’s collision during the sprint race in Singapore was more costly than the one they had in the grand prix 12 months ago.

Norris’s radio messages during the grand prix gave the distinction impression he was looking for ways to make amends, having eventually accepted he was the one at fault for their collision. But above all the team will be anxious to avoid a repeat of the first-corner collision which wrecked their sprint race at the circuit 12 months ago. Particularly as a resurgent Red Bull are poised to relegate the reigning constructors’ champions to fourth place in the standings.

US teams’ driver decisions

Of the two teams competing in their home event this weekend, one has settled its driver plans for 2027. Haas has announced Rafael Camara as the replacement for Esteban Ocon, whose Formula 1 future is in serious doubt as few likely alternatives remain for next year.

Could Cadillac be one of them? F1’s new American team is yet to confirm its plans for next year. However its hopes IndyCar star Colton Herta would take Formula 2 by storm and make himself an obvious candidate for promotion have been dashed: he lies 19th in the standings, 181 points behind fellow rookie and championship leader Camara.

Are Colapinto’s die-hards paying attention?

Last week Franco Colapinto spoke out in criticism of the element of his fanbase which has sent vile abuse to his rival drivers, team members and FIA officials since he made his F1 debut this year. The Alpine driver told those attacking others in his name that they are not helping his cause in F1.

Will they take his words on board? We’ll get an indication the next time he is involved in any kind of incident on-track – however slight it may be.

Sports.title: On This Day: Ralf Schumacher wins Formula Nippon title despite spinning out | Brief
Sports.content:
30 years ago today Ralf Schumacher won the Formula Nippon title despite retiring two laps into a rain-lashed race.

Schumacher arrived at the final race at Fuji Speedway just two points ahead of team mate Naoki Hattori. But Schumacher spun out two laps into the rain-hit race (see 3’50 in the video below).

That left Hattori on course for the title, which looked increasingly secure as the laps ticked down. But conditions worsened, and seven laps from home he spun out too, handing Schumacher the 1996 title. Schumacher made his F1 debut the following year for Jordan (now Aston Martin).

Katsutomo Kaneishi won ahead of future Formula 1 driver Pedro de la Rosa. Another future F1 driver, Shinji Nakano, took fourth place behind Masahiko Kageyama. Just seven of the 26 starters were running at the finish.

Sports.title: Sebastian Fundora Aims To Become Undisputed Champion
Sports.content:
Las Vegas, Nevada – On Saturday night, Sebastian “The Towering Inferno” Fundora (25-1-1, 17 KOs) defended his WBC junior middleweight championship at The Chelsea inside the Cosmopolitan Casino against the very tough and gritty Ermal “The Albanian Sniper” Hadribeaj (23-1-1, 8 KOs).

It was a much more challenging match than many expected; Hadribeaj tested Fundora on the inside by making him miss and countering him with an efficient attack. The Albanian Sniper’s total connect rate of 32.3 percent was more effective than The Towering Inferno’s 25.9

percent.

However, Sebastian did outland Ermal in total punches 202 to 144, outlanding him8 of the 12 rounds(Compubox). Fundora was able to score the finishing blow in the last second of the twelve-round fight, winning the fight by controversial knockout.

After the fight, Sebastian said, “It was an interesting fight. I had to go back and fight on the inside and show everyone again that I can still do that. It was dramatic to knock him out at the last second, but we’ll go back to the gym and fix some things.”

He added whom he’ll like to fight next by saying, “I want to go for undisputed in this division. We’ll break either Jaron Ennis or Josh Kelly down just like the last guy and the guy before that. We’ll keep breaking them down. When asked of the two whom he expects to win, Fundora answered, “I do favor Boots.” Meaning him and promoter Sampson Lewkowicz believe it will be Boots whom they’ll have to negotiate for the undisputed crown, but they appear they’ll be playing hardball in negotiations.

Lewkowicz told the media after the fight what he expects the terms of the contract to be, “It doesn’t make any difference…because we need each other. We need 50-50 because we want to unify. It doesn’t matter how many titles. I see so many st**d guys saying on the internet saying he has three belts. You have only two. People already saying he has three.

So many people saying he have three belts. Who’s he fighting? A bum? I respect boxing, and I tell you Kelly can fight.” Sampson went on to state he had already spoken to Jaron’s advisor on the expectations of terms, making it known it should be a 50-50 fight, and hopes they don’t deviate from it by requesting a higher percentage for themselves.

However, if the fight for undisputed does happen next year, the winner of the Boots-Kelly fight will be a three-belt holder bringing the WBA, WBO, and IBF titles to the table, with Fundora holding the single WBC belt. The undisputed showdown is a fight fans will want to see and will truly crown the junior middleweight king.

Hopefully both sides can come to an amicable agreement, and the fight won’t get derailed as were the contract negotiations between Boots and Vergil Ortiz Jr. For now, Sebastian will rest and wait for the Boots-Kelly winner and prepare for his next goal of becoming undisputed junior middleweight king.

Sports.title: Chris Algieri Doubts An 80% Canelo Alvarez Beats Christian Mbilli
Sports.content:
Chris Algieri argues that Canelo Alvarez must bring his absolute best to get past Christian Mbilli. His claim that Mbilli’s style naturally plays into Canelo’s hands doesn’t hold up, especially given the challenger’s relentless engine.

Algieri does give Canelo credit for stepping right into danger following surgery and significant time away, acknowledging the grueling physical test awaiting him.

“Can we give him a little respect for coming off a layoff and a surgery right into Mbilli?” Algieri pointed out to DAZN Boxing. “Yes, he has his faults. I think he falls right into Canelo’s style, but what Canelo are we getting? If Canelo is at all degraded, an 80% Canelo probably doesn’t beat Mbilli. He’s got to be top-notch for that fight.”

Even a peak version of Canelo might have struggled with this matchup. While aggressive fighters give Canelo plenty of targets, Mbilli refuses to give up the breathing room Canelo usually buys with crisp counterpunches.

Gennadiy Golovkin applied pressure behind a stiff jab, leaning on heavy single shots. Miguel Cotto relied on movement during the twilight of his prime. Neither fighter swarmed with the sustained, multi-punch bursts that define Mbilli’s game.

Canelo typically hurts opponents until they freeze. They back off, rethink their strategy, let him rest, and wait for his next opening. Mbilli simply ignores that script.

Mbilli isn’t invincible, of course. Charging forward recklessly leaves massive openings, and eating flush counter hooks could quickly check his enthusiasm. Canelo has the precision to make him pay for being aggressive. Yet landing clean shots is vastly different from dictating the tempo. If Mbilli walks through fire and keeps throwing, Canelo has to scramble back into a defensive shell before his lungs catch up with the previous exchange.

Managing that volume would test any elite fighter in his prime. Asking a 36-year-old coming off major surgery and ring rust to endure it is an entirely different proposition. Algieri is spot on about the danger here. His warning that an 80% Canelo falls short might ring true, but treating an ultra-high-volume brawler as tailor-made for him severely understates the threat.

If Canelo cannot discourage Mbilli inside the first four rounds, the math turns ugly very quickly. By round six, when Canelo’s output routinely dips and his feet go flat, he will be forced to shell up against the ropes while Mbilli pounds away at his arms, shoulders, and ribs. Heavy volume wears down legs just as fast as clean headshots, especially for an aging fighter carrying thirteen months of inactivity and repaired joints.

Surviving that kind of physical tax requires supreme conditioning and fluid defensive pivots. If Canelo is stuck playing defense just to survive the onslaught, he will not have the legs or the gas tank left to mount a mid-fight rescue. When a fighter relies strictly on finding one perfect counter shot to bail himself out, every missed swing empties the reserve that much faster.

In 2019, Canelo capitalized on a faded, battle-worn Sergey Kovalev, whose gas tank was depleted, waiting out Kovalev’s tired arm punches until round eleven to land the finishing blow. Now, the dynamic has flipped, and Canelo finds himself occupying the aging fighter’s corner against a younger, relentless pressure puncher.

Kovalev came into the fight at 36 with heavy miles and well-documented physical wear, and Canelo is carrying an even larger cumulative toll. With more than two decades in the professional ranks, chronic joint issues, and elbow surgery following a year on the shelf, the engine simply cannot turn over the way it once did.

The pattern across the Jaime Munguia, Edgar Berlanga, William Scull, and Terence Crawford bouts showed a fighter relying almost entirely on bursts, resting for extended stretches, and depending on defensive posturing to steal rounds on ring generalship. Against Crawford, the inability to sustain offense or dictate the terms of engagement laid bare what happens when elite opposition refuses to grant Canelo those customary rest periods.

Against Mbilli, relying on selective counterpunching becomes a dangerous gamble. Landing a crisp left hook or a sharp uppercut only helps if it forces the incoming fighter to step back, reset, and second-guess their entry. If Mbilli treats every clean counter as a cue to unload another four-punch salvo to the body, Canelo will never get the pauses he needs to recharge.

Sports.title: Abdullah Mason Targets William Zepeda Or Joe Cordina
Sports.content:
Abdullah Mason is targeting a December return against William Zepeda or Joe Cordina, with a lightweight unification fight or another defense of his WBO title under consideration.

Mason says nothing is signed, but those are the two names emerging for his next appearance. He is also willing to travel to the UK to face Cordina after being told visa issues prevented the British fighter from meeting him in the summer.

“Right now it’s looking like it could be a unification with Zepeda or a defense with Cordina,” Mason said to Brian Custer’s channel. “That’s what it’s looking like it could be. So I’m definitely ready to face anybody in that position.”

Zepeda would give Mason the opportunity to add the WBC belt and test himself against a pressure fighter who believes he can wear the young champion down. Asked about Zepeda’s claim that he would struggle to last 12 rounds, Mason declined to make a counterprediction.

“Two fighters got to step in the ring to really see how it’s going to go down,” he said.

That would be the harder physical test. Zepeda’s volume would force Mason to decide when to trade and when to use his feet. Mason’s willingness to fight aggressively could make it an action fight, but he would need to avoid letting Zepeda dictate how much work he does every round.

The Cordina option offers a different route, and Mason has no objection to defending on the challenger’s side of the Atlantic.

“If he’s had visa issues in the summer, I’m ready to go over there,” Mason said. “It’s a huge fight card in December in the UK. Why don’t I fight him over there if they can’t come over here?”

Mason did not identify the event or confirm a place on it. His December plans remain a target rather than a completed deal.

“Nothing confirmed, nothing signed off on, but that’s what it’s looking like, and that’s what we’re pushing for.”

Mason’s promoters at Top Rank rarely throw a young fighter into a risky fight when they can take an easier route to build an international footprint. Zepeda represents pure peril right now. His punch output breaks people down, and Top Rank knows Mason is far too young to be taking that sort of physical punishment if it can be delayed.

Letting Zepeda put more miles on the odometer before signing off on a unification makes total promotional sense.

Cordina is the soft landing spot. He gives Mason a recognizable British name to put on the record, introduces the young champion to UK fans on a big DAZN card, and presents minimal stylistic danger. Cordina likes to pick his spots from the outside and does not push a blistering pace, which plays right into Mason’s hands.

It would be a low-risk voluntary defense disguised as a big overseas trip, keeping Mason active, winning, and out of harm’s way while Zepeda’s prime ticks down.

Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson Departure Brings Relief Within Zuffa
Sports.content:
Some inside Zuffa Boxing actually welcomed Shakur Stevenson walking away. When the planned Devin Haney matchup collapsed, the company found itself staring down massive financial obligations with zero marquee headliner to show for it.

Dan Rafael noted that parting ways worked out for both camps, despite the optics sting of Zuffa dropping a prized marquee acquisition right out of the gate.

“There are some people that are sort of relieved that they’re not going to, you know, go down that pit of that money,” Rafael said to Total Boxing.

The broadcast setup explains plenty about why Zuffa executives felt that way. Per Rafael, even if Haney versus Stevenson crossed the finish line, the US broadcast rights belonged to DAZN instead of Zuffa’s domestic partner Paramount+. Zuffa faced bankrolling an enormous purse just to drive its biggest potential viewership straight to a competing network.

Rafael pointed out that securing both men in the ring demanded north of $20 million just for the main event. Spending that kind of cash to cement Shakur as the promotion’s central figure, while asking Paramount+ subscribers to tune in elsewhere, looked like bad business.

When the Haney talks cratered, backup plans looked rough. Zuffa put a hold on Newark’s Prudential Center for January 23, but finding a credible dance rival for a hometown showcase proved tough. Footing an astronomical bill for a soft touch would leave Zuffa paying elite rates without the blockbuster that validated signing Shakur initially.

“I don’t think that everybody involved with Zuffa Boxing and/or their parent company TKO was that upset that they were able to separate because I think they might have had some buyer’s remorse,” Rafael said.

Shakur exiting before ever fighting under the banner definitely hurts Zuffa’s reputation, especially after hyping up the Haney clash. Still, the numbers explain the decision. Retaining Shakur only worked if Zuffa locked down the right opponents alongside favorable platform deals to balance the books. Once Haney slipped away, cutting ties cost far less than trying to patch up an expensive mistake.

Shakur commands elite, eight-figure purses, but his track record does not show independent pay-per-view drawing power or the ability to move tickets outside of a localized Newark gate. When a promoter guarantees that kind of money, the fighter has to generate massive subscription spikes, sell out neutral venues, or command major foreign site fees. Shakur has not done any of that on his own.

His safety-first, low-volume style makes that financial gap impossible to bridge. Fans want drama, sustained action, and knockouts. Shakur is technically brilliant, but his emphasis on distance control and minimal engagement often draws boos from casual crowds and turns off broadcast executives looking for viral, highlight-reel content. Promoting a fighter with that approach is an uphill battle, especially for an outfit tied to the UFC and TKO brand, where audiences expect relentless pressure and decisive finishes.

Paying top-dollar purses for Shakur to out-point mismatched opponents in tactical dull contests would have eroded fan interest and bled capital fast. Zuffa avoided footing the bill for an expensive, low-entertainment asset who brings little commercial leverage to the table.

Sports.title: Rafael Espinoza Wants Naoya Inoue Before Moving Up
Sports.content:
Rafael Espinoza has his sights set on Naoya Inoue, citing the Japanese superstar as his main reason to stay at 126 pounds. The WBO featherweight champion is also realistic, keeping the door open to move up to super featherweight if elite opportunities don’t materialize.

At 6’1″, the Mexican titlist wants unification honors at featherweight, knowing a win over Inoue punches his ticket straight into pound-for-pound conversations. He is even game to travel to Tokyo to make it happen.

“There’s also a big fight, the Inoue fight, and I think that’s the fight that would launch me into the world pound-for-pound rankings. That’s my dream,” Espinoza said to The Ring.

Landing the bout is another story. Espinoza presents an awkward, grueling test for anyone stepping up in weight. His height, wingspan, and relentless motor demand total focus. While Inoue possesses the timing and precision to exploit defensive holes, getting inside on Espinoza means walking through fire against a much bigger fighter.

Espinoza feels fully equipped to take the victory, even if he avoids bold knockout predictions.

“I have the qualities, the desire, and I have the reach, the height. I think I have power,” Espinoza said. “I’m not saying I’m going to knock him out. I’ve never liked talking that way, but I have a lot of hope that I can win that fight.”

Under the guidance of trainer Eddy Reynoso, Espinoza has spent recent camps dialing in his fundamentals. Rather than crowding opponents and absorbing needless shots, he has been drilling range control, leaning hard into straight punches from the outside.

The risk-to-reward ratio is completely tilted against Espinoza. Inoue gets credit for daring to be great no matter who he faces, but taking on a tall physical anomaly in his first outing at 126 offers minimal extra reward compared to the extreme stylistic danger.

Instead of Espinoza getting rewarded for ruling the division, Top Rank and Inoue’s team have plenty of reason to look elsewhere. Whether that means targeting a more conventionally sized titlist like Leo Angelo or Bruce Carrington, or grabbing the newly stripped WBA belt against an opponent with fewer stylistic advantages, Espinoza could find out the hard way that being the most dangerous man in the room often leaves you standing alone.

Sports.title: Jaron Ennis Signs Seven-Fight Extension With Matchroom
Sports.content:
Jaron “Boots” Ennis is locked in for the long haul after signing a massive seven-fight extension with Eddie Hearn’s Matchroom. His eyes remain squarely set on collecting every piece of hardware at 154 pounds.

The timing couldn’t be better since IBF champion Josh Kelly signed fresh terms with the promoter on the exact same day. Because both champions share a promotional home, Hearn holds the inside track to set up an in-house unification clash. Whoever walks away with those three belts would then need only Sebastian Fundora’s WBC title to crown an undisputed king.

Ennis, now 29, picked up the WBA alongside the WBO belt after stopping Xander Zayas in Brooklyn this past July. Matchroom hasn’t announced a date or next rival just yet, but the mission statement is clear.

“I’m excited for my extended partnership with Matchroom,” Ennis stated. “Together we have aligned ourselves in all the right positions to get what I want, and that’s undisputed!” A seven-fight commitment gives Hearn plenty of runway. Still, locking down every title means hammering out contracts with rival camps, and Kelly’s signature alone doesn’t automatically settle fight terms.

Fundora brings another challenge to the bargaining table. His team wants an even split for any clash with Boots. If Ennis handles Kelly first to claim the IBF strap, he enters negotiations holding three belts, giving him total leverage to demand the lion’s share. Yet Fundora would still hold the final piece of the puzzle Ennis desires.

Ennis originally teamed up with Matchroom back in April 2024. That run saw him defend his turf in Philadelphia against David Avanesyan, beat Karen Chukhadzhian, then unify at welterweight by taking down Eimantas Stanionis in Atlantic City. Since jumping up to light middleweight, he obliterated Uisma Lima inside a single round before outclassing Zayas to become a two-division unified champ.

Hearn made his intentions clear, stating the entire Matchroom team plans to honor that loyalty by delivering undisputed opportunities on boxing’s premier stages.

Now comes the real work: turning contract ink into confirmed fight dates. Locking down Kelly gets the ball rolling toward three belts, setting up a clash with Fundora to finish the undisputed sweep.

Hearn had no choice but to lock Ennis down with a massive commitment, because letting him walk into Zuffa’s open arms would have been catastrophic for Matchroom’s stable. Dana White and the Zuffa operation are hungry for legitimate, elite names with actual substance, not smoke and mirrors. Losing Boots to that machine right when Anthony Joshua is clearly nearing the final bell would have stripped Matchroom of its true crown jewel in the United States.

The reality is that Hearn’s roster of genuine, division-ruling stars is paper thin. Ben Whittaker was hyped up as a generational sensation, but the matchmaking quickly exposed the ceiling there. When a promoter has to spoon-feed a 29-year-old fighter soft touches like Richard Rivera just to keep the show on the road, everyone sees through the packaging. Whittaker needs careful stage management and manufactured protection to stay afloat.

Ennis is the exact opposite. Boots does not need protective matchmaking or promotional smoke screens to look elite because the skill set is real. He can fight on the inside, switch stances seamlessly, punch with spite, and wipe out titleholders without Hearn having to hold his hand. While British promoters naturally lean toward homegrown cash cows, Ennis possesses the pedigree to carry the Matchroom banner globally and clean out an entire division on merit alone. Locking him in for seven bouts ensures Hearn stays relevant in the US market instead of watching Zuffa build their boxing empire around Philadelphia’s best fighter.

Sports.title: David Haye Urges Fabio Wardley To Take Year Off
Sports.content:
David Haye thinks Fabio Wardley needs to step away from the ring for an entire year to rebuild his mechanics from the ground up following another brutal second-round TKO loss to Daniel Dubois.

While Haye still sees a path forward for Wardley, he doubts a standard eight-week training camp offers enough runway to fix the technical flaws Dubois repeatedly punished. His advice is simple: take an extended break to master the fundamental skills Wardley missed by turning pro without an amateur background.

“He should take a year out. But not a year out partying, holiday. No, just working on the basic fundamentals,” Haye said to talkSPORT Boxing about Wardley. “Go get a good Cuban coach, someone who just gets your legs right, gets your balance.”

Haye is assuming a lot if he thinks a year off in a Cuban school of boxing is going to rewire a 31-year-old brawler who learned his trade on the white-collar circuit. Fighters do not magically develop fluid footwork, ring IQ, and nuanced balance at this stage of life in an empty gym. Those instincts are drilled into kids through hundreds of amateur bouts between the ages of twelve and twenty.

If Wardley steps away for twelve months with millions already sitting in the bank, he will not return as Guillermo Rigondeaux. He will return as an older, heavier, rustier version of the exact same guy, minus whatever sharp edge kept him dangerous.

Taking a year off ignores human nature, especially for a fighter who just cashed massive checks. Inactivity dulls timing and slows reflexes, and when a fighter relies almost entirely on explosive athleticism and punching power, ring rust is lethal.

“In the heat of the battle, you do what you do,” Haye explained. “He hasn’t done the correct thing, enough reps.” “He could continue in this division, and we’ll have some great fights, but it’s not going to be good for his health.”

The blueprint to keep his career alive is obvious: step down levels immediately. Wardley needs active reps under the lights against beatable, mid-tier opposition. He needs guys who will test him for six to eight rounds without having the world-class power or technical precision of a Daniel Dubois or Joseph Parker to punish every fundamental mistake.

The punishment he absorbed across those three elite fights is the kind that takes chunks out of a fighter’s prime. Throwing him into gym purgatory will only make him think too much in the ring, and a hesitant brawler gets knocked out twice as fast.

Sports.title: Josh Kelly Extends Matchroom Deal, Targets 2027 Unifications
Sports.content:
Josh Kelly is staying put. The IBF light middleweight champion just signed a multi-fight contract extension with Eddie Hearn and Matchroom Boxing, setting his sights directly on major unifications for 2027.

The deal keeps Kelly locked in with Matchroom following a breakout run where he claimed his first world championship and successfully defended it. While Matchroom announced no date or opponent alongside the new paperwork, Kelly made his intentions clear immediately.

“I’m World Champion, and I am very excited about the future with Matchroom Boxing,” Kelly said. “Now I only want the biggest fights in the division. Unifications. Bring it on.”

The 32-year-old slickster took the IBF belt via majority decision over Bakhram Murtazaliev at Newcastle’s Utilita Arena in January. He then traveled to Jeddah in July, handing Caoimhin Agyarko his first career defeat over twelve rounds.

Those victories completely transformed his negotiating leverage. Kelly enters future talks holding genuine hardware rather than petitioning as a challenger.

Matchroom must now translate that ambition into reality. Kelly wants fellow champions, though Hearn stopped short of naming specific targets for the stablemate.

“We are thrilled to extend Josh Kelly’s contract with Matchroom Boxing,” Hearn stated. “He is an elite operator and one of the pound-for-pound best the UK has to offer. It is no secret that we have some huge plans ahead for Josh in 2027, where he will be aiming to add more World Titles to his collection.”

Kelly’s signature footwork carried him to the top. Meeting another belt-holder will test if that slick style holds up while mounting enough offensive output to take rounds against elite champions.

Now sitting at 19-1-1 with nine knockouts under trainer Adam Booth, Kelly gave his promoter clear instructions for 2027: line up the champions and let him work.

Hearn is rolling the dice here, because putting Kelly in the ring with Jaron Ennis looks like a recipe for a demolition. If that unification gets made, Kelly is facing an elite-level talent.

Ennis operates on an entirely different level of spite, power, and switch-hitting precision. Kelly might have the flashy reflexes to look cute for two or three rounds, but once Ennis starts cutting off the ring, targeting the body, and applying sustained heat, Kelly’s habit of pulling straight back with his hands down will catch up to him fast.

The foundation holding up Kelly’s sudden championship status looks shaky at best. Squeaking past Agyarko in Jeddah exposed all his familiar flaws. He spent long stretches coasting on the back foot, surviving on safety-first potshots, and failing to stamp any real authority on an opponent who had never operated anywhere near world level.

Before that, taking the belt off Murtazaliev raised plenty of eyebrows. Murtazaliev was relentlessly pressing the action, landing the heavier, more damaging blows while Kelly relied on flashy flurries that largely caught gloves and air. Handing Kelly a majority decision on home soil in Newcastle felt like a gift, not a definitive changing of the guard.

Locking Kelly down to a multi-fight extension right now puts Matchroom in a vulnerable spot. If the grand plan for 2027 is throwing him in against Ennis in a unification, Kelly’s market value could disappear in a defeat.

Ghana News.title: ‘We must move beyond potential’: Upper West Region courts global investors with massive tax holidays
Ghana News.content:
In a major move to correct the historical skew of Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) towards southern Ghana, the Ghana Investment Promotion Authority (GIPA) has unveiled a comprehensive package of aggressive tax holidays and multi-million-dollar investment projects for the Upper West Region.

The pitches were made during the Upper West Regional Investment Forum, an initiative designed to transform the region's raw agricultural and natural resources into high-value commercial enterprises.

Upper West Regional Minister Charles Lwanga Puozuing challenged local stakeholders and assemblies to move beyond merely describing the region's wealth to demonstrating what can be produced.

"Potential alone does not create prosperity. Resources must be developed, ideas must become viable businesses, and opportunities must be supported by infrastructure, financing, access to markets, and responsive public institutions," Puozuing stated, noting that investors need reliable data, viable project proposals, and regulatory clarity before committing capital.

Representing the Speaker of Parliament and the Upper West Parliamentary Caucus, Lawra Member of Parliament Bede Anwataazumo Ziedeng echoed this urgency, warning that the region must actively package and market its opportunities to remain competitive.

"Currently, investment is the way forward. So if other regions are attracting investment into their regions and Upper West we fail to do so, then we will end up being the losers," Mr. Ziedeng noted, highlighting specific potential in the shea industry, cereals, and groundnuts.

To attract this much-needed capital, GIPA Principal Promotions Officer Yussif Mustapha announced highly competitive tax incentives tailored for the northern zone. Agro-processing businesses setting up in the Upper West Region will pay just a 1% corporate tax rate for their first five years, and only 5% subsequently.

"When you look at historical data of FDI flowing into Ghana, you realize that the flow is skewed towards the south, nothing comes to the northern part of Ghana," Mustapha explained, adding that this structured tax relief is a "huge incentive for investment".

Mustapha outlined several costed, bankable projects ready for immediate global investment, including a $20 million Industrial Park, a $15 million Renewable Energy solar facility, a $5 million Commercial Crop and Livestock Program, and targeted agro-processing plants for cashew, groundnut, and shea.

Complementing GIPA’s efforts, Kumasi Regional Manager for the Ghana Free Zones Authority (GFZA), Samad Akalilu, pitched the Free Zones program to investors focused strictly on exports. Companies exporting at least 70% of their production will enjoy a 10-year total corporate tax holiday and a 100% exemption from import duties on raw materials and machinery.

"We also have what we call a one stop shop... so you just walk to us... you don't have to be walking around struggling to get those services done" Akalilu stated, emphasizing that the GFZA has no minimum capital requirements and manages inter-agency compliance, including visas and environmental permits.

A promotional documentary showcased at the forum framed the region as a strategic commercial gateway to the wider Sahel, highlighting opportunities beyond traditional agriculture. Because of the region's heavy reliance on two-wheel transportation, there is a unique opportunity to transition from petrol to electric motorcycles, creating an entirely new mobility value chain.

Addressing the role of youth in this economic transformation, Lecturer and Director for Career Guidance at UBIDS, Prof. Felicia Natu, urged authorities to actively involve students from local technical schools and institutes.

She noted that these institutions have the capacity to produce tangible goods, such as furniture and building materials, and advocated for regional competitions among technical schools to drive innovation and entrepreneurship using available local resources.

Ghana News.title: 700 sewing machines distributed to apprentices in Nkoranza South under  MP’s SOMPA Training Program
Ghana News.content:
In a significant boost to youth empowerment and vocational development, a total of 700 sewing machines have been distributed to hundreds of apprentices in the Nkoranza South Constituency of the Bono East Region.

The donation, made on behalf of the Member of Parliament for the area, was carried out by the Municipal Chief Executive of Nkoranza, Godfred Dapaah, under the SOMPA Training Program—an initiative spearheaded by the MP to equip young people with free vocational skills.

A Pathway to Self-Reliance

The items are intended to equip individuals who have successfully completed the free training program, enabling them to establish their own sewing businesses and potentially employ others in their communities.

The initiative is seen as a strategic investment in the socio-economic development of the constituency, moving beneficiaries from apprenticeship to entrepreneurship.

MCE Highlights Government's Commitment to Youth Empowerment

Speaking at the handover ceremony, the Municipal Chief Executive for Nkoranza South, Godfred Dapaah, emphasized that the donation reflects the government's dedication to empowering the youth and reducing unemployment in the area.

"This initiative is not just about giving out machines; it is about giving hope and creating opportunities for our young people to become self-reliant," Mr. Dapaah said. "The MP and the government are committed to ensuring that the youth of Nkoranza South have the tools they need to succeed. I urge all beneficiaries to take good care of these machines and use them to build successful businesses."

He further noted that the SOMPA Training Program is a testament to the government's focus on skills development as a driver of economic growth.

Traditional Council Commends MP

Speaking on behalf of Nananom, the Krontihene of the Nkoranza Traditional Council, Nana Akwasi Agyei, praised the MP for contributing to the socio-economic development of the area.

He urged the beneficiaries to make good use of the machines given to them, emphasizing that the equipment represents an opportunity to build sustainable livelihoods.

"The MP is doing a great job contributing to the socioeconomic development of our area," Nana Akwasi Agyei said. "To the beneficiaries, these machines are your future—make good use of them."

Regional Minister Charges Beneficiaries to Be Hardworking

The Bono East Regional Minister, who was represented at the event by the NDC's Regional Political Coordinator, Prince Opoku Mensah, also addressed the gathering.

Speaking on behalf of the Regional Minister, Mr. Opoku Mensah commended the MP for the initiative and charged the participants to be hardworking and dedicated as they begin their entrepreneurial journeys.

"The Regional Minister sends his warm regards and appreciation to the MP for this wonderful initiative," he said. "But he also wants to remind you that receiving these items is only the beginning. You must be hardworking, disciplined, and committed to your craft. Success does not come overnight—it comes through dedication and perseverance."

He further encouraged the beneficiaries to see themselves as job creators rather than job seekers, noting that with the right attitude, they could grow their businesses and employ others in their communities.

Beneficiaries Express Gratitude

Some of the beneficiaries expressed their heartfelt appreciation to the legislator for the gesture, noting that the support will go a long way in helping them establish their sewing businesses.

For many of the young artisans, purchasing a sewing machine after completing their apprenticeship had seemed an impossible dream. The donation has now lifted that burden, giving them a head start in their entrepreneurial journey.

"I am so happy. I didn't know how I was going to start my sewing business. This support will go a long way. We are very thankful to the MP," one beneficiary said.

About the SOMPA Training Program

The SOMPA Training Program is an initiative by the MP aimed at providing free vocational training to the youth in Nkoranza South. The program focuses on equipping beneficiaries with practical skills that enable them to become self-employed and contribute to the local economy.

With 700 machines now in the hands of skilled artisans, the Nkoranza South Constituency is witnessing not just a donation—but the birth of hundreds of new businesses set to stitch together a brighter economic future.

Ghana News.title: Obuasi SHTS sex scandal: Lack of safeguarding training for teachers raises concern — Father
Ghana News.content:
A father of five girls has expressed concern about the apparent lack of formal safeguarding training for teachers, saying it raises serious questions about how students are protected in schools.

Francis Deamenu said parents entrusted their children to teachers to provide education and help shape their character, but that responsibility must also include ensuring their safety.

Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Tuesday, October 20, amid allegations of sexual abuse involving female students at Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS), he said parents were deeply worried about what might be happening to their children while they were at school.

“I feel highly embarrassed because looking at the kids that we have sent there, we don't actually know what is happening there,” he said.

Mr Deamenu said comments during the programme suggesting that teachers had not received formal training in safeguarding students highlighted a major challenge for parents and the education system.

“It is a very serious headache,” he said, adding that parents had a shared responsibility to ensure their children were protected.

He said the relationship between parents and teachers depended on trust, with families expecting schools to provide formal education while working alongside parents in the moral upbringing of their children.

“We have entrusted them [teachers] with the kids that are our properties. We just want them to give them a formal education so that the moral aspect will also play our role. They also play their role,” he said.

His comments come amid investigations into allegations of sexual abuse involving female students at Obuasi SHTS. The school’s headmaster, Zakaria Abdulai, has been interdicted by the Ghana Education Service (GES) and arrested by the Ghana Police Service as investigations continue following a JoyNews investigation by investigative correspondent Manasseh Azure Awuni.

The allegations have renewed public concern about student safety, the responsibility of school authorities to protect children and the systems in place to prevent and respond to abuse.

Mr Deamenu’s concerns underscore the importance of equipping teachers with appropriate safeguarding knowledge and clear procedures for identifying, reporting and responding to suspected abuse. The allegations against the headmaster remain subject to investigation.

Ghana News.title: ‘It is never your fault’ — advocate tells sexual abuse survivors
Ghana News.content:
Amtu Akumfi-Ameyaw

A co-founder of On This Side, Amtu Akumfi-Ameyaw, has urged survivors of sexual abuse to reject self-blame, stressing that responsibility for abuse rests with the perpetrators and not the victims.

She said adults had a duty to protect children and ensure their safety and that survivors needed constant reassurance that they were not to blame for what had happened to them.

“We have to keep reminding survivors that it is never their fault. It is never your fault,” she said on Joy News’ PM Express on Tuesday, October 20.

“If you're a survivor listening to me today, if you have a child that's a survivor, if you have happened to become a parent yourself and you were a survivor when you were a lot younger, this is a reminder that it is never your fault.”

Her comments come amid national concern over allegations of sexual abuse involving female students at Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS), where headmaster Zakaria Abdulai has been interdicted by the Ghana Education Service (GES) and arrested by the police as investigations continue.

The case has attracted widespread attention following reports by JoyNews investigative correspondent Manasseh Azure Awuni.

Ms Akumfi-Ameyaw said adults entrusted with the care of children must be held to their responsibility to protect them from harm.

“Adults are supposed to be responsible. Adults are supposed to protect you and make sure that you are safe. So it is never your fault that they abused you,” she said.

Abuse cuts across school levels

Ms Akumfi-Ameyaw said cases of sexual abuse were not confined to senior high schools, citing experiences involving children at primary and junior high school levels.

She recounted the experience of a colleague who had been abused in a classroom at the age of eight, almost nine, and who was now in tertiary education.

She also referred to a separate case involving a 12-year-old girl approaching her 13th birthday, in which her organisation had helped secure a conviction. In that case, she said, the perpetrator was someone close to the child’s family.

Ms Akumfi-Ameyaw said her organisation had also received cases involving alleged abuse by teachers, underscoring the need for children to be protected in schools and other settings where adults exercise authority over them.

Her examples highlighted the different circumstances in which abuse can occur and the importance of taking disclosures seriously, regardless of a child’s age or relationship to the alleged perpetrator.

Calls for stronger action

The advocate also criticised what she described as failures to adequately protect students, saying those working to expose abuse had to be prepared to speak out despite resistance.

“I know that I keep saying that. I know that abusers are not happy with me this week, but that's not why we do the work. We do the work because we need to see results,” she said.

She added: “And I would repeat that good girls don't get the jobs done. Only the people that are ready to take the risk and are ready to put their voices out there.”

Ghana News.title: USTED professor calls for Ghana-backed research into locally suited drainage solutions
Ghana News.content:
A coastal engineering and climate adaptation specialist at the University of Skills Training and Entrepreneurial Development (USTED), Professor Isaac Boateng, has urged Ghanaian research funders to invest in studies that identify sustainable drainage solutions suited to local conditions.

Speaking at a workshop on teaching Sustainable Drainage Systems (SuDS) in Ghanaian TVET and higher education institutions, Prof. Boateng said research is needed to determine which interventions work best across the country.

“I therefore appeal to the Ghana Research Fund to consider investing in sustainable drainage system research in Ghana,” he said.

He also appealed to the British Council to consider additional funding for the project.

“Given the challenges, the British Council may consider giving the team additional funding to enable us to deal with the additional identified issues,” he said.

Prof. Boateng said international experience, including lessons from the United Kingdom, could inform Ghana’s efforts, but warned against adopting designs without adapting them to local conditions.

“Successful knowledge transfer does not mean copying designs without considering local realities,” he said, citing Ghana’s rainfall patterns, soil conditions, available materials, land constraints, maintenance capacity and financial circumstances.

He said locally generated evidence would help guide engineering practice and public policy, and called for field monitoring, student research and collaboration across disciplines.

The workshop addressed flooding and stormwater management challenges in Ghanaian communities. Prof. Boateng cited rapid urbanisation, changing rainfall patterns, expanding impermeable surfaces, blocked drains and encroachment on waterways as factors that can worsen flooding.

“Rather than treating stormwater as waste, we must manage it as a resource,” he said. Sustainable drainage approaches can slow runoff, support infiltration and storage, and improve water quality. Examples include rain gardens, permeable pavements, vegetated swales, green roofs and rainwater harvesting.

He said these approaches should complement conventional drainage and be selected according to local site conditions. He also called for SuDS concepts to be integrated into existing engineering, construction, environmental management and urban planning courses, with practical learning opportunities for students.

“A drainage system is not successful simply because it has been constructed. It must continue to function effectively throughout its service life,” he said, stressing the importance of inspection, maintenance, performance monitoring and long-term cost management.

“The drains we design today will influence the safety of our communities tomorrow,” he said. “The skills we teach today will shape the infrastructure of the next generation,” he added.

Associate Professor of Real Estate at Edinburgh Napier University and project lead, Dr Cletus Moobela, said the project aims to adapt international knowledge and solutions to Ghanaian conditions.

“Our aim is to take solutions developed and applied globally and adapt them to the Ghanaian context,” he said. “We recognise that not every solution will be suitable for Ghana,” he stated.

Dr Moobela said the project focuses on education and curriculum development rather than installing drainage systems at individual sites. The team is working with instructors and educational institutions to introduce SuDS into teaching.

“Our focus is on the institutions responsible for educating and training future professionals,” he said.

The project will assess whether instructors incorporate SuDS into their curricula, gather feedback from students and examine the extent to which educational institutions adopt the approaches.

Dr Moobela said graduates entering the built environment would be expected to apply what they learn in their professional careers.

Higher Education Project Manager at the British Council in Ghana, Afia Yeboah Agyeman, thanked Edinburgh Napier University and USTED for working together on the project.

“I want to say thank you to Edinburgh Napier and USTED for coming together on such an important project,” she said.

Afia said drainage problems were a major concern in Ghana and expressed hope that the project would make a positive difference.

“We are hoping to see the positive impact that this project will create,” she said.

She also hoped the initiative would attract more partnerships and funding so it could expand across other higher education institutions, with SuDS embedded in curricula and educators receiving further training.

“Moving forward, [we hope to] draw more partnerships, more funds to support this project on a larger scale across other higher education institutions and embed SuDS in the curriculum, [with] capacity building of teachers,” she said.

Afia said the project forms part of the British Council’s work to facilitate transnational education partnerships between Ghanaian institutions and UK universities. The Council facilitated five such partnerships last year, she said, enabling institutions to share expertise and explore ways to work together. The Council is also developing a policy to guide transnational education collaboration.

Ghana News.title: ‘Some schoolgirls position themselves to sexually exploit teachers for their money’ – Teacher alleges
Ghana News.content:
Stephen Desu

A teacher at Ekumpoano Catholic Basic School, Stephen Desu, has raised concerns about alleged transactional sexual relationships between teachers and female students, saying some girls seek money from teachers in exchange for sex while others may be drawn into such arrangements because of financial hardship.

Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Tuesday, October 20, during a discussion on allegations of sexual abuse involving female students at Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS), Mr Desu said the issue had different dimensions and required attention to the financial pressures facing students.

“There are girls in schools who position themselves to sexually exploit teachers for their money whilst teachers get sex from them in a transactional relationship,” he said.

He cited concerns about students’ access to food and money, saying some teachers had allegedly given female students money during periods when food provision in schools was a concern, with sex exchanged in return.

“Especially when this food issue came up in our schools, where they're not getting food. Some teachers stepped up, and they were giving the girls money, and they were exchanging sex for the money they were giving them,” he said.

Mr Desu urged parents to consider how their daughters were meeting their needs when they were away at school, particularly when they received little financial support from home.

“If you leave your girl child in school and you don't support her with money and she's surviving, you as a parent, what makes you think that that child is surviving just because she's just there?” he asked.

Calls for vigilance and accountability

The teacher said the profession had a responsibility to protect students while acknowledging that misconduct could occur among a large workforce.

“I mean, all professions can boast, but the teacher taught them all. So we position ourselves as the noble profession. Unfortunately, if you have more than 300,000 persons in your classroom as teachers, you may get such persons as predators,” he said.

His comments came amid heightened public scrutiny of alleged sexual abuse involving more than 14 female students at Obuasi SHTS. The school’s headmaster, Zakaria Abdulai, has been interdicted by the Ghana Education Service (GES) and arrested by the police as investigations continue.

The case has attracted widespread attention following reports by JoyNews investigative correspondent Manasseh Azure Awuni.

The case has prompted renewed debate about student protection, the handling of complaints of sexual misconduct and the responsibilities of school authorities.

While Mr Desu described some relationships as transactional, any sexual relationship between a teacher and a student raises serious concerns about the imbalance of power and the teacher’s duty of care. Financial vulnerability can also make students more susceptible to coercion or exploitation.

Ghana News.title: Obuasi SHTS: ‘You are supposed to be the protector’ — Safeguarding Lead questions school’s response
Ghana News.content:
Ashesi University’s Safeguarding Lead, Dr Millicent Adjei, has questioned Obuasi Senior High Technical School’s response to safeguarding concerns. She says children entrusted to a school must feel safe enough to report abuse.

Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Tuesday, she identified two failures in the accounts presented. These were boundary crossings between staff and students, and an environment that discouraged children from speaking up.

“When you are given that duty of care, you are supposed to be the protector. You are supposed to create that environment where children will be able to come to you, right?”

Dr Adjei is Ashesi University’s Director of International Programs and Campus Cohesion, and its Safeguarding Lead.

Her comments follow Manasseh Azure Awuni’s investigation, Inside the Dreaded Headmaster’s Bungalow. It examines allegations of sexual abuse against Obuasi SHTS headmaster Zakaria Abdulai.

The investigation found that authorities received complaints months before they suspended him.

The Ghana Education Service has interdicted the headmaster pending investigations. A complaint has also been lodged with the police.

Dr Adjei said the first boundary was crossed when children were allowed to run personal errands for staff.

“Where children are going to the headmaster's house, that is the first level that shouldn't have happened,” she said.

She argued that asking students to collect and carry food was inappropriate in itself. Her concern extended beyond where the food was delivered.

The second failure, she said, concerned students’ confidence in the school’s reporting system.

Referring to an account discussed on the programme, she said a girl had not felt comfortable reporting her experiences herself.

“It took the girl's house prefect to go and report, and the girl had several experiences.”

Dr Adjei also cited an account of the girl being hospitalised after being caned. She said nothing had been done about it.

For her, these accounts raised questions about whether the school had created conditions in which children could seek help.

“So the second layer, where an environment that doesn't support speaking up when some of these things happen, was also broken,” she said.

She maintained that the school’s responsibility included giving students the confidence to approach someone with their concerns.

“The school did not create that environment for the children, for the young children to be able to have that confidence to report to anyone.”

Ghana News.title: Obuasi SHTS: ‘That boundary should not be crossed’ – Safeguarding Lead on students’ food errands
Ghana News.content:
Ashesi University’s Safeguarding Lead, Dr Millicent Adjei, says asking students to collect food for school authorities crosses a boundary that should protect children from the outset.

Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Tuesday, she identified food errands and an environment that discouraged reporting as key safeguarding failures in the Obuasi Senior High Technical School case.

Dr Adjei, also Director of International Programs and Campus Cohesion at Ashesi, said the concern began when staff assigned children personal errands.

“From what is shared, right from even asking a child entrusted to you to take care of your elderly needs, go to the cafeteria, carry your food for you. That boundary should not be crossed, right?”

She said allowing students to take food to the headmaster’s residence represented the first breakdown in protection. Her objection extended to students delivering food elsewhere.

“Whether he carried the children to the classroom or wherever, that is a no-no.”

Her comments follow Manasseh Azure Awuni’s JoyNews investigation, Inside the Dreaded Headmaster’s Bungalow. It examines allegations of sexual abuse involving Obuasi SHTS headmaster Zakaria Abdulai.

The investigation also documented complaints made to authorities months before his suspension.

The Ghana Education Service has interdicted the headmaster pending investigations. A complaint has also been lodged with the police.

Dr Adjei said a second failure concerned whether students felt safe enough to report their experiences.

“The second level is the environment, the environment that didn't make it conducive because one of the victims did not feel confident enough or comfortable enough to report, so that enabling environment that allows and empowers them to report was broken.”

Referring to the account discussed on the programme, she said a girl’s house prefect had to report the matter. She also cited an account of the girl being hospitalised after being caned, without action being taken.

For Dr Adjei, adults entrusted with children must create conditions that encourage them to speak up.

“So the second layer, where an environment that doesn't support speaking up when some of these things happen, was also broken, because when you are given that duty of care, you are supposed to be the protector.”

“You are supposed to create that environment where children will be able to come to you, right?”

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.
