World.title: Uduaghan’s remains arrive Delta as tributes pour in
World.content:
•Oborevwori, Obi, Obaseki, others pay tribute

By Dapo Akinrefon, Jimitota Onoyume & Ochuko Akuopha

WARRI—The remains of former Delta State governor, Dr. Emmanuel Uduaghan, arrived in the state, yesterday, as Governor Sheriff Oborevwori and his wife, Tobore Oborevwori, joined members of the late governor’s family to receive them at Osubi Airport, Okpe Local Government Area of the state.

Oborevwori and his wife later visited the family at the deceased’s residence in Warri, where they commiserated with his widow, Deaconess Roli Uduaghan.

The governor described the late Uduaghan as his boss, recalling the political support he received from him and his appointment as one of his special advisers in 2007.

“He contributed immensely to the development of Delta State, most especially the Asaba International Airport. He was a man of few words. He was very articulate, calm. He has gone, but he can never be forgotten by Deltans,” Oborevwori said.

Uduaghan’s death was announced on Monday by his son, Toju. He was 71.

The deceased governed Delta State from 2007 to 2015, and also served as commissioner for health and secretary to the state government during the administration of former Governor James Ibori.

Meanwhile, tributes have continued to pour in for the former governor, with the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Peter Obi; Chairman of the Niger Delta Development Commission, NDDC, Mr. Chiedu Ebie; former Edo State governor, Godwin Obaseki; and NDC governorship candidate, Deacon Chris Iyovwaye, acknowledging his contributions to public service and Delta State’s development.

Obi, in his condolence message, recalled the cordial relationship he shared with Uduaghan when they served as governors of their respective states, saying the late governor treated him like a younger brother.

“I am deeply saddened by the passing of my very dear elder brother, His Excellency, Dr Emmanuel Eweta Uduaghan, former Governor of Delta State. In my interactions with him, he treated me like his junior brother,” Obi said.

He recalled their collaboration in advocating the award of the contract for the Second Niger Bridge, which he described as important to national integration, commerce and the development of the South-East and South-South.

Obi extended his condolences to Uduaghan’s family, the Delta State Government and the people of the state, praying for the deceased’s eternal rest.

Ebie, in a statement by his media aide, Jerome-Mario Utomi, described Uduaghan’s death as a moment of collective grief, saying his contributions to public life would continue to inspire future generations.

“Beyond the offices he occupied and the political milestones he recorded, Dr Uduaghan was a son of Delta whose life was intertwined with the aspirations, challenges and development journeys of his people,” Ebie said.

On behalf of his family and the NDDC Governing Board and Management, he commiserated with the Uduaghan family and the people of Delta State, praying to God to grant them the strength to bear the loss.

Obaseki described the death as a painful loss to Delta State, the South-South region and Nigeria’s political community.

He said Uduaghan, a medical doctor by training, brought a deep sense of service to public life and pursued a vision of a Delta beyond oil during his tenure as governor.

According to Obaseki, the former governor invested in the welfare of the people and promoted regional cooperation among South-South states.

He said Uduaghan’s contributions to Delta State and the relationships he built would endure as part of his legacy.

Iyovwaye, in his condolence message, said he received news of Uduaghan’s death with a heavy heart, describing the deceased as an elder brother with whom he shared a relationship built on mutual respect.

He said Uduaghan’s administration would be remembered for the Delta Beyond Oil initiative, which sought to diversify the state’s economy, as well as his contributions to healthcare, education, infrastructure and human capital development.

Iyovwaye extended his condolences to the deceased’s wife, children, the Uduaghan family, the Itsekiri nation and the people of Delta State, praying for strength for the family and eternal rest for the departed former governor.

Uduaghan was a political bridge builder without bitterness – Evah

Also, Coordinator of the Ijaw Monitoring Group, IMG, Chief Joseph Evah, has described late Uduaghan, as a man who had a heart of gold and a spirit for humanity.

The former former Publicity Secretary, of the Ijaw National Congress, INC, said: “Dr. Uduaghan was the first political symbol of Niger Delta unity. He was a political bridge builder without bitterness. His distribution of infrastructures across the state was without bias. I remembered when he visited Ijaw Monitoring Group’s office in Lagos and toured the Niger Delta Hall of Fame in 2006 when he has contesting for governorship, he said ‘seeing the faces of great men and women on the wall of the hall of fame here, you have confirmed to me that all your struggle against Ken Saro-Wiwa’s trials and River Niger dredging without EIA and our dead seaports among advocacy you pursue during the military era is for the genuine unity of our region. ‘The faces I am seeing here represent all the tribes in our region.’

A detribalised statesman sleeps, Agbeyi mourns

Chairman of Ifiekporo Community in Warri South Local Government Area of Delta State, Dr. Monday Agbeyi, yesterday, described Uduaghan’s death as a painful personal tragedy and a monumental blow to the state and Nigeria.

Agbeyi, who shared a close relationship with the late former governor, said Uduaghan was more than a political leader to him, but a father, mentor and confidant whose exemplary leadership, compassion and commitment to peace, unity and human development would remain enduring legacies.

Agbeyi disclosed that he was overwhelmed by shock and disbelief when he learnt of Uduaghan’s passing.

In a condolence statement, Agbeyi said described Uduaghan was a detribalised Nigerian, whose leadership transcended ethnic, political and religious boundaries.

According to him, the former governor was a firm believer in the unity of Delta State and Nigeria, demonstrating throughout his public service that leadership should be driven by compassion, inclusiveness and a genuine commitment to the common good rather than narrow ethnic or political interests.

Uduaghan: Deltans mourn, hail his contributions

Former Speaker of the Delta State House of Assembly, Mr. Peter Onwusanaya, expressed sadness over the death of the former governor.

Onwusanya, in a statement, described the late governor as a boss and one of the greatest Deltans who ever propelled peace, unity and development in the state.

He said Uduaghan was a leader in all ramifications, and was disposed to all, irrespective of ethnicity or political party affiliation.

He commiserated with the family, and also prayed to God to grant repose to his gentle soul and his friends, political associates and others he left behind the fortitude to bear the loss.

Similarly, former Nigerian Envoy to Thailand, Ambassador Oma Djebah expressed grief over Uduaghan’s demise.

Oma Djebah described the late former Governor as a visionary statesman and a detribalized leader whose huge legacies of peacebuilding, human capital development and infrastructural development in Delta State and Nigeria would remain evergreen in the minds of all.

“I am deeply shocked and saddened over the sad demise of this great leader, a patriot, and a very compassionate administrator who gave his all in his service to Delta State and Nigeria.

“His death has created a void that would be very difficult to fill. I’m still short of words to convey my feelings over this sad loss”, he said.

Djebah recalled that the late former Governor contributed immensely to the sustainable peace and security in the Niger Delta region, especially in helping to broker enduring peace during the volatile Niger Delta crisis.

“He was resilient, forthright, educated and visionary. He was a great boss, friend, leader and astute administrator.”

His politics was highly refined. He led from the front, and with his heart,” Djebah said.

World.title: NCC, Customs move against non-compliant mobile devices
World.content:
By Juliet Umeh

The Nigerian Communications Commission, NCC, has announced plans to strengthen collaboration with the Nigeria Customs Service, NCS, to check non-compliant mobile devices entering the country.

It warned that devices that failed to meet regulatory requirements might be blocked from accessing telecommunications networks.

The commission said the initiative would improve the monitoring of imported devices, ensure compliance with applicable duties and promote fair competition among businesses in the communications equipment market.

In a notice issued on October 19, 2026, the NCC reminded manufacturers, importers, distributors, dealers and retailers of their obligations under the Nigerian Communications Act 2003, the Type Approval Regulations 2024 and the Type Approval Business Rules 2024.

The commission stated that all device models intended for importation, assembly, distribution or sale in Nigeria must obtain the required type approval.

It said: “All device models intended for importation, assembly and distribution or sale in Nigeria must have obtained the required NCC Type Approval.”

The requirement, according to the NCC, is backed by Section 132 of the Nigerian Communications Act 2003 and Regulation 4 of the Type Approval Regulations 2024.

As part of the compliance process, Original Equipment Manufacturers, OEMs, Original Device Manufacturers, ODMs, importers and other responsible suppliers are required to submit the International Mobile Equipment Identity, IMEI, information of individual devices through approved channels for verification before sale and distribution.

The commission also directed distributors, dealers and retailers to examine devices already in their stock and work with suppliers to resolve any outstanding compliance issues.

Newly imported devices must equally satisfy the applicable approval and verification requirements before being placed on the market.

Explaining the enforcement measures, the NCC said it was strengthening monitoring through technology-enabled verification to identify irregularities in the importation and distribution of communications devices.

“The automated Type Approval Compliance process will strengthen the Commission’s oversight of devices entering the Nigerian market and improve its ability to identify potential irregularities in their importation and distribution,” it said.

The commission disclosed that it had engaged manufacturers, importers and relevant industry associations, urging businesses that required clarification to seek guidance through its approved onboarding and support channels.

It warned that, upon full implementation, devices that fail to meet applicable requirements may be restricted from accessing Nigerian mobile telecommunications networks in line with the approved enforcement framework.

The NCC said the initiative was intended to protect consumers and ensure that businesses complying with regulatory requirements were not disadvantaged by those that failed to meet their obligations.

Stakeholders seeking compliance guidance and onboarding assistance were advised to its website.

World.title: Subsidy Furore: Experts, opposition take on Oyedele over N4,000/$ crash claim
World.content:
Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister for the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele

*You’re paying fuel subsidy through back door, APM tells Tinubu *NDC kicks, asks why are our refineries not working? *Magnitude cannot be established by assertion alone – Prof Iledare *Minister must show assumptions, economic model underpinning projection — Egbomeade *You’re the Egypt Nigerians’ll never return to, Atiku tackles Tinubu

By Henry Umoru, Peter Egwuatu, Udeme Akpan & Luminous Jannamike

LAGOS — Some opposition parties and experts yesterday challenged the Minister of Finance, Taiwo Oyedele, to explain the assumptions he based his assertion that the Naira might crash to N4,000/$ should the Federal Government restore fuel subsidy.

The minister had in an interview on the sidelines of the just-concluded World Bank/IMF meetings in Bangkok, Thailand, said the local currency would crash to N4,000/$, if subsidy was restored.

Some opposition presidential candidates, including African Democratic Congress’ Atiku Abubakar; Social Democratic Party’s Adewole Adebayo; and Nigeria Democratic Party’s Peter Obi, had in the past few weeks, said they would restore fuel subsidy, if they were elected president to assuage the sufferings of the people.

Aside from Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, and Allied People’s Movement, APM, which disagreed with the finance minister’s assertion, experts, including petroleum experts, Prof. Wumi Iledare; and Economic and Communications expert, Clifford Egbomeade, also challenged him to explain the assumptions on which he based his assertions.

Reacting to the minister’s declaration, the APM accused President Bola Tinubu’s administration of paying fuel subsidy through the back door, questioning the recent petrol price reduction, despite government’s declaration that subsidy was gone.

The party also dismissed Oyedele’s warning that restoring subsidy could push the naira to N4,000 per dollar, describing the projection as unfounded and accusing the government of pursuing economic policies driving businesses into closure.

APM National Secretary, Ayodele Adebayo, who stated this in a response to Vanguard’s inquiries, faulted the administration’s handling of fuel prices and its claims about investors’ loss of confidence in opposition parties.

“What are they doing now with the current reduction in petrol price for one month? Is it not returning subsidy through the back door?” Adebayo queried.

He argued that the naira had previously exchanged at a stronger rate, rejecting the minister’s projection as an attempt to justify the government’s position on subsidy.

Adebayo also challenged Oyedele’s claims that investors had written off opposition parties as unserious, alleging that harsh economic policies had forced several companies to shut down.

“Where are even the investors the Minister of Finance, Taiwo Oyedele, is talking about? Is it the recycled ones by the present administration?” he queried.

The APM secretary said his party favoured an appropriate pricing framework for petroleum products to prevent further hardship, insisting that Nigerians should not be left with little money after paying for fuel.

“We cannot subscribe to seeing Nigerians use all their entitlements and earnings to buy fuel due to harsh economic policies,” Adebayo said.

NDC kicks, asks why are our refineries not working?

Similarly, the national leadership of the NDC slammed Oyedele for his statement, describing it as a subtle blackmail.

National Publicity Secretary of the NDC, Osa Director accused the All Progressives Congress, APC-led government of mortgaging a sizeable portion of Nigeria’s crude oil to take foreign loans “to the extent that we are unable to supply Dangote refinery the needed crude oil to satisfy domestic consumption and demand.”

Osa Director said: “The most important aspect of the subsidy conversation is not yet addressed. Why are our refineries not working? Why did the APC government mortgage a sizeable portion of our crude oil to take foreign loans, to the extent that we are unable to supply Dangote refinery the needed crude oil to satisfy domestic consumption and demand?

“If all these and the criminality in the subsidy regime are addressed, the doomsday prediction of the Minister of Finance would not be necessary.”

The ADC had taken a similar position in its reaction to the issue on Monday.

Magnitude cannot be established by assertion alone — Prof Iledare

Examing the minister’s statement in an interview with Vanguard yesterday, Petroleum Economist, Prof. Wumi Iledare, said: “The petrol subsidy debate should be guided by fiscal sustainability, market efficiency and measurable public welfare, not political rhetoric or unsupported forecasts.

“Restoring the subsidy would require the government to finance the gap between the regulated price and petrol’s economic cost. Depending on its scale and design, this could increase fiscal pressure, borrowing, foreign-exchange demand, import dependence, smuggling and arbitrage.

“However, the claim that subsidy restoration would push the naira to N4,000 per US dollar should be treated as a risk scenario, not an inevitable outcome.

‘’Finance Minister, Taiwo Oyedele, has linked such a possibility to capital flight and weaker investor confidence if reforms are reversed. These are plausible channels, but the specific exchange-rate projection requires evidence and clearly-stated assumptions.

“The naira is influenced by foreign-exchange supply and demand, crude-oil receipts, domestic production, capital flows, reserves, monetary policy and investor confidence. Subsidy restoration could add depreciation pressure, but its magnitude cannot be established by assertion alone.

“Subsidy removal, however, should not be judged only by its fiscal benefits. Higher petrol prices affect transport, food distribution, production costs and household welfare. Savings matter only when converted into productive investment, infrastructure, efficient public transport and targeted support for vulnerable households.

“Nigeria should, therefore, assess both options against affordability, fiscal sustainability, energy security and public value. Any restoration proposal should disclose its cost per litre, total fiscal exposure, funding source, beneficiaries, anti-leakage safeguards and exit strategy. ‘’If removal continues, the government must show how the savings are being used and what measurable welfare gains citizens receive.

“Nigeria needs neither cheap petrol at any cost nor expensive petrol in the name of reform. It needs competitive petroleum markets, efficient energy supply, transparent governance and targeted support.”

Minister must show assumptions, economic model underpinning projection — Egbomeade

Reacting in a similar manner, Clifford Egbomeade , Economics and Communications expert, said: “Rather than restore blanket fuel subsidies, the government should address the structural factors driving petrol prices, particularly exchange-rate volatility, domestic refining capacity and distribution costs.

‘’The government must also disclose how much subsidy removal has saved and how those savings have been spent, and the measurable economic benefits achieved.

“The minister’s N4,000/$ projection describes a possible risk, not an inevitable outcome. Subsidy restoration could widen the fiscal deficit, undermine investor confidence and increase foreign-exchange demand, particularly if fuel imports rise.

‘’However, the minister must show the assumptions and economic model underpinning the projection. The naira’s value also depends on oil revenues, foreign-exchange supply, capital flows and monetary policy.

‘’Policy-makers must evaluate subsidy restoration against its fiscal cost, impact on household purchasing power and implications for exchange-rate stability, rather than rely on political promises or forecasts not supported by evidence.”

This may not be an exaggeration – Adonri

However, David Adonri, an economist and Managing Director, HighCap Securities Limited, said: “The removal of subsidy on petrol has achieved several objectives for government. First, it ended the issuance of public debt to finance the consumption subsidy. It repaired the damaged balance sheet of NNPC which could not remit revenue to government while the subsidy lasted. As a result of savings from subsidy removal, the federation account has more distributable income which has restored the financial health of sub-nationals.

For the public sector in general, the policy has produced unimaginable financial turnaround and revived the integrity of the Petroleum industry. It has enabled domestic production to become competitive and viable.

‘’That without removal of fuel subsidy, the value of the Naira now would have crashed to N4,000/$ as expressed by the Minister of Finance. This may not be an exaggeration.

While the public sector has enjoyed all the benefits accruing from subsidy, unfortunately, it has left in its trail the worst cost of living crisis ever experienced by consumers in the country. ‘’This is because of the inability of the fiscal authorities to run an effective supply side policy to enhance agriculture and mining due to rural insecurity, close the expanding housing deficit and drive the use of alternative sources of energy such as solar and CNG.

You’re the Egypt Nigerians’ll never return to, Atiku tackles Tinubu

On President Bola Tinubu’s declaration that Nigeria would not return to Egypt, following calls by the opposition for fuel subsidy to be restored, presidential candidate of African Democratic Congress, ADC, Atiku Abubakar, said the statement exposed “how little he (President) understands the suffering of Nigerians”.

In a statement issued on his behalf by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Atiku said Tinubu boasted of removing the subsidy on his first day in office “like a wicked king recounting the suffering he had inflicted as a triumph.”

He said: “Bola, you are the Egypt Nigerians are desperate to escape. You celebrate the day you made fuel more expensive, then lecture families struggling to pay for food and transport about why they must never go back.”

“At least, Pharaoh knew he was holding people captive. Tinubu watches families cut meals, workers spend their salaries on transport and businesses struggle to keep their lights on, then tells them a story about Moses.

‘’He may quote scripture, but he governs like Pharaoh, Herod and Ahab combined: deaf to the cries of the people, proud of the hardship he has imposed and convinced that power excuses him from answering for it.

“Bola, a mother trying to feed her children cannot pay for food with a metaphor. A worker cannot get to work on a story about the Red Sea. Nigerians are asking how you intend to make life affordable. Answer them.

“I will make life affordable again through practical relief Nigerians can feel. My proposal is clear: give limited, budgeted support only to verified petroleum products refined in Nigeria and sold to Nigerians.

‘’Imported fuel gets nothing. Independent auditors must track every naira, and the benefit must reach consumers in the price they pay. If it does not lower that price, it has failed its purpose.

“But hardship is not the only captivity Nigerians face. Tinubu’s failure on security cannot be buried under Buhari’s record. He asked Nigerians for the presidency knowing that communities were under attack, families were paying ransom and children were afraid to travel to school.

‘’He took the oath to protect them. Yet his own campaign Director-General asks, ‘What do you expect Tinubu to do when even Buhari, a general, could not wipe out insecurity?’ Let me remind them that President Yar’Adua was not a sergeant, yet he stamped it out.

“Nigerians expect their President to confront the killers, rescue the abducted and make it possible to travel, farm, work and sleep without fear. If Tinubu cannot tell them how he will do that after more than three years in office, he has no business asking for four more years.

‘’The lives lost under his watch are not an argument about his predecessor. They are an indictment of his own leadership. And look at what Tinubu asks of the officers sent to protect us.

‘’A retired Assistant Superintendent told me he receives ₦29,000 a month. Serving officers are drawing down their pension savings to feed their families. How can a President demand courage from police officers in the field while leaving them worried about food at home and destitution in retirement?

“Bola, answer the retired officers asking for a pension they can live on. Act on the Police Exit Bill and review serving officers’ salaries, as was done for members of the Armed Forces. Give the people who protect Nigerians the pay, healthcare and retirement security their service has earned.

“Stop pointing to Egypt as though it lies behind us. For millions of Nigerians, Egypt is the hunger, fear and indignity they are living through under you. They deserve affordable fuel, safe communities and police officers who can serve without sacrificing their families’ future. Tinubu made life expensive. I will make life affordable again.”

World.title: Currency in circulation rises 81% to N5.4trn
World.content:
By Peter Egwuatu

Currency in circulation in Nigeria rose by 81 per cent to N5.44 trillion in August 2026, from N3.01 trillion in August 2023, underscoring the continued strong demand for physical cash despite the rapid expansion of electronic payments over the past three years.

Data from the Central Bank of Nigeria’s, CBN, Money and Credit Statistics show that the strongest increase occurred between August 2023 and August 2024 when currency in circulation rose from N3.010 trillion in August 2023 to N4.55 trillion in August 2024, representing an increase of N1.54 trillion or 51.1 per cent.

The growth moderated considerably in the following years. In August 2025, currency in circulation increased to N5.057 trillion, up N508 billion or 11.2 per cent from the previous year.

By August 2026, the growth rate moderated further though it hit new threshold of N5.436 trillion, an increase of N379 billion or 7.5 per cent Year-on-Year, YoY.

The figures therefore indicate that while the amount of physical cash in circulation has continued to rise, the pace of growth has slowed significantly, from 51.1 per cent in 2024 to 11.2 per cent in 2025 and 7.5 per cent in 2026.

Banks’ reserves

The increase in currency in circulation occurred alongside a substantial rise in banks’ reserves. According to the data supplied, banks’ reserves rose from N18.528 trillion in August 2023 to N25.456 trillion in August 2024, an increase of N6.928 trillion or 37.4 per cent.

They increased further to N31.583 trillion in August 2025, before reaching N36.067 trillion in August 2026. Overall, banks’ reserves increased by N17.539 trillion, or 94.7 per cent, between August 2023 and August 2026. The CBN’s monetary statistics identify currency in circulation and banks’ reserves as components of reserve money or base money.

Commenting on the development, David Adonri, Managing Director, High Cap Securities Limited, said: “When more money is held as physical cash, a portion of liquidity is outside the immediate deposit base of commercial banks and is therefore less available for banks to intermediate through loans and other financial assets.

However, the rising currency stock should not automatically be interpreted as evidence of excessive liquidity or inflationary pressure. Demand for cash can also increase because of higher nominal prices, larger transaction values and the expansion of economic activity.

The increase is particularly noteworthy because Nigeria has experienced rapid growth in electronic payments, mobile banking, fintech services and instant-payment platforms.

The continued expansion of physical currency therefore suggests that Nigeria’s digital-payment revolution has not eliminated the country’s cash economy.”

World.title: Defection of some candidates to APC good riddance to bad rubbish — NDC
World.content:
By Henry Umoru

ABUJA – THE national leadership of Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, has described the defection of some of its members to the All Progressives Congress, APC, as good riddance to bad rubbish.

In a statement yesterday by the National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, the alleged that some of its candidates had been bribed by APC to defect to the ruling party.

According to Director, the NDC is fully aware of what he described as the desperate and malicious tactics of the APC, which has resorted to offering money, political appointments and other material incentives to induce some money-minded candidates of the party to jump ship and defect to its sinking fold.

The statement read: “It has come to the attention of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, that some candidates of our party have been bribed by the APC to defect to the ruling and ruinous All Progressives Congress, APC, obviously for pecuniary reasons.

“The NDC is fully aware of the desperate and malicious tactics of the APC, which has resorted to offering money, political appointments, and other material incentives to induce some money minded candidates of our party to jump ship and defect to its sinking fold.

“For those who have fallen for this bait, it is clear that they lack the values, virtues, and ideological commitment associated with our great party.

“They were never truly of us. To them, we say good riddance to bad rubbish, and we wish them luck in their political misadventures.

“In line with the provisions of the Electoral Act, 2026, the party will immediately conduct fresh congresses to elect credible, competent and trustworthy candidates to replace the defectors in the affected constituency.”

“We wish to reassure our teeming party members, supporters, and well-meaning Nigerians not to be perturbed by the antics of the ruling party in bribing a few of our members. These are the last kicks of a dying horse that has seen the handwriting on the wall of its imminent defeat.

“NDC remains resolutely committed to its historic mission of rescuing our country from the vice grip of the buccaneers in power and give Nigerians the good governance, security and prosperity they so richly desire. A New Nigeria is POssible. We can do it!”

World.title: FG confirms Ebola case in FCT, begins contact tracing
World.content:
By Chidinma Chukwu, Abuja

The Federal Government has reportedly commenced contact tracing after a suspected imported case of Ebola disease was identified in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), with 44 close contacts said to have been identified.

The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Muhammad Ali Pate, was quoted as disclosing this in a statement signed by the ministry’s Assistant Director of Information and Public Relations, Ado Bako, following the reported laboratory confirmation on Tuesday, October 20, 2026.

According to the statement, the patient is a woman who recently arrived in Nigeria on an international flight from Uganda.

The woman was reportedly admitted to a private hospital in the FCT, where she received treatment for several days before the diagnosis was confirmed. She is said to be in isolation and receiving medical care.

Pate said the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC), the FCT Health Services Secretariat and other relevant authorities were working together to contain the reported infection.

He said contact tracing had commenced, with public health teams identifying and monitoring people who might have been exposed to the virus.

Those being monitored reportedly include healthcare workers, patients, caregivers and people who may have come into contact with the patient during her travels.

The statement also said surveillance had been intensified, while the hospital where the patient was treated was receiving support to strengthen infection prevention and control measures.

The minister urged people contacted during the tracing exercise, including relevant airline passengers, to provide the necessary information and comply with public health advice.

He also called on public and private healthcare facilities nationwide to remain vigilant and promptly report suspected cases to public health authorities.

Healthcare workers were advised to maintain a high index of suspicion, identify and isolate suspected cases without delay, and observe strict infection prevention and control measures.

The government urged Nigerians to remain calm and vigilant, practise regular hand hygiene and avoid contact with the body fluids of anyone suspected of having Ebola.

Symptoms to watch for include fever, severe weakness, headache, vomiting and diarrhoea, particularly among people who may have been exposed to the virus.

Pate advised anyone who suspected exposure to contact public health authorities immediately, even if they had no symptoms.

He also urged anyone who developed symptoms to avoid close contact with others and call public health authorities for guidance before visiting a healthcare facility.

The minister warned against spreading rumours or stigmatising people who might have been exposed, urging Nigerians to rely on verified information from official health authorities.

He said the Federal Government, FCT authorities and their partners were working to protect healthcare workers, patients and the wider public, adding that investigations were ongoing.

The statement said the NCDC’s toll-free call centre was available 24 hours a day, seven days a week, to provide information and receive reports of suspected cases. Members of the public were advised to call 6232 for assistance.
