World.title: ‘What did she do’? Fans speculate why Tracy Hlophe MUST apologise
Kearsney College mourns former top student’s tragic death
World.content:
Kearsney College is mourning the death of one of their star past pupils. Images via FB

Kearsney College is mourning the death of one of their Old Boys, Ndabenhle Shazi, who died in a car accident last week.

The star actor and performer passed just two days before his 33rd birthday.

The KwaZulu-Natal all-boys private school is South Africa’s Top 5 expensive schools.



KEARSNEY COLLEGE MOURNS ACTOR AND ARTIST ALUMNUS

On their social media platforms, Kearsney College shared the tragic news of the passing of their former top student, Ndabenhle Shazi.

They shared: “With deep sadness, we announce the tragic death of a shining Kearsney star and one of our dear brothers. Shazi, also known to family and older friends as Boyo, died in a car accident on the afternoon of Monday, 14 October 2026, near Ermelo. He was laid to rest at the family’s homestead on Saturday.

Affectionately known as “Shazi”, the 2012 matriculant was a distinguished drama student and musical artist who was involved in the school choir and theatre productions that were performed around the world.

This included an international tour to Asia in 2010 and to the World Choir Olympics in Cincinnati, USA, 2012, where the Kearsney College choir won 3 gold medals.

“Shazi made us laugh, cheer, sing and smile over many years. His laugh and personality brought joy to so many. With a heart of gold, he loved his Kearsney brothers and, being based in KZN, often popped in to visit staff members he respected and cared for.

“Shazi, you will always be a Kearsney legend and loved by many around the world. Rest in Peace, ” added the post.



CELEBRATED MUSIC AND DRAMA STUDENT

During his tenure at Kearsney College, Shazi served as chairman of the dance and drama club, head of choreography, and soloist in the school choir. He was also co-head of the Pembroke Inter-House Plays.

During his matric year, he received his colours and honours in music and dramatic arts.

After matriculating, he pursued his love of the performing arts through his entertainment company, SM ENT, where he continued to produce music and DJ under his artist name, Shazi Mayne.

He also graduated with a BCom in Supply Chain Management from the University of Pretoria.

World.title: Wednesday’s coastal tides: What beachgoers and anglers should know
World.content:
Beachgoers, surfers and anglers can check Wednesday’s high and low tide times before planning activities along South Africa’s coastline. Image: Unsplash

If you’re heading to the coast on Tuesday, check the tide times before planning your activities.

Water levels change throughout the day, while wind, waves, swell and the shape of the seabed also affect conditions along the shore and at sea.

When to expect the next spring tide

Spring tides are important to watch out for because they bring higher high tides and lower low tides than usual.



The next spring tide is expected around the full moon on Monday, 26 October 2026.

These changes can affect swimming, surfing and fishing. High tides may cover rocks and reefs, while low tides expose more of the shoreline.

Check the tide times and the latest weather and marine warnings before you head to the coast.

World.title: Tso uses Max Verstappen analogy to explain Kaizer Chiefs’ struggles
World.content:
Former Orlando Pirates midfielder Benedict Vilakazi believes Fernando Da Cruz’s time as Kaizer Chiefs coach could be short-lived, arguing that the club’s struggles go beyond the technical team.

Vilakazi, popularly known as Tso, believes Amakhosi lack the quality of players needed to compete for major trophies and fears the club could once again turn to a foreign coach if Da Cruz is dismissed.

Speaking to iDiski Times, the former midfielder predicted that Chiefs would look overseas for another coach rather than appoint a local tactician.



“He will leave and again, they will still go overseas to get a new coach,” he said.

Vilakazi also questioned why Chiefs did not consider local coaches such as Rulani Mokwena and Pitso Mosimane when they were available, pointing to their achievements at Mamelodi Sundowns.

“I don’t think Kaizer Chiefs will consider a local coach. When Rulani Mokwena and Pitso Mosimane were unattached, that was a perfect opportunity for them to say, ‘If we want to bring back glory days, here are people who showed at Sundowns that they are winners’. It didn’t happen,” he said.

However, Vilakazi believes changing coaches alone will not solve Amakhosi’s problems, insisting that the club must improve the quality of players at its disposal.

He argued that even an elite coach would struggle to deliver results without the right squad, using a car analogy to illustrate his point.

“Even if they bring in the best coach like Jose Mourinho, you still driving the same car. You can’t beat a Maserati driving a Toyota Tazz. You can put Max Verstappen in a Tazz and I’ll drive a Mercedes and I’ll be faster than him; that’s how it is,” he said.



Kaizer Chiefs told to get quality players

Vilakazi added that the quality of the squad ultimately determines what a coach can achieve, regardless of their reputation or experience.

“So whoever you put in the team, with the same material, he won’t get results for Kaizer Chiefs,” he concluded.

Do you agree with Tso?

World.title: Media houses challenge bid for closed-door evidence at Madlanga Commission
World.content:
PRETORIA - Three media houses are opposing an application by the National Intelligence Co-ordinating Committee (NICOC) for evidence to be heard in-camera at the Madlanga Commission.

NICOC is responsible for co-ordinating strategic intelligence from various intelligence structures.

Its acting coordinator, Ntandaza Sifolo, has applied for his evidence to be heard in-camera. The Commission will consider the application on Wednesday.

The application will be heard in an open session in Pretoria on Wednesday.

World.title: Unions, unemployed groups to protest Godongwana's mini-budget
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - The South African Federation of Trade Unions (SAFTU), the Association of Mineworkers and Construction Union (AMCU) and the Assembly of the Unemployed will protest against the government’s austerity measures on Wednesday.

Marching under the Cry of the Xcluded banner, the groups plan to lead thousands of workers to the National Treasury as Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana delivers the Medium-Term Budget Policy Statement in Parliament.

The movement is calling on the government to increase spending on healthcare, education, housing and service delivery.

World.title: All eyes on Godongwana as he delivers mini-budget
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana is set to deliver the Mid-Term Budget Policy Statement on Wednesday afternoon.

Also known as the mini-budget, it comes as the country navigates a tough economic period driven by the Middle East War.

It's adding to the pressure of an economy failing to create jobs, record-high fuel prices, and a constantly rising cost of living.

These are some of the issues the Minister will have to consider as opposition and economists watch closely.

Godongwana will deliver the budget at 2pm in Parliament.

World.title: Asian stocks rally as tech firms enjoy bounce ahead of key earnings
World.content:
HONG KONG - Asian markets rallied on Wednesday as tech firms enjoyed a much-needed rebound, with investors taking heart from upbeat earnings that lifted sentiment ahead of a crucial reporting season.

Seoul and Tokyo were the headliners again as chipmakers and other key players in the AI buildout boom chalked up healthy gains, following a torrid few weeks fuelled by concerns about profitability and debt financing.

South Korea's SK hynix and Samsung both surged at least seven percent, while Kioxia, Advantest and SoftBank spiked between two and four percent in Japan -- having all been pummelled since the start of last week.

The gains came after Elon Musk's SpaceX reported its first quarterly profit as a public company, as deals to rent out computing power to AI firms sent revenue at its artificial intelligence unit soaring.

Server-maker Super Micro Computer also provided a fillip to buying sentiment as it said preliminary quarterly earnings had come in better than forecast.

The developments soothed worries on trading floors about the outlook for the AI boom, which has seen companies pump hundreds of billions into R&D, software building data centres and other hardware in recent years.

It also bodes well ahead of reports from Magnificent Seven members Tesla and Meta later in the day.

Seoul's Kospi jumped more than four percent, with infrastructure firm Elice soaring around 30 percent, almost wiping out the colossal losses suffered on its trading debut Tuesday.

Tokyo added more than one percent, while Hong Kong, Singapore, Wellington, Manila and Jakarta were also up.

There were losses in Sydney, where data centre developer NEXTDC tanked more than 40 percent after slashing its outlook and renewing its capital expenditure programme.

The broad gains followed a healthy day on Wall Street, though analysts said a lot of the gains were spurred by traders rotating into industrial firms and away from the once-all-powerful tech sector. The Dow ended up one percent and the Nasdaq was marginally lower.

Oil prices jumped more than one percent on supply concerns as the UKMTO maritime agency said on Wednesday that a tanker sailing off the north coast of Qatar had reported being struck "by multiple projectiles", causing an unspecified number of casualties.

World.title: Christina Applegate says she was misdiagnosed with MS
World.content:
LOS ANGELES - Christina Applegate on Tuesday said she had been misdiagnosed with multiple sclerosis, which doctors had attributed her symptoms to since 2021.

The Emmy-nominated actor, who first gained fame in the late 1980s for her role in the sitcom "Married... with Children," said she continues to suffer debilitating symptoms and that learning of her misdiagnosis has only left her "back at square one."

Applegate discussed the ordeal on the latest episode of her podcast, "MeSsy."

"You don't get misdiagnosed and then all of a sudden I'm better," she told her co-host Jamie-Lynn Sigler of "Sopranos" fame, who herself has lived with multiple sclerosis for more than two decades.

Sigler had been hosting the podcast solo for months while Applegate dealt with health issues, including a lengthy hospital stay.

MS is an autoimmune neurodegenerative disease that affects nearly three million people worldwide and can be difficult to diagnose, leading to misdiagnoses in a fifth of cases, according to the Cleveland Clinic.

Applegate had previously described dealing with difficulty walking and balance problems, as well as a lack of coordination and numbness in her extremities.

But she said the diagnosis had provided some clarity and a path forward, whereas having no explanation for her symptoms left her once again searching.

"It's hard to say, but she came into my room and she said,'Congratulations, you don't have MS.'" Applegate said. "I was like, not happy at all. Everybody else was so happy."

"I still have to use wheelchairs when I go to the doctor's office. I can't walk from the car to the room. I'm still in this."

World.title: Ronaldo let Man Utd down says Ten Hag
World.content:
LONDON - Former Manchester United manager Erik ten Hag has accused Cristiano Ronaldo of letting the team down during his time in charge.

Portugal star Ronaldo was in his second spell at United when Ten Hag was hired in 2022.

Ten Hag's relationship with Ronaldo quickly became tense, and the striker refused to come on as a substitute in a win over Tottenham in October 2022.

Ronaldo was dropped for a subsequent match against Chelsea, prompting him to give an explosive television interview in which he said he felt betrayed by United and did not respect Ten Hag.

The former Real Madrid forward's contract at United was mutually terminated the following month.

"He let the team down, and he let me down, because we planned with him," Ten Hag said in an interview with The Athletic.

"Obviously, he's one of the best in football history. I respected him a lot. But at that time, as a manager, I had to make a rational decision and keep the players I admire in."

Ten Hag said Ronaldo pulled out of training sessions and did not complete the full run that players were set after they were beaten 4-0 by Brentford early in his reign.

"I confronted him with this. Many times I say, 'Ronnie, everyone wants to work for you to bring you in the right position, but if you can't bring yourself in the box, you can't score'. He was not capable to do this," Ten Hag said.

"It's the wrong idea to put this to me that I expected him to do the pressing, that he's exhausted. But he couldn't.

"He ran neither in possession nor out of possession. The reason was because he didn't prepare himself."

Ten Hag also claimed promises made by United's owners went unfulfilled before he was sacked in 2024, shortly after signing a new contract.

Although United won the FA Cup just months earlier with a surprise final victory against Manchester City, Ten Hag was axed with the team languishing in 14th place in the Premier League.

The Dutchman blamed the United hierarchy of some of his problems, saying he was left humiliated when Scotland midfielder Scott McTominay was sold to Napoli without his consent.

Ten Hag also said he wanted to sign Harry Kane, Declan Rice and Frenkie de Jong during his spell at United.

"They promised me loyalty, they promised me backing, they promised communication, that we get aligned. We spoke about the issues. But the promises, they didn't keep," he said.

"I said, 'No selling Scott McTominay'. And in the end they sold him. I got, of course, very embarrassed and disappointed."

World.title: Alberta separatists vow to fight on, risking turmoil for Canada
World.content:
MONTREAL - Separatists in Canada's Alberta province say their independence fight is not over despite a decisive referendum loss, risking long-term political turmoil in an oil-rich province crucial to the Canadian economy.

The western province chose overwhelmingly on Monday to remain a part of Canada, with 75.5 percent of voters rejecting a plan to move forward with a binding independence referendum.

As he entered parliament on Tuesday, Prime Minister Mark Carney said he was "thrilled that Albertans have chosen unity."

Asked what message he'd like to deliver to the separatist side, Carney, who grew up in Alberta, said: "The result is absolutely clear. It's a large majority for Canada and now is the time to work together."

But separatist leaders projected a starkly different message after the results came in.

Jeffrey Rath, a top official with the Alberta Prosperity Project who met with US officials earlier this year to discuss support for the secession project, said the fight would "absolutely" continue.

"We've created a massive movement in this province," he said. "We're continuing to move forward."

Rath told reporters it was impossible to win an independence referendum while Alberta is led by someone who supports Canadian unity.

He vowed to challenge Premier Danielle Smith, who aligned with Carney, and "to take control back" of Alberta's conservative movement.

"We will form a government, period," he said.

World.title: Zelensky, US hail 'productive' talks to end Trump feud
World.content:
OSLO - Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and the United States hailed "very productive" talks in Oslo on Tuesday amid efforts to draw a line under a bitter feud between Kyiv's leader and US President Donald Trump over the war with Russia.

After talks with Trump's envoys in the Norwegian capital, Zelensky thanked Washington for the resumption of US intelligence of looming Russian strikes on civilian targets and energy plants.

Trump's special envoy Steve Witkoff is now due to head from Oslo to Russia for talks with President Vladimir Putin on Wednesday in a bid to end Russia's four-year-old war on Ukraine.

The positive tone followed days of tensions between Kyiv and Washington since Trump struck a diesel-supply deal with Putin, and furiously called for Zelensky to be replaced after Ukraine refused to stop hitting Russian oil refineries.

"We are thankful that intelligence works," Zelensky told reporters in Oslo. "I'm speaking about early warning, what is very important for our people, for children, adults, civilians, because we can hear when ballistic is coming."

Flanked by Norway's Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store and Finnish President Alexander Stubb -- a golfing buddy of Trump -- Zelensky said it was "important that we keep the conversation going."

A US official told AFP after the talks that Zelensky held "very productive and constructive discussions" with businessman Witkoff and Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner, who took part remotely due to the flu.

"Ukraine brought forward new ideas and proposals," the official said.

World.title: 2027 hots up as Gachagua-Sifuna plot alliance against Ruto
World.content:
DCP leader Rigathi Gachagua hosts Edwin Sifuna and Linda Mwananchi leaders at his Wamunyoro residence on October 20, 2026. [Kibata Kihu, Standard]

Former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua returned quietly from the United States but hours later generated political shockwaves by hosting Linda Mwananchi leaders led by Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna at his Wamunyoro home in Nyeri.

Sources who attended the one-hour-long meeting disclosed that the leaders discussed a possible alliance between the DCP and Linda Mwananchi ahead of next year’s General Election, an agreement on Nairobi leadership, and strategies to lock out President William Ruto in Western and Mt Kenya regions.

World.title: Judge certifies fresh bid to jail Sakaja, Charles Kerich over Sh76.7m debt as urgent
World.content:
Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja. [File, Standard]

The High Court has certified as urgent a fresh application seeking to have Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja, former Finance Executive Charles Kerich and two other county officials jailed over an alleged breach of a court-approved payment plan in a Sh106.7 million legal fees dispute.

Justice Francis Gikonyo certified the application by Kwengu & Company Advocates seeking to reinstate a three-month jail sentence previously imposed on Kerich and hold Sakaja, current Finance County Executive Committee Member Ibrahim Auma Nyangoya and Chief Officer for Finance Asha Abdi accountable for the alleged failure to pay Sh76.7 million.

World.title: Kenya confirms third Ebola case
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kenya has confirmed a third case of Ebola involving a 65-year-old woman who is a close relative of the first two patients.

The Ministry of Health, in a statement, said the woman developed a fever, sore throat and malaise while in quarantine, prompting her isolation and testing.

Her samples tested positive for Ebola at both the National Virology Reference Laboratory and the Kenya Medical Research Institute (KEMRI).

According to the Health Director-General Patrick Amoth, the patient has been transferred to an infectious disease unit, where she is receiving supportive care and being monitored.

“Having been in quarantine, she was diagnosed early and is currently receiving supportive care, improving her chances of recovery while limiting the risk of further spread of the disease,” the statement read.

The second patient, on the other hand, is in stable condition and responding well to supportive care.

The latest case brings the number of confirmed Ebola infections in Kenya to three.

According to the Ministry, of the 130 contacts identified so far, 127 had been traced and placed in quarantine, with efforts ongoing to trace the remaining three.

World.title: Motorists, households face fresh fuel price hikes
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

EPRA attributed the price increases to the escalating conflict in the Middle East. [FIle, Standard]

The Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority (EPRA) has increased fuel prices, raising the cost of super petrol by Sh12.93 per litre, diesel by Sh9.90, and kerosene by Sh28.49.

The new prices, effective from October 15 to November 14, 2026, will see motorists in Nairobi pay up to Sh226.96 per litre for super petrol, Sh227.76 for diesel, and Sh219.85 for kerosene.

EPRA Director-General Edward Mwirigi Kinyua attributed the price increases to the escalating conflict in the Middle East, which has disrupted petroleum supply chains and driven up the cost of importing fuel.

The rise in kerosene prices is likely to hit low-income households that rely on the fuel for cooking and lighting.

Meanwhile, higher diesel prices could raise the cost of transporting goods and operating public service vehicles, potentially driving up fares and commodity prices.

Diesel is a key fuel for the country's freight transport sector and a significant portion of public service vehicle operations, meaning the increase could have a ripple effect across the economy.

The latest review comes after EPRA maintained pump prices during the September 15 to October 14 pricing period, despite a decline in the cost of importing petrol.

World.title: Oburu Oginga to leave hospital soon - ODM
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

ODM SG Catherine Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician.

ODM Secretary General Catherine Omanyo has dismissed social media reports about the health of party leader Oburu Oginga, saying he is recovering well and is expected to be discharged from hospital either today or tomorrow.

Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician, accusing them of exploiting his health condition to attract online attention and increase engagement.

“It's unfortunate what I've been reading on social media. Those people who are seeking to have more likes or viewers, they will be disappointed because he's up, he's well, he's fine. In fact, he's headed home either today or tomorrow,” she said.

Omanyo insisted that the reports had exaggerated his situation, dismissing claims of his death and assuring the public that he was doing well.

She noted that health conditions could fluctuate, saying Oburu's position as ODM party leader had made his well-being a subject of heightened public interest.

“Everybody, everybody, including you and me, our health is not static. You can be under the weather any time. It's just that he's a party leader, and it makes breaking news,” Omanyo said.

She urged social media users to exercise restraint when discussing the health of public figures, warning against spreading unverified reports, particularly claims of death, before confirmation from credible sources.

Her remarks come amid growing speculation on social media about Oburu's health, with some users circulating unverified claims about his condition.

World.title: Kenya declares Ebola a formidable epidemic disease, sets new rules
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale, who declared Ebola caused by the Bundibugyo virus a formidable epidemic disease under the Public Health Act. [File,Standard]

Kenya has declared Ebola virus a formidable epidemic disease, introducing new rules governing screening, isolation, quarantine, contact tracing and the handling of bodies.

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale issued the declaration through a legal notice published in the Kenya Gazette on Monday, October 12, under Section 35 of the Public Health Act.

The declaration follows Kenya’s confirmation of its first imported case of Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease on October 6, after a Kenyan citizen who had been living in the Democratic Republic of Congo travelled through Uganda to Nairobi. The patient died despite receiving supportive treatment.

The case prompted health authorities to trace people who may have come into contact with the patient and strengthen screening at points of entry.

In an update on October 12, the World Health Organization (WHO) said Kenya had listed 127 contacts, with 94 in quarantine, and screened more than 665,000 travellers at points of entry.

WHO also supplied protective equipment and testing materials worth about US$70,000 to support the response.

The government published two legal notices on October 12. Legal Notice No. 203 declares the disease a formidable epidemic, while Legal Notice No. 204 establishes the Public Health (Ebola Disease) Rules, 2026.

The regulations provide for screening at points of entry, medical assessment, isolation, referral, quarantine and monitoring.

They also assign responsibilities to transport operators, health facilities, medical practitioners and laboratories.

Health authorities will conduct investigations and contact tracing, while designated health facilities will manage suspected and confirmed cases. The rules also provide for the inspection and decontamination of premises.

The regulations cover the safe and dignified disposal of bodies, burial procedures, record-keeping, transportation and repatriation. They also address public communication, media houses’ responsibilities in public sensitisation and assistance from enforcement agencies.

The rules provide for offences and penalties, although the Gazette extract does not specify the penalties for individual violations.

What the declaration means

Bundibugyo virus disease is a form of Ebola that spreads through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of an infected person or contaminated materials.

Contact with the body of someone who has died from the disease can also expose people to infection during unsafe burial practices.

Symptoms can include fever, fatigue, muscle pain, headache and sore throat, followed by vomiting and diarrhoea. The incubation period ranges from two to 21 days.

WHO says no approved vaccine or specific treatment currently exists for the Bundibugyo strain, making early detection, isolation, supportive care and contact tracing central to controlling its spread.

The health agency has advised against travel or trade restrictions on Kenya, Uganda and the Democratic Republic of Congo based on the information available.

The new rules establish a legal framework for managing the disease, from identifying suspected infections and monitoring contacts to caring for patients and preventing exposure during burials.
