World.title: Albanian police clash with anti-government protesters for eighth day
World.content:
Police fired tear gas and used water cannons to push back protesters, on the eighth straight day of violent anti-government demonstrations in the Albanian capital, Tirana, on Tuesday (October 20, 2026).

High school and university students demanding lower tuition fees, greater State investment in education, and protesting corruption in the education system, have joined a broader anti-government movement calling for the resignation of Socialist Prime Minister Edi Rama. For days, protesters have hurled rocks, flares, firebombs and fireworks at the police, who have used batons, water cannons and tear gas in clashes in the city centre.

Albania is one of several European countries experiencing protests over rising fuel costs, discontent with the state of schools, declining public services and a housing crisis, including France and Italy. In Spain and Portugal, tent camps have sprung up to protest unaffordable housing, while a rally and a protest were also being planned in Greece on Tuesday (October 20) evening and Wednesday (October 21, 2026).

In Albania, the latest protests follow months of rallies organised by the so-called Flamingo movement, launched in opposition to a major luxury tourism development on Albania’s southern coast, linked to an investment firm founded by Jared Kushner, U.S. President Donald Trump’s son-in-law.

“A wave of stones, an attempt to overthrow the government and change those in power through the imposition of violence — something that will never be allowed to happen, in any form or for any reason,” Mr. Rama said, after a meeting on Tuesday with teachers and representatives of Tirana’s schools.

He argued that legitimate concerns were being hijacked by people deliberately causing violence during the protests. “This is a hybrid war that naturally works to the extent that it does because it is based on real concerns, not fantasies. Concerns about the cost of living are certainly real. Concerns about a secure future, housing, and greater opportunities to get ahead are also real,” he said.

Mr. Rama accused protesters of “holding the city under a climate of terror,” and said students involved in the protests “belong to emerging currents of political extremism.”

World.title: Canadian unity or separation: why did Alberta province hold a referendum?
World.content:
The story so far: Majority of citizens of the Canadian province Alberta, in a referendum on Monday (October 19, 2026), chose to push down a rising separatist movement, giving Prime Minister Mark Carney a much-needed relief and boost amid tension with neighbouring U.S. over trade policies and President Donald Trump’s provocative ambitions. While official results of the non-binding referendum are to be announced on October 29, the vote, with more than 90% of votes counted by Wednesday (October 21) morning, has given an overwhelming support for the oil-rich province to stay with the country.

Why is the province feeling separatist sentiments?

Alberta, with its abundant ‘oil sands’, is home to the world’s fourth-largest proven oil reserves, behind Venezuela, Saudi Arabia, and Iran. While neither the largest nor the most populous province in the North American country, Alberta accounts for more than 80% of Canada’s crude oil production and contributes a disproportionate share to the country’s economy among the provinces. This has long kept separatist sentiments alive along the fringes of the province’s social fabric, with some believing that the province is not getting the same from federal government as it is providing.

The environmental-friendly policies of liberal governments at the centre that aimed at putting curbs on oil extraction stoked the sentiments of the constituents of the conservationist province, which snowballed into a popular movement in recent years, helped along with resentment towards restrictions and regulations during the pandemic and post-pandemic period, including mandatory vaccinations. The MAGA movement under Mr. Trump on the other side of the border also inspired conservatives in the province, who rallied towards secession and autonomy which would let Alberta decide what to do with the oil present in its territory, and collect and keep the income from oil for itself.

What did the latest referendum seek to settle?

The referendum was initially introduced as a pair of motions approved in March with 9 questions on immigration and welfare policies and constitutional questions on federal structure and inter-provincial cooperation. The 10th question, added to the 9 initial ones with a separate order approved in May, dealt with the separation. Instead of seeking yes or no answers like the previous 9 questions, the last question gave voters two options. “Should Alberta remain a province of Canada or should the Government of Alberta commence the legal process required under the Canadian Constitution to hold a binding provincial referendum on whether or not Alberta should separate from Canada”, the question asked.

Option one was that Alberta should remain a Province of Canada, while the second option called for the provincial government to commence legal process to hold a binding referendum on whether or not Alberta should separate from Canada. In essence, the referendum wanted citizens of the province to either close the door on separation talks or urge the government to initiate a second referendum to decide on separation. With results from more than 90% of the voting centres in, 14,67,256 people out of a total of 19,51,821, more than 75%, voters chose option one.

How do the federal and provincial administrations perceive the vote?

Prime Minister Carney, who hails from Alberta, has always spoken against the separatist movement, urging Albertans in the run up to the vote to choose unity. The votes against any separation referendum was a “large majority for Canada”, Mr. Carney said on Tuesday (October 20) evening after telling parliament that he was “thrilled that Albertans have chosen unity”. The result is absolutely clear... now is the time to work together,” Mr. Carney said.

Alberta Premier, Danielle Smith, who called for the vote in a sign of growing pressures from within her United Conservative Party but stated that she will vote for unity and urged others to do the same before the referendum and reacting to the early results as a vote for a “stronger Alberta in a united Canada”.

What will become of the secession movement?

However, separatist leaders have not given up. “We are not going anywhere”, Jeff Rath, leader of the Alberta Prosperity Project and one of the faces of the separatist movement, said after the referendum results became apparent. “We have dominated the conversation in the last year. We have been educating Albertans on the benefits of independence, and we are going to continue moving forward. While his movement faced an overwhelming barrier in the referendum, Mr. Rath sees a silver lining in the 30% votes for his cause. Former Premier Jason Kennedy had pointed out before the referendum that separatist parties traditionally attracted less than 2% of votes in elections and referendums. The 30% vote on Monday (October 19) is an exponential growth for the movement and could be the way to the mainstream for Mr. Rath and his ideas, one of which is replacing Ms. Smith as the head of the UCP and getting a pro-separatist government for the province which take forward.

But with global uncertainties and trade wars with the U.S. under Mr. Trump who had demeaned Canada’s sovereignty multiple times with public comments about making the country a 51st State of the U.S., Prime Minister Carney needs his country united and resources flowing. Mr. Carney would also find strength from the fact that leaders of the separatist movement had had public meetings with U.S. lawmakers in the run up to the referendum and yet he had the overwhelming solidarity from his home province. The support from the referendum will boost his ambitions to get a major pipeline out of Alberta that he hopes could revive the economy. As an economist who was in charge of the Bank of England during Brexit, not having to go through the economic fallout from the separation of one of the most profitable provinces in the country would be a relief.

World.title: Special officers to administer rural local bodies in 37 districts till April 2027 in T.N.
World.content:
The Tamil Nadu government has extended the tenure of special officers administering rural local bodies in 28 districts by another six months, till April 19, 2027. It has also appointed special officers to administer rural local bodies in nine other districts until the same date.

The Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Department issued a government order to this effect. The tenure of elected representatives of rural local bodies in 28 districts ended on January 5, 2025. The State government subsequently appointed special officers to administer village panchayats, panchayat union councils and district panchayats in these districts from January 6, 2025, for six months.

Since then, the tenure of the special officers has been extended every six months in these 28 districts and the Tamil Nadu Panchayats Act, 1994, was amended accordingly.

Similarly, the tenure of elected representatives of rural local bodies in nine districts such as Kancheepuram, Chengalpattu, Villupuram, Kallakurichi, Vellore, Ranipet, Tirupattur, Tirunelveli and Tenkasi ended on October 19, 2026.

In a letter to the government, the Commissioner of Rural Development and Panchayat Raj had said that it would not be possible to conduct elections to rural local bodies in all 37 districts before October 19, 2026.

This was because the process of merging 46 rural local bodies with urban local bodies was being finalised. The notification of expanded urban local bodies would also alter the boundaries of village panchayats, panchayat union councils and district panchayats.

The Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Department subsequently issued final notifications for nine newly-formed panchayat unions, 93 village panchayats and the amalgamation of one village panchayat. Following these changes, delimitation and reservation exercises have to be undertaken in 23 districts. Elections to rural local bodies cannot be conducted without completing these processes, the letter said.

Against this backdrop, the State government has extended the tenure of special officers in 28 districts and appointed special officers in nine districts to administer village panchayats, panchayat union councils and district panchayats, excluding the nine newly formed panchayat unions and 93 newly formed village panchayats, till April 19, 2027.

World.title: Tamil Nadu rains LIVE: Schools declare holiday in Chennai, four other districts
World.content:
Schools in five districts of Tamil Nadu, including Chennai, will remain closed on Wednesday (October 21, 2026), owing to heavy rain, according to district authorities. The Collectors of Chennai, Tiruvallur, Kancheepuram, and Chengalpattu districts have declared a holiday for schools, while a similar order has been issued in Ranipet district due to rain.

Several places in and around Chennai received heavy rainfall till 6 a.m. on Wednesday (October 21), according to Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC) data. The weather stations in Meenambakkam and Nungambakkam recorded 12 cm and 11 cm of rainfall respectively, followed by Taramani (10 cm) Madhavaram (9 cm), Villivakkam and Nandanam (8 cm).

Also read: Fresh weather system likely to sustain heavy rainfall in Tamil Nadu till October 26

Minister for Rural Development and Water Resources N. Anand inspected areas affected by waterlogging due to heavy rains in his T. Nagar Assembly constituency. He also instructed officials to swiftly drain the stagnant water using motor pumps. He said the ongoing Metro Rail works had led to water stagnation in several parts of T. Nagar.

World.title: French PM to meet unions as government prepares for more protests
World.content:
France's Prime Minister plans to meet unions on Wednesday (October 21, 2026) to discuss security and has vowed a "massive" police deployment at protests, following riots in the past week that led to curfews and arrests.

The Eurozone's second-largest economy was rocked on the weekend by some of its worst rioting in recent years, just six months before voters head to the polls to elect a successor to President Emmanuel Macron.

Sebastien Lecornu will meet with representatives from five unions on Wednesday (October 21, 2026) morning to discuss "ways and means to guarantee the essential freedom to demonstrate" according to a letter sent to the organisations, which noted some were attempting to subvert the protests with "unacceptable acts”.

More protests centred over rising living costs are planned on Saturday (October 24, 2026), organised by the "Yellow Vest" movement and high school students, with another called for November 5 by labour unions.

School students have not been invited to the Wednesday (October 21, 2026) meeting.

Images of clashes, mobs looting stores and public buildings set ablaze last weekend prompted several countries, including the United States, China and Germany, to issue travel advisories for their citizens in France.

Facing angry lawmakers in parliament, Mr. Lecornu acknowledged that the security response had fallen short and promised a stronger approach ahead of the new wave of protests.

"The deployment for next Saturday (October 24, 2026) will be massive," Mr. Lecornu said.

Arrests and investigations

French authorities announced on Monday (October 19, 2026) partial curfews in Paris and other cities, and Mr. Lecornu said fresh ones would be imposed on Tuesday (October 20, 2026) where needed.

The nighttime curfew in the capital, from 2100 GMT Tuesday (October 20, 2026), applied to Republique square in the centre-east and Les Halles shopping district in the centre.

A ban on public gatherings was also ordered for the Champs-Elysees, near several public buildings, and at train stations.

Paris police ordered a temporary ban on people carrying cans or bottles of petrol or gas, after mobs set fire to government buildings and shops last weekend.

Security forces arrested a man believed to be connected to the ultra-left over the burning down of a historic town hall in Limoges, whose destruction has become a symbol of the violence.

Authorities have faced criticism from parties across the political spectrum, with far-right presidential candidate Marine Le Pen describing the unrest as a "wake-up call" that exposed a "profound crisis" of authority.

Recent polling suggests Ms. Le Pen leading first-round presidential voting intentions by a wide margin and far-left candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon emerging as the strongest contender for the runoff.

Mr. Lecornu has accused ultra-left radical groups of forging an "insurrectionary plan" that led to the riots.

In a sign of growing political scrutiny over the street violence, lawmakers from across France's fractured parliament agreed on Tuesday (October 20, 2026) to launch a parliamentary inquiry into the unrest, including possible intelligence failures, policing tactics and the government's preparedness.

Investors have sold off French debt in recent weeks amid rising doubts about the government's ability to rein in spending.

Nearly 150 people had been jailed and more than 800 brought before the courts, according to the Justice Minister.

Interior Minister Laurent Nunez offered to resign on Sunday (October 18, 2026), saying police "had lost control" during the unrest. Mr. Macron rejected his resignation and Mr. Nunez was also set to attend Wednesday's (October 21, 2026) meeting with union representatives.

Other European countries have seen demonstrations over rising prices, with smaller clashes breaking out in Italy's financial centre of Milan as well as in Belgium over the weekend.

U.S. President Donald Trump has seized on the unrest in France to amplify his anti-immigration and anti-Islam rhetoric, at a time when his Republican party is facing headwinds in upcoming midterm elections.

Mr. Trump launched into a lengthy tirade at a midterms rally on Monday (October 19, 2026) in Kansas, saying France was being "conquered, looted, and burned to the ground by migrants, jihadists, and communists”.

Several analysts have countered Mr. Trump's rhetoric, saying immigration was not a driving force in France's unrest.

World.title: Speed up utilisation of SC and ST Sub-Plan Funds: Bhatti
World.content:
Telangana Deputy Chief Minister and Finance Minister Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka has directed officials to expedite the utilisation of funds allocated under the Scheduled Castes (SC) and Scheduled Tribes (ST) Sub-Plans, stressing that welfare allocations meant for the social and economic advancement of marginalised communities should be spent without delay.

Chairing a review meeting with senior Finance Department officials at the Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Telangana State Secretariat, Mr. Bhatti reviewed department-wise allocations, expenditure and progress under the SC and ST Progress Sub-Plan. He emphasised that all departments must ensure that funds are utilised strictly for their intended purpose and in line with budgetary allocations.

Expressing concern over delays in expenditure by some departments, the Deputy Chief Minister directed officials to identify gaps in utilisation and take immediate corrective measures. He instructed the Finance Department to conduct special reviews with departments lagging behind and convene meetings with secretaries of priority departments to accelerate spending. Departments to be reviewed include Agriculture, Medical and Health, Energy, Municipal Administration, Panchayat Raj, Social Welfare, Industries and Tribal Welfare.

Mr. Bhatti said funds earmarked for the welfare, social advancement and economic empowerment of SCs and STs should be fully utilised in accordance with statutory provisions. He called for comprehensive reports detailing department-wise allocations, expenditure incurred and measures required to ensure effective utilisation of the remaining funds during the current financial year.

The Deputy Chief Minister also focused on broader financial management issues, directing officials to prepare a comprehensive action plan on financial reforms, resource mobilisation and debt restructuring. He stressed the need to strengthen the State’s finances through efficient use of resources, enhanced revenue generation and prudent expenditure management.

Highlighting the importance of long-term fiscal stability, Mr. Bhatti urged officials to formulate policies that support sustainable economic growth. He also suggested engaging experienced consultants and financial experts to adopt best practices in financial management and ensure better coordination between budget allocations, expenditure and development programmes.

Finance and Planning Secretary Gaurav Uppal, Finance Special Secretary Sikta Patnaik and other senior officials attended the review meeting.

World.title: Delhi High Court imposes ₹1 cost on Niva Bupa over ₹5 crore suit against influencer
World.content:
The Delhi High Court has imposed a token cost of ₹1 on Niva Bupa Health Insurance Company Limited for invoking its Intellectual Property Division to pursue a ₹5 crore suit against social media influencer Vishal Rattewal over allegedly disparaging posts, holding that the dispute did not involve trademark infringement.

Justice Anup J. Bhambhani, in an order passed on September 21, observed that merely using an insurance company’s name or trademark to identify it in social media posts did not, in the circumstances of the case, amount to trademark infringement.

Niva Bupa had approached the court seeking the removal of allegedly disparaging posts published in late August this year by Mr. Rattewal on Instagram, Facebook, YouTube and X.

It submitted that Mr. Rattewal, a social media influencer and content creator with a substantial following, had deliberately used its distinctive name, trademarks, logo and other brand identifiers, including ‘NIVA BUPA’, prominently in the titles, thumbnails, captions, visual presentation and content of his publications. The company alleged that he had simultaneously associated the brand with allegations of “fraud, dishonesty, deception, and unfair trade practices”.

It sought an apology, ₹5 crore in damages and litigation costs, alleging that the content had harmed its reputation and infringed its registered trademark.

The dispute stemmed from a consumer complaint filed by Mr. Neeraj Kumar against the insurer before the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission in Charkhi Dadri, Haryana. In an order passed on October 9, 2024, the commission ruled in Mr. Kumar’s favour and made certain observations concerning medical insurance companies.

Niva Bupa alleged that Mr. Rattewal subsequently published offensive and disparaging content about the company in connection with the consumer proceedings.

In this backdrop, Niva Bupa contended that, by publishing allegedly offensive content on his social media accounts, Mr. Rattewal has infringed its registered trade mark by harming its reputation in India.

The court, however, held that Mr. Rattewal was neither engaged in the insurance business nor connected with it. Using Niva Bupa’s name or trademark to identify the company in the alleged posts did not amount to use “in the course of trade” or constitute infringement under the Trade Marks Act, it said.

“In the opinion of this court, this suit is not maintainable before the Intellectual Property Division of this court, since it is not a matter relating to infringement of any intellectual property right of either of the plaintiffs,” the court held.

After the court dictated its order returning the plaint, Niva Bupa sought permission to withdraw the suit and pursue its claims through an ordinary civil action. The court allowed the request, granting them liberty to file a fresh suit on the same cause of action, subject to payment of ₹1 as costs to Mr. Rattewal.

World.title: T.N. Health Minister directs officials to ensure hospital preparedness, uninterrupted health services during monsoon
World.content:
With the Northeast monsoon setting in, Health Minister K.G. Arunraj has directed health officials to ensure uninterrupted medical services and to strengthen hospital preparedness for all government hospitals in the State.

In an official communication, the Minister said that all districts were instructed to take up precautionary measures to achieve three objectives of preventing the spread of diseases during the monsoon, preventing deaths and ensuring uninterrupted medical services.

He said that priority should be given to vulnerable areas in Chennai, Tiruvallur, Kancheepuram, Chengalpattu, Villupuram, Cuddalore, Nagapattinam, Mayiladuthurai, Thanjavur, Tiruvarur, Pudukottai, Ramananthapuram, Thoothukudi, Tirunelveli and Kanniyakumari, and ensure that all government hospitals, primary health centres, urban primary health centres, health sub-centres and vaccine cold chain centres in these areas remain prepared.

He said that a proper advance evacuation plan for healthcare facilities located in low-lying, riverbank and coastal areas should be developed, along with plans to shift patients to safer hospitals. Officials were told to ensure that blood banks, vaccination facilities, drug warehouses and critical electrical infrastructure are located at elevated sites that are not vulnerable to flooding.

Medical camps should be conducted in areas affected by floods and cyclones in coordination with district administration and local bodies, he said.

Dr. Arunraj said that an adequate number of medical teams, mobile medical units and ambulances should be stationed at the flood relief centres in advance.

Also read: How southwest monsoon deficit affected parts of India

The Health Department should work in coordination with the Tamil Nadu Electricity Board and Public Works Department to ensure that transformers are located at elevated sites protected from flooding and remain operational with adequate fuel availability.

He also wanted officials to ensure uninterrupted oxygen supply in government and private hospitals and maintain emergency stocks sufficient for at least seven days. Life saving equipment, including ventilators and adequate number of ambu bags should be available, while all ambulances should be ready for deployment with sufficient fuel, medicines and trained personnel.

Hospitals should maintain stocks of essential medicines, intravenous fluids, disinfectants, oral rehydration solution for diarrhoea, anti-snake venom, chlorine tablets and other medical consumables sufficient for at least seven days.

The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation must ensure the timely supply of essential medicines to drug warehouses in coastal and flood-prone districts. He also wanted essential personnel, including electricians, plumbers, lift operators and sanitation workers to be engaged round-the-clock and to ensure that lifts and fire fighting equipment are properly maintained and kept ready for use during emergencies.

To prevent waterlogging on hospital campuses, drains, sewage pipelines, manual openings and toilets should be properly cleaned and blockages removed. Pumps should be kept ready to drain water from low-lying areas.

He said that post-rain, disease surveillance should be strengthened to ensure earlier identification of dengue, leptospirosis, chikungunya, acute diarrhoeal diseases and other water-borne diseases to ensure prompt treatment.

Pregnant women nearing their delivery dates should avoid staying in flood-prone areas and seek the necessary medical advice, the Minister added.

World.title: Makkah alliance binds partners to decade-long pact
World.content:
• Turkiye seeks parliamentary nod for defence agreement; officials say Ankara’s support may be limited to provision of weapons, equipment and intelligence sharing

• Pakistan has already ratified treaty; only PM and cabinet’s nod required under Article 90

• Egypt’s parliament to vote on support for Riyadh on Oct 26

• Pakistan, Turkiye, Qatar and Indonesia expected to sign defence cooperation agreement in Doha today

ANKARA: Turkiye has submitted the Makkah defence pact to parliament for ratification, moving Nato’s second-largest army closer to a formal mutual defence pledge with Riyadh as it continues to face Houthi attacks.

Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye signed the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement in August, under which an armed attack on one member is considered an attack on all.

The provision, similar to Nato’s Article 5, refers to Article 51 of the UN Charter, which covers the individual or collective right of states to self-defence against armed attacks.

All three members have agreed to use “all necessary means” to eliminate threats to one another’s territorial integrity, sovereignty or internationally recognised borders, as per the text seen by Reuters.

The agreement will enter into force upon the deposit of the ratification documents with the secretariat in Riyadh, and will remain valid indefinitely. The parties may not withdraw from the agreement for the first 10 years.

While Pakistan has made it clear that ‘collective deterrence measures’ under the trilateral defence agreement are “already in play”, Ankara still requires formal parliamentary ratification for the agreement. According to official sources, Pakistan follows an executive-led treaty-making system, where the federal government’s ratification is enough for subjects in the federal legislative list.

According to Article 90 of the Constitution, “the executive authority of the Federation shall be exercised in the name of the President by the Federal Government, consisting of the Prime Minister and the Federal Ministers, which shall act through the Prime Minister, who shall be the chief executive of the Federation.”

However, under Tur­kiye’s constitution, separate permission from parliament is required to deploy troops abroad, regardless of any international agreement.

According to the Reuters news agency, Parliament Speaker Numan Kurtu­lmus, currently visiting Kyrgyzstan, is expected to refer the agreement to parliament’s foreign affairs commission upon his ret­urn, which could debate the agreement as early as Friday.

President Recep Tayyip Erdogan’s communications director, Burha­nettin Dur­an, said that Turk­iye’s re­cent step marked an important mile­stone towards the institutionalisation of strategic cooperation between the three nations.

“This strategic partnership developed between our countries aims to stre­ngthen collective deterrence, enhance joint capabilities in the defence sector, and safeguard security and stability in our region,” Duran said in a post on X.

A Turkish official, who spoke to Reuters on the condition of anonymity, said Turkiye’s own contribution was expected to be limited to military equipment, intelligence sharing and weapons systems, adding that no other form of deployment had taken place under the alliance so far.

Asked how Turkiye could help Saudi Arabia defend against attacks by Yemen’s Houthis, Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said that the Makkah Agree­ment was not an “offensive agreement,” adding that Turkiye would not send troops to another country to carry out attacks on its territory.

Although not part of the Makkah alliance, Egypt’s parliament is also expe­cted to vote on authorising pote­ntial military support for Saudi Arabia on Oct 26.

Ahead of its submission for parliamentary appr­oval, the contents of the agreement were published in full for the first time by Turkish state broadcaster, TRT Haber.

Turkiye, which has a rob­ust defence industry, has condemned Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, expressed willingness to help meet Riyadh’s military technology needs and agreed to join a Saudi-led coalition to ensure navigational safety in the Red Sea.

The agreement also envisages close cooperation on defence industry, intelligence sharing, logistical support and the fight against “all means of terrorism,” including at the operational level.

Defence deal

Meanwhile, TRT World also reported that Turkiye, Qatar, Pakistan and Indonesia are expected to sign a defence industry cooperation memorandum today (Wednesday).

The signing will be held in Qatar, which is also expected to announce plans to establish a local defence production hub, the Gulf state’s Minister of State for Defence Affairs Sheikh Saoud bin Abdulrahman Al Thani told the Global Security Forum in Doha on Monday.

Turkish Defence Mini­ster Yasar Guler will travel to Doha for the signing. Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, who was also in Doha for the security for­um, is expected to represent Pakistan at the signing.

Earlier, Mr Naqvi met with his Qatari counterpart Sheikh Khalifa bin Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani, who also commands Qatar’s Internal Security Force (Lekhwiya). The two discussed the current regional situation and matters concerning regional peace and stability, the state-run APP news agency reported.

During their meeting, the two men agreed to expand the security partnership between Pakistan and Qatar. They also held detailed discussions on expanding cooperation in areas related to internal security.

Published in Dawn, October 21st, 2026

World.title: CDF Munir-Pezeshkian meeting raises peace hopes
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Iranian leaders have told Pakistan that the United States must take the first steps to rebuild trust, and that the acceptance of Tehran’s seven-point proposal could provide a starting point for renewed negotiations.

The message was conveyed during Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir’s visit on Tuesday, where he met with President Masoud Pezeshkian, Parliament Speaker Bagher Ghalibaf, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and Mohsen Rezaei, a representative of Iran’s supreme leader and secretary of the Supreme National Security Council.

Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi also accompanied the army chief.

As diplomatic efforts intensified to prevent a resumption of hostilities, Field Marshal Munir’s visit is being viewed as a move to quell escalating regional tensions.

Tehran says acceptance of its 7-point proposal can be starting point for renewed talks with US

The visit came a day after Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov held talks with Iranian leaders on the conflict and efforts to restore regional stability.

The visit was aimed at conveying messages and exploring whether the Islamabad understanding could still provide a basis for negotiations, but no breakthrough or formal agreement was announced after Tuesday’s meetings.

The discussions also touched on bilateral relations, including a recent disruption in commercial trade across the Pakistan-Iran border. Iranian officials also raised concerns over the closure, while Field Marshal Munir told them that the border closure was temporary and due to technical reasons and that the crossings had reopened on Tuesday.

Importantly, Iranian officials reportedly shared with the field marshal their response to a US proposal, reiterating that Tehran would not make concessions under pressure and that Washington must meet its conditions before trust could be restored.

While there was no official word from Pakistan’s Foreign Office or Inter-Services Public Relations, Iranian media described the response as “clear, serious, and explicit”.

An Iranian source said the visiting Pakistani army chief was told that “Iran has nothing new to say to the Americans” and it was for them to return to Islamabad Memorandum.

Although not many details about President Pezeshkian’s meeting were released to media, in a post that was unrelated to his meeting with Field Marshal Munir, the president said that Iranians may endure hardship, but they will not surrender their land.

Speaker Ghalibaf told Field Marshal Munir that the US could not regain Iran’s trust without fulfilling the seven conditions Tehran had presented during meetings in New York. He said Washington’s past actions, including what Iran considers a violation of the Islamabad understanding, had only deepened its distrust of the US administration.

“Threats and military manoeuvres cannot influence the strategic decisions of the Islamic Republic of Iran,” Mr Ghalibaf said, according to an Iranian account of the meeting, adding that it was now up to Washington to take the necessary steps to extricate itself from the conflict.

Mr Rezaei, meanwhile, said Iran would not surrender its enriched nuclear material, describing it as a national asset intended for domestic use. He said Iranian officials were united in their view that negotiations could not proceed without steps by Washington to meet Tehran’s conditions.

The inflexible Iranian response has thrown a challenge for Pakistan, which has sought to revive negotiations between Washington and Tehran after an earlier diplomatic breakthrough failed to produce a lasting settlement.

Islamabad brokered a ceasefire in April and hosted direct talks that led to the signing of the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding in June. The agreement outlined steps towards easing the conflict, reopening the Strait of Hormuz and addressing economic and nuclear issues, but the process subsequently stalled after disagreements.

Despite the breakdown of the peace process, Pakistan has continued to offer its good offices to both sides for preventing another round of fighting.

Published in Dawn, October 21st, 2026

World.title: Man accused of running over Multan teenager killed in alleged CCD encounter
World.content:
The suspect accused of running over and killing a 14-year-old boy in Multan was killed in an alleged encounter with the Crime Control Department (CCD) in Bahawalpur early on Wednesday, police said.

The suspect, identified as Tauqeer, had allegedly escaped from police custody while on remand, a CCD spokesperson said.

A Multan court on Tuesday granted police three-day physical remand of the suspect. The suspect was accused of hitting the victim, who used to work for him, with his car in a private housing society. The suspect was arrested on Monday and presented before Judicial Magistrate Saadia Aslam on Tuesday.

According to the spokesperson, the CCD personnel attempted to stop two individuals riding a motorcycle on Bahawalpur’s Northern Bypass when an exchange of fire ensued, leaving the suspect dead.

On Tuesday, police requested a 14-day physical remand of the suspect for investigation. However, the judicial magistrate granted the police a three-day remand.

At the time, Multan City Police Officer (CPO) Akhtar Farooq said while speaking to the media that raids were being conducted for the arrest of a second suspect.

“We all are in deep pain,” the CPO said, adding that the orphan boy had been “subjected to barbarity”.

The CCTV footage of the incident shows a boy running on the road after spotting a car. The car is seen swerving and chasing the boy, eventually hitting him. The boy, who fell, then rams into the gate of a nearby house and dies on impact.

A case was registered on the state’s behalf at Multan’s DHA police station.

The first information report (FIR) named two suspects and invoked Sections 302 (intentional murder) and 34 (acts done by several persons in furtherance of common intention) of the Pakistan Penal Code.

According to the FIR, the teenage boy had been working for the suspects and was being trained as an electrician. His cousin told police that the boy had reportedly faced violence and threats by the suspects, the FIR said, adding that the 14-year-old was fleeing when the suspects pursued him in a car and hit him.

Police arrested one of the suspects while the other escaped, the FIR stated. It added that their vehicle had been taken into custody.

World.title: Pakistan warns India against attempt to alter strategic balance
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Adviser to the National Command Authority retired Lt Gen Khalid Kidwai on Tuesday warned that Pakistan could review its deployment options to restore strategic balance in South Asia, saying India was moving towards a more prepared, potentially first-use capable nuclear posture.

“Pakistan never has and never will accept strategic imbalances to be induced in South Asia,” Mr Kidwai said at the second Islamabad Non-Proliferation Conference, hosted by the Strategic Vision Institute, an Islamabad based think tank specialising in strategic issues.

“Pakistan will review and reconsider all options for appropriate deployments in order to restore the strategic balance and strategic stability while retaining the policy of strategic ambiguity,” he added.

Mr Kidwai and retired Lt Gen Sarfraz Sattar, both former heads of the Strategic Plans Division and advisers to the NCA, said India’s reported deployment of nuclear weapons aboard a submarine, alongside missile modernisation and recent military confrontations, raised the risk of escalation between the two neighbouring arch rivals.

NCA adviser reminds India of Pakistan’s Full Spectrum Deterrence policy

Nuclear warheads

Citing the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute’s SIPRI Yearbook 2026 and other publicly available information, they pointed to reports that India had deployed around 12 nuclear warheads on a submarine for deterrence patrols. They also cited missile canisterisation and wider nuclear and conventional modernisation as developments that cast doubt on India’s declared No-First-Use policy.

Mr Kidwai said the reported deployment suggested India had mated nuclear warheads with submarine launched ballistic missiles and begun sea based deterrence patrols.

“I do not see any reason as to why an SIPRI report might be inaccurate or speculative,” he said.

“This irresponsible escalatory transition towards creating asymmetry in nuclear posture will have profound destabilising effects on South Asian strategic stability,” he added.

Mr Kidwai said India’s ability to maintain a continuous at sea deterrent further undermined the credibility of its No-First-Use policy and pointed to a more offensive nuclear posture.

“The operational reality that emerges is that India can undertake a first strike against Pakistan at zero notice,” he said.

Advance notification

He also questioned the absence of advance notification for Indian submarine launched ballistic missile tests, warning that such developments could heighten the risk of miscalculation during a crisis.

Referring to the February 2019 confrontation, he said India had reportedly deployed its Arihant nuclear submarine in the Indian Ocean after carrying out air strikes near Balakot in Pakistan, presumably with nuclear weapons aboard. He described the latest reported deployment as part of India’s wider effort to operationalise mated nuclear weapons on submarines.

“Pakistan reserves the right to undertake all appropriate measures to safeguard its national security and preserve strategic balance in the region under all circumstances,” Mr Kidwai said.

He urged India to understand the implications of Pakistan’s Full Spectrum Deterrence policy.

“India in fact will be well advised to read and re-read Pakistan’s policy of Full Spectrum Deterrence and seriously absorb its wide ranging implications for strategic deterrence, strategic stability, and for India’s security,” he said.

Mr Sattar said the May 2025 conflict between the nuclear-armed neighbours showed how quickly conventional hostilities could escalate. The ceasefire came after both sides used cruise and ballistic missiles and India deployed strategic naval assets, he said.

He drew parallels with the 2019 confrontation, when Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi referred to the deployment of nuclear submarines for deterrence patrols and the positioning of BrahMos missiles along Pakistan’s border.

The May 2025 fighting was more intense, involving kamikaze drones, supersonic BrahMos missiles capable of carrying conventional or nuclear warheads, and cyber and electronic warfare, he said.

“It is now clear that the 2025 conflict was much more lethal in comparison to the 2019 conflict,” Mr Sattar said, warning that the fighting risked spiralling towards nuclear escalation through accident or miscalculation.

He cited India’s canisterisation of land and sea based missiles, pursuit of multiple independently targetable reentry vehicle (MIRV) capabilities, short-range tactical missiles, ballistic missile defences, hypersonic weapons and autonomous platforms as further sources of concern.

Combined with India’s Cold Start doctrine, wider military modernisation and the absence of a bilateral arms control mechanism, these developments raised doubts about its No-First-Use declaration and traditionally recessed deterrence posture, he said.

“Rather, as I said, it signals a shift towards more first use capable posture,” Mr Sattar said.

“The future strategic stability in South Asia is placed on a perilous and worrisome course with heightened risk of misunderstanding and miscalculation, potentially leading to unintended or accidental escalation to the nuclear level,” he added.

World.title: State of deceased’s eyes not proof of ‘unwitnessed’ death: SC
World.content:
• Court dismisses petitions challenging double-murder convictions

• Verdict explains that closing eyes of a corpse is ‘religious’ custom, not legal duty

ISLAMABAD: The Supreme Court ruled on Tuesday that the condition of a deceased person’s eyes at the time of death cannot conclusively establish the fact that the incident was not witnessed.

The Qanun-i-Shahadat Order, 1984, does not impose a legal duty to close a deceased person’s eyes. Rather, the practice is customary and religious, observed Justice Salahuddin Panhwar while dismissing jail petitions filed by Azmat Ullah alias Motu and Muhammad Luqman alias Gona.

The petitioners had challenged their convictions in a 2011 double-murder case, upheld by the Lahore High Court (LHC) on May 18, 2022.

Justice Panhwar was part of a three-member bench, headed by Justice Muhammad Hashim Khan Kakar. The bench upheld the convictions under Section 302(b) of the Pakistan Penal Code but maintained the high court’s decision to commute the death sentences to life imprisonment.

In criminal trials, defence lawyers often argue that an incident was ‘unwitnessed’ if the post-mortem report records the deceased’s eyes as open, reasoning that close relatives would ordinarily close them after death.

During the hearing, the petitioners’ counsel pointed to discrepancies in eyewitness statements and argued that the post-mortem and inquest reports, which recorded the eyes of both victims as open, indicated that the murders had not been witnessed.

Article 129 versus rigid presumptions

In a nine-page judgement, Justice Panhwar referred to Article 129 of the Qanun-i-Shahadat Order, which allows courts to presume facts they consider likely in the circumstances of a particular case.

However, the judgement stressed that human behaviour could not be assessed in a vacuum or through rigid assumptions. Responses to trauma, terror and violent loss vary from person to person, making it unsafe to draw categorical conclusions from a single circumstance.

It noted that relatives witnessing a gruesome incident may be overwhelmed by shock and trauma.

Hoping their loved one might survive, they may focus on obtaining urgent medical assistance rather than performing customary rituals associated with death.

Relatives and bystanders may also continue treating the victim as injured until a doctor or police official confirms death, which may not be immediately apparent at the scene.

Other factors

From a forensic perspective, the position of the eyelids is governed by physiological processes rather than the presence or absence of witnesses, the judgement explained.

Following death, muscles initially become relaxed, allowing eyelids to remain open or partially open, a condition known as lagophthalmos.

Handling or moving a body may also cause previously closed eyes to reopen, particularly before rigor mortis develops. As rigor mortis sets in, muscles become stiff and retain their prevailing position.

The court also cited Locard’s Exchange Principle, which holds that every contact leaves a trace. Relatives, bystanders and rescue workers may avoid touching a body to prevent contamination or disturbance of blood-spatter patterns, trace evidence and DNA material before forensic experts arrive.

It would therefore be unsafe to presume that every person knows how to handle a deceased body or feels obliged to close the eyes, the judgement said.

Concluding that neither forensic literature nor the law recognises closed eyes as an indicator of a witnessed death, the court rejected the argument that open eyelids alone could establish that a crime was unwitnessed.

The judgement further observed that minor discrepancies and natural variations in eyewitness accounts, arising from the passage of time and the rigours of cross-examination, do not undermine otherwise credible and consistent testimony.

World.title: Judicial Commission of Pakistan’s transfer-only policy for IHC judges challenged
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: A writ petition filed in the Islamabad High Court has challenged the Judicial Commission of Pakistan’s (JCP) April 28 decision that vacancies arising from the transfer of a judge “shall be filled through transfer only”, arguing that the three vacant judges’ seats in the IHC should be filled through fresh appointments under the Constitution rather than further transfers.

The petition, filed by Advocate Supreme Court Syed Nayyab Hassan Gardezi against the Federation of Pakistan, JCP, president and prime minister, contends that the impugned decision has no constitutional foundation and conflicts with Article 175A(8), which requires the commission to nominate one person “for each vacancy” of a high court judge. It argues that the Constitution recognises no category of high court vacancy exempt from this requirement and that the commission cannot create one through a resolution.

The petition contends that the JCP decision was taken in disregard of the procedure prescribed by the Judicial Commission of Pakistan (Appointment of Judges) Rules 2024. It points out that Rule 11(2) requires the secretary to notify all members at least 14 days before a scheduled meeting, providing the agenda and supporting materials. According to the petition, the impugned decision was reportedly introduced during the proceedings rather than being included in the circulated agenda.

It further states that the JCP Rules, as notified, contain no provision for their amendment, while the only provision allowing the commission to remove difficulties — Rule 15 — requires the votes of at least two-thirds of its total membership. The impugned decision, however, records only a “majority of its total membership”.

The petition also questions the composition of the JCP when the decision was taken. It argues that the impugned decision governs future appointments to the IHC, yet it was taken at meetings convened to consider transfers, at which the commission sat under the first proviso to Article 200(1), with the chief justices of the high courts concerned in each transfer.

By contrast, the Constitution prescribes a distinct composition for the appointment of IHC judges under Article 175A(6). Besides the IHC chief justice, it includes the head of IHC’s constitutional benches, an advocate nominated by the Islamabad Bar Council and a federal minister nominated by the prime minister.

The petitioner submits that procedural and compositional defects reinforce the need for the IHC’s three vacancies, created by the transfers notified on April 29, 2026, to be filled through the constitutional process of fresh appointments. For this purpose, nominations should be invited from members of the commission under Article 175A(23) and Rule 9(1) of the JCP Rules, rather than through a transfer-only route.

The petition also challenges the decision on grounds of discrimination, retrospectivity and an unlawful fetter on discretion. It notes that in July 2026, the JCP filled vacancies in the Lahore High Court, Sindh High Court and Baloc­histan High Court through initial appointments, while the IHC’s vacancies have been reserved for transfers.

It emphasises that the IHC is currently functioning with a chief justice and nine judges against a sanctioned strength of a chief justice and 12 judges, and that the three vacancies have remained unfilled for more than five months.

Along with the writ petition, the petitioner has filed an application for interim relief, seeking to restrain the respondents from recommending, advising or notifying the transfer of any judge to the IHC against the three vacancies while the petition remains pending.

The petition seeks a declaration that the JCP’s decision is ultra vires Articles 4, 25, 175A and 193 of the Constitution and the JCP Rules, and is of no legal effect.

World.title: Hegseth discusses Iran with Netanyahu in unannounced visit
World.content:
JERUSALEM: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth arrived in Israel on an unannounced visit, and discussed the Iran war with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, as tensions continue to simmer between the US and Iran.

Doron Spielman, a spokesperson for the Israeli PM, confirmed that Netanyahu had met Hegseth at the Uvda air force base in Israel’s southern Negev desert region.

Mr Netanyahu and Mr Hegseth discussed “the threats in the region” and the US-Israel partnership in dealing both “offensively and defensively” with those threats, he said in a brief phone call.

The defence secretary thanked Israel for hosting US forces, which Spielman said numbered in the thousands, and discussed President Donald Trump’s support for the prime minister.

Israeli PM celebrates Trump’s endorsement ahead of next week’s election

“There’s a deep personal relationship here that was at the core of this discussion,” Spielman said.

The Pentagon has not publicly commented on Mr Hegseth’s visit.

Earlier, he posted that he had visited US service members in the Central Command area of responsibility, which covers the Middle East, northeast Africa and parts of Asia, but did not specify where he had met the personnel.

Hegseth’s visit comes as tensions flare between the US and Iran over the Strait of Hormuz, and Yemen’s Houthis intensify their attacks on Saudi Arabia.

The Israeli prime minister also said he spoke with President Trump on Sunday about the importance of eliminating the Iranian government.

“We are committed to completing the elimination of the Iranian regime,” Mr Netanyahu said in a statement released by his office. “I have discussed this with Trump many times, including the day before yesterday.”

Netanyahu basks in Trump endorsement

Netanyahu basked in Trump’s endorsement on Monday ahead of close-fought elections, airing a phone call in which the US president predicted he would win, and suggested they may again attack Iran together.

“I think you’re going to have a tremendous victory, actually,” the US president can be heard saying on speakerphone.

“You’re the man I want by my side, Bibi,” Donald Trump said, referring to Mr Netanyahu by his nickname.

Netanyahu, while reminding the famously loose-lipped president that they were on an open line, hailed Trump for joining Israel in attacking Iran in February.

“Donald, we have a job to finish,” Netanyahu beamed. “We’ll finish it together. We’ll finish it, and no one else will do it.”

Netanyahu did not elaborate, but again described Iran as “the greatest danger”.

Trump, 80, and Netanyahu, who turns 77 on Wednesday, have forged a close partnership at a time when both are vastly unpopular in public opinion in most democratic nations.

The pair have also managed to avoid prosecution while in power, with Mr Netanyahu facing charges of corruption that could land him in prison.

World.title: Balochistan says Rs14bn spent to counter terrorism
World.content:
• Insists 18 laws enacted, 17 institutions set up under security plans

• Officials claim 60,000 operations conducted, 1,100 terrorists killed

QUETTA: The Balochistan government has passed 18 laws, established 17 institutions and departments and spent more than Rs14 billion on counterterrorism measures under the National Action Plan, Counterterrorism Policy and Provincial Action Plan, senior provincial officials said on Tuesday.

They also claimed that more than 60,000 counterterrorism operations had been conducted across Balochistan up to October, killing over 1,000 terrorists.

The Counter-Terrorism Depart­ment alone had killed 250 terrorists and arrested another 250 suspects. They said 101 police personnel and around 200 members of other law enforcement agencies had lost their lives, while 551 civilians had been killed in terrorist violence.

The figures were revealed during a joint press conference held by Provincial Home Minister Ziaullah Langove along with Chief Mini­ster’s Adviser on Media and Political Aff­a­irs Shahid Rind and Additional Chief Secretary Home Hamza Shafqaat.

They said measures had also been taken to secure the Quetta-Rakhni, Quetta-Karachi and Quetta-Taftan highways and expressed confidence that the security situation would improve over the next three to four months.

Mr Shafqaat said the provincial government had taken a series of measures over the past two years to implement the National Action Plan, Counter Terrorism Policy and Provincial Action Plan.
